defects.defect: `.dock-layer-grid` is a class with zero CSS rules anywhere; the container is display:block/position:static, so the producer's `position:absolute; inset:0` on the inactive layer resolves against `.dock-face` and the hidden layer is stretched across the whole dock face.
defects.evidence: Live CSSOM walk of every rule in every stylesheet: gridRuleCount 0; getComputedStyle → display "block", position "static"; grid rect x=584.7 w=184.0. Both children report offsetParent "dock-face". Measured boxes: ActionToolbar active x=584.7 w=184.0 h=40; ColorInput inactive x=519.7 w=400.5 h=46; ColorInput active x=584.7 w=282.5; ActionToolbar leaving/inactive x=519.7 w=400.5. Overhang: 65.0 px left of the grid, 151.5 px right. Static: `grep -rn "dock-layer-grid" . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=docs` → one hit, ActionBarLayer.vue:101 (the site that writes it); `grep -rn "dock-layer-grid" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/` → no output. The producer's real stacking container is `.dock-layers { display:grid; min-width:0 }` in dist/components/dock/styles/layers.css — a different class.
defects.mechanism: A class name copied from the producer's vocabulary that the producer never defined; the stacking contract (display:grid + a positioned container) is therefore absent, and the absolutely-positioned inactive layer escapes to the nearest positioned ancestor.
defects.reproduction: Console at /#/ with the action bar open: `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.dock-layer-grid')).display` → "block"; `[...g.children].find(c=>!c.classList.contains('is-active')).offsetParent.className` → "dock-face".
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by C-2 — DockCrossfade supplies `.dock-crossfade{display:grid;position:relative;isolation:isolate}` and grid-area-stacks its faces. Do NOT patch by adding a local `.dock-layer-grid{display:grid;position:relative}` rule; that deepens the private-CSS coupling of C-4.

defects.defect: The file hand-writes the producer's private layer class vocabulary (`dock-layer`, `is-active`, `is-leaving`) and nests those elements inside a genuine producer `.dock-layer`, so every descendant-scoped producer rule lands on the sub-layers unintentionally.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:91 emits `class: ["dock-layer", { "is-active": …, "is-leaving": … }]`. Measured live: producerLayerAncestor = "dock-layer dock-layer--full is-active"; the full layer list is ["dock-layer dock-layer--full is-active", "flex items-center justify-around flex-1 dock-layer is-active", "grid grid-cols-1 gap-y-2 p-0 m-0 dock-layer min-w-0", "dock-layer dock-layer--summary"] — a .dock-layer inside a .dock-layer. Producer selectors are descendant-scoped: `:where(.glass-dock,.dock-layer-group) .dock-layer{display:flex;align-items:center;grid-area:1/1;gap:…}`, `.glass-dock:not(.vertical) .dock-layer{white-space:nowrap;min-height:var(--dock-layer-height,2.5rem)}`, `.glass-dock[data-morphing] .dock-layer.is-active > *{opacity:var(--child-reveal);scale:calc(0.82+0.18*var(--child-reveal))}` (dist/components/dock/styles/layers.css). Measured effect of min-height: the inactive box is 46 px tall vs the active toolbar's 40 px.
defects.mechanism: Undeclared, name-based coupling to a producer's private CSS — invisible to package.json, to vue-tsc, and to every test. A glass release renaming `.dock-layer` or tightening the selector to `>` breaks this component with no compile error and no failing test.
defects.reproduction: Console: `document.querySelector('.dock-layer-grid').children[0].closest('.dock-layer--full')` → non-null.
defects.proposedCure: C-2 — DockLayer renders its own `.dock-face` host and never asks the consumer to author producer class names.

defects.defect: Propose mode has no exit path: ColorInput's "Signal parent to exit propose mode" is a comment above no signal, and ActionBarLayer — which owns `toolbarMode` — binds no completion listener, so a successful proposal leaves the component stuck in propose mode with the field silently repopulated by a CSS color string.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:236-241 — `await proposeColorName(...); proposedName.value = ""; // Signal parent to exit propose mode; if (inputColorRef.value) { inputColorRef.value.innerText = formattedCurrentColor.value; }`. `grep -c "defineEmits" demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue` → 0. `grep -n "emit(" demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue` → no output. ActionBarLayer.vue:115-121 binds only ref / v-bind / :edit-target / :propose-mode / class — no listener. The field keeps aria-label "Propose a color name" (ColorInput.vue:15) while displaying a serialized color, and the toggle still reads "Close propose" (ActionBarLayer.vue:131).
defects.mechanism: State ownership without a completion channel — the parent opens a modal sub-state and provides no programmatic way back; the child's only 'signal' is a DOM write.
defects.reproduction: Code-certain from the two greps (zero emits in the child, zero listeners in the parent). The exact on-screen residue after a live POST was NOT reproduced (requires a session + network write, outside this read-only seat) — that leg is labelled a hypothesis.
defects.proposedCure: ColorInput emits `proposed`; ActionBarLayer handles it with `toolbarMode = "actions"`. The mode machine already has the legal propose→actions edge at lines 42-44; it simply has no programmatic caller.

defects.defect: `toolbarMode` is never reconciled when `canProposeName` flips false — the component can sit in "propose" for a color that cannot be proposed, and the exposed writable ref lets any caller enter that state while bypassing the entry gate.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:37 gates entry on `actionBar.canProposeName.value`; nothing gates remaining. The file's only `watch` is line 71 (inside the shim, on `activeLayer`) — no watch on canProposeName. `canProposeName` is `!findCustomName(currentXYZString)` (demo/color-session/useColorNameResolution.ts:66-70), so it flips false the instant a proposal succeeds — the exact transition C-5 fails to report — and on any external color change. ActionBarLayer.vue:47-51 returns EllipsisVertical for "propose" regardless, so the icon gives no stale-state signal; ColorInput keeps data-placeholder="propose a name..." (ColorInput.vue:261). ActionBarLayer.vue:96 exposes `toolbarMode` writable.
defects.mechanism: A cached local `ref` mirroring a derived condition, with the gate evaluated once per click instead of continuously — the cache and its own precondition are free to diverge.
defects.reproduction: Non-network leg is code-certain: enter propose, then change the color to one already carrying a custom name → canProposeName false, toolbarMode still "propose". The network leg (stuck after a successful POST) is labelled a hypothesis — not reproduced live.
defects.proposedCure: `watch(() => actionBar.canProposeName.value, ok => { if (!ok && toolbarMode.value === "propose") toolbarMode.value = "actions"; })` — better, derive the mode instead of caching it in a ref that can disagree with its own gate.

defects.defect: The toggle is a disclosure control with no aria-expanded, no aria-controls, no aria-live in scope, and zero focus management; the control it reveals precedes the trigger in DOM order, so forward Tab moves away from it.
defects.evidence: Measured live over the subtree: toggle { tag "BUTTON", role null, ariaExpanded null, ariaControls null, ariaPressed null, w 40, h 40 }; ariaLiveInDock 0; inputPrecedesToggleInDom true; document.activeElement was "BODY.relative" before the swap and at all nine frames after it. `grep -c "focus" demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue` → 0. Asymmetry: entering "propose" DOES focus the field (ColorInput.vue:262, `requestAnimationFrame(() => inputColorRef.value?.focus())`) but entering "input" does not. The repo's own gate concedes the reachability failure — e2e/smoke/flows/color-propose.spec.ts:20-22: "the propose-mode <span role=\"textbox\" contenteditable> … is not reliably reachable via accessible-name selectors during the cross-fade".
defects.mechanism: The shim reimplemented the class/inert half of the retired producer contract and left the focus half behind; nothing catches a focused descendant when `inert` lands (ActionBarLayer.vue:92) and nothing moves focus into the revealed region.
defects.reproduction: Measured: at /#/ with the action bar open, the toggle carries none of aria-expanded/aria-controls/aria-pressed, the dock subtree has zero [aria-live], `ce.compareDocumentPosition(toggle) & Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_FOLLOWING` is truthy, and activeElement stays BODY across the swap. The specific focus-orphan outcome (activeElement falling to body when focus is inside ColorInput at the moment inert lands) was NOT reproduced — labelled a hypothesis.
defects.proposedCure: `:aria-expanded="showInput"` plus an :id/aria-controls pair on the sub-layer hosts, and ONE focus policy for both reveal legs; structurally C-2, which inherits the producer's documented focus-transfer-on-dissolve. The sibling ActionBarToggle.vue in this same directory already models the idiom (aria-label + :aria-pressed + :tabindex).

defects.defect: Vacuous gate: the component has zero unit tests, its sole e2e touch asserts only the toggle's aria-label (which four independent breaking mutations leave green), and the spec's COVERAGE NOTE cites a fallback unit test that does not exist.
defects.evidence: `find test -iname "*dock*" -o -iname "*action*" -o -iname "*layer*"` → no output. `grep -rln "ActionBarLayer" test/ e2e/ demo/` → only e2e/smoke/flows/color-propose.spec.ts. That spec (line 24) claims: "the contenteditable submission has unit coverage in test/parsing/extract.test.ts via the underlying submitProposedName handler". But `find . -name "extract*.test.ts" -not -path "*/node_modules/*"` → no output; `ls test/parsing/` → `timeline` (one directory, no files); `grep -rn "submitProposedName\|proposeColorName" test/ e2e/` → exactly one hit, the sentence claiming coverage. Every surviving assertion reads the aria-label computed at ActionBarLayer.vue:131 from toolbarMode + canProposeName alone; measured toggleLabelAfter = "Propose color name" after one click. Mutations that keep it green: (1) delete 53-95 and make subLayerProps `() => ({})`; (2) SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS = 0 or 10_000_000; (3) invert to `inert: isActive ? true : undefined` (inert the visible layer, leave the hidden one in the tab order); (4) swap the ids so the wrong layer shows in every mode; (5) delete the `provide(COLOR_MODEL_KEY, …)` at line 22.
defects.mechanism: The gate observes a label rather than the state machine or the DOM invariants, and the documented compensating control is a citation to a nonexistent file — a coverage gap wearing a receipt.
defects.reproduction: Run the three commands above; the third returns only the self-referential comment line.
defects.proposedCure: A component test asserting the real invariants — exactly one sub-layer carries `is-active`, the other carries `inert`, the active id tracks `toolbarMode`, and the propose leg returns to `actions` on success — and DELETE the false citation at spec line 24 rather than let it stand as evidence.

defects.defect: No size reserve: the sub-layer swap is an unreserved, uninterpolated layout jump.
defects.evidence: Measured active sub-layer width across the swap at the same origin (x 584.7): before 184.0 px (ActionToolbar), after 282.5 px (ColorInput) — a +98.5 px instantaneous change with no reserved box and, per C-1, nothing to interpolate. The producer's DockCrossfade.vue.d.ts documents the reserved box as a measure-once min-block-size with `reserve: "block" | "inline"`, `inline` documented for exactly this shape (a horizontal control run). The shim's own comment at ActionBarLayer.vue:55 concedes glass's version did "the layer size-morph + crossfade", then reimplements only the crossfade bookkeeping.
defects.mechanism: The retired producer composable owned the size-morph; the reimplementation kept only the id bookkeeping.
defects.reproduction: Click "Open color input"; sample `document.querySelector('.dock-layer-grid').children[i].getBoundingClientRect().width` before and after.
defects.proposedCure: C-2, with `reserve="inline"`.

defects.defect: The crossfade timer is never cleared on unmount, and because `toolbarMode` is a component-local ref inside a v-if-destroyed layer, an unmount silently discards the user's mode and any half-typed color.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:70-79 sets `timer = setTimeout(...)` and clears it only on the next swap. `grep -c "onScopeDispose\|onUnmounted" demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue` → 0. The watch is auto-disposed with the setup scope; the pending setTimeout is not. Observed live: between two consecutive read-only probes ~10 s apart at /#/ with no navigation issued, `document.querySelector('.dock-layer-grid')` went non-null → null, the dock carried class "…collapsed…" and its face list went 4 → 3 with the action-bar face gone (faces: ["dock-face justify-center","dock-face justify-center","dock-face is-active"]; layers: ["dock-layer dock-layer--full","dock-layer dock-layer--summary is-active"]). Dock.vue:153,156 gate the layer behind two v-ifs (hasAnyActionBar, then actionBar).
defects.mechanism: Missing-cleanup the retired producer composable would have owned, plus component-local state living inside a destructible v-if branch.
defects.reproduction: The measured fact (the layer vanished mid-session while the dock auto-collapsed) is reproduced above; the precise mechanism that flipped hasAnyActionBar was NOT isolated and is labelled a hypothesis.
defects.proposedCure: C-2 removes the timer entirely (the producer owns the crossfade lifetime). If C-2 is deferred: `onScopeDispose(() => timer && clearTimeout(timer))`. Independently, lift `toolbarMode` to an owner that survives the layer, or stop v-if-destroying it.

defects.defect: All three template refs in the file are unread, and two competing template-ref idioms coexist in one 158-line file.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "colorInputRef\|actionToolbarRef" demo/` returns exactly four lines: the two declarations (ActionBarLayer.vue:28-29, using the pre-3.5 `ref(null)` idiom) and the two `ref=` bindings (lines 103, 116). No `.value` access anywhere in the repo. Line 83 uses `useTemplateRef` (the Vue 3.5 idiom) for `subLayerGridEl`, which is itself dead — its sole consumer is `void opts.containerEl` (C-12).
defects.mechanism: Accreted ceremony from the retired composable's call shape; owner edict 7 (idiomatic Vue 3.5) violated by carrying two idioms for one job.
defects.reproduction: Run the grep above.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `colorInputRef`; `subLayerGridEl` goes with C-2. Keep `actionToolbarRef` only if the C-15 cure is taken via reach-in, and convert it to `useTemplateRef`.

defects.defect: A `containerEl` parameter is threaded, passed, and immediately discarded for "signature parity" with a composable that exists nowhere.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:63-67 — `function useLayerTransition(opts: { containerEl: Ref<HTMLElement|null>; activeLayer: Ref<string> }) { void opts.containerEl; // signature parity with the retired producer composable`. `grep -rn "useLayerTransition" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` → no output. The useTemplateRef (line 83) → call-site argument (line 86) → `void` chain has no effect, and drags `Ref` and `useTemplateRef` into the line-2 import where neither is otherwise needed.
defects.mechanism: Back-compat shimming against a void (edict 2) plus contrivance (edict 3): there is no caller to be compatible with and no second implementation to swap in.
defects.reproduction: Run the grep above; then observe lines 63-67, 83, 86.
defects.proposedCure: C-2. Interim: delete the parameter, the call-site argument, the `ref="subLayerGridEl"` binding, and the `Ref` / `useTemplateRef` imports.

defects.defect: `defineExpose` publishes three members with zero consumers, one of them a writable `toolbarMode` ref that bypasses the component's own state-machine gate.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:96 — `defineExpose({ currentToggleIcon, toolbarMode, cycleToolbarMode });`. `grep -rn "currentToggleIcon\|cycleToolbarMode\|toolbarMode" demo/ e2e/ test/ | grep -v "layers/ActionBarLayer.vue"` → no output. The sole mount site (Dock.vue:156) passes props and listens to events; it holds no template ref to this component. A caller writing `toolbarMode.value = "propose"` bypasses the canProposeName gate at line 37, and per C-6 nothing downstream reconciles it.
defects.mechanism: A public surface with no consumer that also widens the state machine's write set beyond its only guarded transition function.
defects.reproduction: Run the grep above.
defects.proposedCure: Delete line 96.

defects.defect: `canProposeName` is computed, passed to ActionToolbar, declared there, and never used.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:106 passes `:can-propose-name="actionBar.canProposeName.value"`. `grep -n "canProposeName" demo/shell/dock/ActionToolbar.vue` → `72:    canProposeName: boolean;` — one hit, the declaration; it appears nowhere in ActionToolbar's 63-line template.
defects.mechanism: A dead reactive dependency that re-renders the toolbar for nothing and misstates the toolbar's contract to every reader.
defects.reproduction: Run the grep above.
defects.proposedCure: Drop the binding at ActionBarLayer.vue:106 and the declaration at ActionToolbar.vue:72.

defects.defect: ActionToolbar publishes a `clearHover` reset for exactly the hidden-while-hovered case and ActionBarLayer never calls it, so a stale hover highlight can survive the swap.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ActionToolbar.vue:85-91 — `const activeHover = ref<string|null>(null); function clearHover() { activeHover.value = null; } defineExpose({ clearHover });`. `grep -rn "clearHover" demo/` returns only the definition and the expose (plus an unrelated `clearHoveredPath` in ColorNutritionLabel.vue) — no caller. ActionBarLayer holds `actionToolbarRef` (C-11), the only handle from which clearHover() could be called, and never calls it.
defects.mechanism: Producer of the state published the cure; the consumer that inerts the producer ignored it.
defects.reproduction: NONE — the pointer sequence needed to strand activeHover (keyboard-driven cycling, or a pointer resting on a toolbar button at the moment the layer is inerted) was not reproduced live. Labelled a hypothesis.
defects.proposedCure: Preferred (KISS, no cross-component reach-in): move the reset into ActionToolbar via a `watch` on an `active` prop.

defects.defect: An untokenized 260 ms magic duration that does not match — and is outlived by — the producer's 300 ms visibility delay it actually races, in a file whose other transition is fully tokenized and PRM-guarded.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:62 — `const SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS = 260;`. Tokens in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/scheme-motion.css: --duration-instant .1s, --duration-control .12s, --duration-fast .2s, --duration-normal .3s, --duration-slow .45s, --duration-panel .55s — 260 ms is not among them and no CSS in the repo consumes the constant. Measured disagreement: `is-leaving` cleared at t=286 ms (the 260 ms timer) but the layer's computed `visibility` was still "visible" at t=403 ms and only "hidden" at t=628 ms — the producer's `.dock-layer{transition: visibility 0s linear var(--duration-normal)}` adds 300 ms after the class drops, so the mis-positioned 400.5 px box (C-3) persists ~560 ms, 2.15x the constant. Contrast the icon swap 72 lines below: `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` (line 134), tokenized at demo/styles/animations.css:104-117 and neutralised by the global prefers-reduced-motion guard — the recipe demo/DESIGN.md:275 cites this very file as the reference for.
defects.mechanism: A JS clock coupled to no CSS token cannot agree with, or even drift into agreement with, the CSS clock it shares an element with.
defects.reproduction: Sample `getComputedStyle(child).visibility` and `child.classList.contains('is-leaving')` across the swap: leaving cleared at ~286 ms, visibility hidden only at ~628 ms.
defects.proposedCure: C-2. KISS interim using vocabulary already in this file and already blessed by DESIGN.md: a plain `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` around the sub-layer content — PRM-guarded, tokenized, and it would actually render.

defects.defect: ColorInput sets `pointer-events-auto` on a descendant of the layer that glass hides with `pointer-events: none`, so the hidden 400.5 px-wide, 65 px-overhanging box is one attribute away from being clickable over the sibling `Back` control.
defects.evidence: Producer rule `.dock-layer:not(.is-active):not(.is-leaving){opacity:0;visibility:hidden;pointer-events:none}` — measured on the live inactive layer: pointerEvents "none", inert true. Its immediate child re-enables it: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:3-8 — `<Popover trigger="hover" :close-delay="0" :open-delay="300" class="pointer-events-auto w-full">`. pointer-events is inherited and a descendant setting `auto` becomes hit-testable regardless of the ancestor's `none`; today only the `inert` attribute (ActionBarLayer.vue:92) masks it — and C-8 mutations 1 and 3 both remove `inert` while staying green. Per C-3 that box is 400.5 px wide starting 65.0 px left of the grid, i.e. directly over the Back DockControl (Dock.vue:154).
defects.mechanism: The hiding guarantee is split across two files and two mechanisms (CSS pointer-events + the consumer's inert), and the child defeats one of them; also a per-instance override against edict 5.
defects.reproduction: Measured: inactive layer computed pointerEvents "none" with inert true; the child's `pointer-events-auto` class is code-certain from the template. The clickable-overlay outcome is contingent on inert being absent and is labelled a hypothesis for the current tree.
defects.proposedCure: C-2 (DockCrossfade's `.dock-face` owns the hiding and does not depend on a consumer class staying non-interactive). Independently, remove ColorInput's `pointer-events-auto` or move it to the glass root.

defects.defect: `canProposeName` checks only the custom-name registry, contradicting the e2e spec's own stated contract that it excludes built-in names — so the propose leg is offered for every named CSS color.
defects.evidence: e2e/smoke/flows/color-propose.spec.ts:7-9 states "the canProposeName computed (true when the active color doesn't match a built-in or custom name)". Implementation: demo/color-session/useColorNameResolution.ts:66-70 — `const canProposeName = computed(() => { const colorString = currentXYZString.value; const hasCustom = !!findCustomName(colorString); return !hasCustom; });` and demo/color-session/useCustomColorNames.ts:60-65 — `findCustomName` iterates `normalizedCustomNames.value` (the proposed-names registry) only; no built-in table is consulted. ActionBarLayer.vue:37 acts on it (entry gate) and ActionBarLayer.vue:131 renders the accessible name "Propose color name".
defects.mechanism: Same family as C-2/C-5/C-8: prose asserting behaviour the code does not have, with a consumer built on the prose.
defects.reproduction: Read the three cited sites; no built-in name table is referenced on the path. Not exercised live (would require seeding a built-in color and reading the toggle label) — labelled a hypothesis for the runtime leg.
defects.proposedCure: Either consult the built-in name table in `canProposeName` or correct the spec's stated contract. Charged to useColorNameResolution; filed here because ActionBarLayer is the only place the divergence is user-visible.

defects.defect: A re-provide justified in-comment as back-compat, plus an unnamed DI failure on a non-null-asserted inject.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:21-24 — `// Re-provide COLOR_MODEL_KEY so ColorInput works unchanged` / `provide(COLOR_MODEL_KEY, actionBar.colorModel);` / `const safeAccent = inject(SAFE_ACCENT_KEY)!;`. The provided value is evaluated once at setup; `actionBar` comes from ColorPicker.vue:315 via App.vue:38 (`colorPickerRef?.actionBarContext ?? null`) and a ColorPicker remount destroys this component too (Dock.vue:156 v-if), so it cannot go stale in the current tree — the guarantee is incidental, not stated. The producer this file already imports from models the named-failure alternative: dist/dockContext-*.js throws "[glass-ui:dock] useDockContext() called outside `<GlassDock>`; use useOptionalDockContext() if the primitive may render outside a dock."
defects.mechanism: Compatibility framing (edict 2) over what is really a DI boundary, plus an unnamed crash surface on a non-null assertion.
defects.reproduction: NONE — no path was found that mounts ActionBarLayer outside the provider or swaps the context identity. Labelled a hypothesis.
defects.proposedCure: State the DI boundary honestly in the comment (or pass the model as a prop), and replace `inject(...)!` with a named throw in the producer's idiom.

defects.defect: The visual matrix has zero coverage of this component's rendered state — the action-bar layer is closed in all 60 captures — so none of C-1, C-3, C-6, C-7 or C-9 could ever have appeared in the visual audit.

Separately, both mobile picker rows report allElements 228 / bodyTextLength 70 against desktop's 1738 / 859 — the mobile capture did not render the app.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for `demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue`
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M context). Declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — the local `useLayerTransition` shim hand-binds `.dock-layer` / `.is-active` / `.is-leaving`, which is NOT orphaned CSS (as pass 1 concluded) but glass-ui 7.0.0's LIVE PRIVATE shell-pane contract: `GlassDock` renders exactly two of them (`dock-layer--full`, `dock-layer--summary`) as its expand↔collapse pane pair, while `<DockLayer>` faces moved to `.dock-face`. ActionBarLayer impersonates the dock's own shell panes two nesting levels below where that contract lives, and inherits the shell's behaviour: with `data-morphing` stamped on `.glass-dock`, ColorInput's content computes `opacity: 0`, `scale: 0.82` from `.glass-dock[data-morphing] .dock-layer.is-active > *`. An unversioned, type-invisible coupling to producer internals that carries live behaviour.

defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition, not a patch: `isAdminMode` is `currentView in adminViews` in full — make it a computed over the ONE nav table. `const isAdminMode = computed(() => NAV[currentView.value].group === "admin")`. This deletes useDockAdminMode.ts:31,41-47,52-61 (18 lines -> 1); `toggleAdminMode` keeps working unchanged because it already navigates (`:44,46`) and navigation is what the computed reads. Under the report's `shell/nav/` lattice the defect becomes unrepresentable rather than fixed.

defects.defect: MAJOR (new this pass) — CORRECTION to the pass-1 'Probe note', which dismissed an observed deep-link redirect as sibling-seat contention on a shared browser. It is not contention: deep-link cold loads lose the requested route in an UNCONTENDED session, 3 of 6 observed. The 7 routes this selector does not offer are reachable only by typing a URL (pass-1 L-3), and that sole entrance is ~50% unreliable at boot. Underlying structural fact (not a hypothesis): the view-switch authority has four uncoordinated writer sites and no arbiter.
defects.evidence: Six deep-link loads, single uncontended Playwright session, `location.hash` polled every 200-250 ms: (1) goto #/atmosphere -> #/extract REDIRECTED; (2) goto #/atmosphere -> held; (3) goto #/blob -> #/palettes REDIRECTED; (4) about:blank -> goto #/atmosphere -> held (12 samples x 250 ms); (5) about:blank -> goto #/blob -> #/ REDIRECTED (already gone at the first 200 ms sample); (6) about:blank -> goto #/blob -> held (16 samples x 200 ms). In-app control: hooked `history.pushState`, then `location.hash='#/blob'` -> { pushes: [], finalHash: "#/blob" } — writer is boot-scoped, not navigation-scoped. Writer sites: demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts:44,46,72; demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:55,56; demo/color-picker/composables/usePaletteWiring.ts:78,109,169; demo/color-session/useColorUrl.ts:64.
defects.mechanism: Four uncoordinated writers to one navigation authority, at least one of them firing during boot before the router has resolved. HYPOTHESIS for the specific #/blob -> #/ case (NOT confirmed): demo/color-session/useColorUrl.ts:64 does `router.replace({ query: {...} })` with no `name` and no `path`, from a 300 ms debounce (`:51,64`) that is not gated on `router.isReady()` (useViewManager.ts:36-37 is the only place that awaits it); resolved against START_LOCATION that replaces to `/`. It does NOT explain observations 1 and 3 (-> #/extract, -> #/palettes), whose shapes match Dock.vue:55-56 and usePaletteWiring.ts:78,109. At least one further writer is involved.
defects.reproduction: INTERMITTENT (3 of 6 observed). about:blank, then goto http://localhost:9000/#/blob (or /#/atmosphere), then poll location.hash every 200 ms for ~3 s. Roughly half the loads land on a different route (#/, #/palettes, #/extract observed). In-app hash changes to the same routes never redirect.
defects.proposedCure: Give navigation one owner (`demo/shell/nav/useNavigation.ts` in the report's lattice) so `switchView` has a single arbitrated entry point, and gate every boot-time route write on `router.isReady()`. Then verify the specific mechanism before touching useColorUrl.ts:64 — the hypothesis above is explicitly unconfirmed and must not be cured blind.

defects.defect: MAJOR (new this pass) — the demo contains ZERO link elements. Fifteen routes, no `<a href>`, no `<RouterLink>`; every transition in the product is an imperative `switchView` call, and the primary navigation is a `role=combobox` whose children are `role=option`. vue-router's own navigation primitive is entirely unused.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "RouterLink|router-link" demo --include="*.vue" | wc -l` -> 0. Live: opened listbox reports { expanded: "true", optionCount: 7, options: [Home, Palettes, Browse, Extract, Mix, Generate, Gradient] } against 14 named routes in demo/color-picker/router/index.ts:21-36.
defects.mechanism: The routing library's link primitive was never adopted; navigation was modelled as 'the selected value of a select' rather than 'a set of destinations'. Nothing is middle-clickable, cmd-clickable, open-in-new-tab-able or crawlable; the product has no link graph. It is also the root of the pass-2 L-13 a11y result (`aria-selected` false on every option, `aria-activedescendant` null on 7 routes): a select with no value to model.
defects.reproduction: grep above returns 0. In the running app at any route, no element in the dock nav has an `href`; the trigger is `role=combobox` and its children are `role=option`.
defects.proposedCure: Replace the Select with glass-ui `DropdownMenu` + `RouterLink` items (glass-ui ships ./dropdown-menu; the subpath idiom is already used 15x for /dock and 9x for /dom). This retires the role=option semantics mismatch, the aria-selected gap, the aria-activedescendant gap and the `"__admin_toggle__"` sentinel (pass-1 L-8) in one move — a mode command in a menu is an ordinary DropdownMenuItem, which is not a value and never was.

defects.defect: MAJOR (independently re-confirmed this pass, with a new measurement) — the shell depends on a feature for its auth read. `DockViewSelect.vue:8` imports `SESSION_PORT_KEY` from `demo/palettes/usePalettePorts` and `:35` injects it, to read one boolean at `:122`. The port named `Symbol("palette.session")` has ZERO consumers inside `demo/palettes/`.
defects.evidence: `grep -rln "SESSION_PORT_KEY" demo --include="*.vue" --include="*.ts"` -> 6 files: demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue, demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue, demo/shell/dock/menus/ProfileSection.vue, demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue, demo/shell/dock/menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue, demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts (the provider). 5 of 6 are demo/shell/dock/**; zero palette consumers. Port contents at usePalettePorts.ts:126-135 are 100% platform auth, sourced at :57-59 from demo/platform/auth/{useAdminAuth,useUserAuth,useSession}. demo/platform/auth/useAdminAuth.ts:17-25 is a module-level lazy singleton — `useAdminAuth().isAuthenticated` returns the identical computed to every caller with no injection at all. And Dock.vue:37 already injects the same port and Dock.vue:44 feeds it into useDockAdminMode, while passing this child five other props (Dock.vue:167-174).
defects.mechanism: A platform concern (identity/auth) is homed inside a feature module and keyed with the feature's name, which forces five shell->feature edges. The child then opens a SECOND acquisition path (inject) for a sixth datum its own parent already holds and already prop-drills — five-of-six by prop, one-of-six by inject, no rule being followed.
defects.reproduction: grep above. Also: the component is un-mountable in isolation — with no provider, `inject(SESSION_PORT_KEY)!` is undefined and the template's `pm.isAdminAuthenticated.value` at :122 throws.
defects.proposedCure: Move the session port to demo/platform/auth/ (it is already entirely platform code) and delete the inject here: pass `isAdminAuthenticated` as the sixth prop, or drop it entirely since useAdminAuth() is a module singleton. Deletes all five shell->feature edges. Direction becomes platform -> shell/nav -> shell/dock -> glass-ui, acyclic, with features reading the shell and the shell reading no feature.

defects.defect: MINOR (new this pass) — CORRECTION to pass-1 L-12, which recorded edict 5 (root-level styling) as PASS. That verdict examined only the `<style scoped>` block and the two global recipes. The template carries three per-instance overrides, one of them a self-documented unpaid root fix that reaches through the design system's internals.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue:69 `[&>span]:line-clamp-none` — the file's own comment at :57-59 states the root fix is a `clampLabel` prop on glass-ui DockSelectTrigger, 'filed coordination/Q.md §3'. :90 `min-w-[12rem]` on SelectContent, with the comment at :89 admitting it overrides `--menu-min-w`. :96 and :127 `py-1.5 px-2.5` on every SelectItem, written twice. (Edict 6 PASS is upheld: `.gold-shimmer-icon` at demo/styles/utils.css:162 and `.palettes-ramp-text` at :192 are correctly global, and the :159-161 `transition: --accent-view` is a genuinely scope-local bounded animation over a registered property.)
defects.mechanism: Per-instance overrides substituting for a root-level design-system change; the :69 case is an arbitrary-variant escape hatch used to undo a decision made inside glass-ui, with the correct fix already identified and unpaid.
defects.reproduction: Read demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue:69, :89-90, :96, :127.
defects.proposedCure: Pay the filed root fixes at the glass-ui root component level via the standing BH/BI relay: a `clampLabel` prop on DockSelectTrigger, a `--menu-min-w` token value that fits long view labels, and item padding on SelectItem's root. Delete all three brackets here.

defects.defect: MINOR (new this pass) — `demo/shell/dock/composables/usePopupMutex.ts` is a self-declared local fork of a glass-ui composable that glass-ui DELETED. A fork with a dead parent is a dual implementation that can never converge.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/composables/usePopupMutex.ts:1-2 verbatim: '// `usePopupMutex` was retired upstream from glass-ui at the D-II tranche. // Local fork — single-open mutex for dock popups with a brief swap delay.' Called once at Dock.vue:69; `popupModel("view-select")` is handed to this component as v-model:open at Dock.vue:168. glass-ui 7.0.0 owns ./dock (41626 B, 15 demo consumers).
defects.mechanism: A design-system boundary crossed by copying rather than negotiating. Joins demo/ui/** (pass-1 L-5 / pass-2 L-15) and demo/shell/dock/index.ts (pass-1 L-9) as the third demo-side structure that exists only because a glass-ui boundary was forked instead of extended. Edict 4 and edict 2's no-legacy clause.
defects.reproduction: `sed -n '1,2p' demo/shell/dock/composables/usePopupMutex.ts`.
defects.proposedCure: Relay to glass-ui ./dock as a `DockPopoverGroup` primitive — the four keys named at Dock.vue:70-73 are its entire API — then delete the fork. NOTE: I raised and then DISPROVED a behavioural claim against this fork (that its 180 ms write-transforming swap desyncs the defineModel round trip). Measured: with @mbabb open, pointerdown+pointerup+click on .view-select-trigger gives t=0 view=false/mbabb=true/options=0, t=80 mbabb=false, t=240 view=true/options=7, held to t=1040. Control identical. The finding rests on the fork's existence only.

result.strongestDefect: L-20 — the admin-authorisation ink leak. `isAdminMode` (useDockAdminMode.ts:31) is a second writable copy of `currentView in adminViews`, raised by a watch that has no else branch (:52-56) and lowered only through a path gated on admin authentication (:41-47 via DockViewSelect.vue:122). Because `atmosphere` and `blob` are in `adminViews` while carrying no `meta.admin` and no route guard, any unauthenticated visitor who opens `/#/atmosphere` or `/#/blob` is placed in admin mode for the whole session, and this component paints the product's admin gold (`--dock-ring: var(--color-gold)` at :70, `gold-shimmer-icon` at :80) on every view thereafter. Measured live: `#/atmosphere` -> ring `var(--color-gold)`, icon `gold-shimmer-icon`, computed color `oklch(0.751 0.147 84.2)` = the resolved `--color-gold`; then `location.hash='#/'` with no reload -> still gold on the Home glyph; independently again via `#/blob` -> `#/gradient`. It is the same disease as the pass-1 BLOCKER L-1 (option set and model value have different owners) — a `ref`/array duplicate of something `VIEW_MAP` plus the route already know — and like L-1 it becomes unrepresentable, not merely fixed, once `isAdminMode` is a `computed` over one nav table.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so no global negative is claimed. One axis of the challenge does hold up under proof and is recorded as such (report §L-11, sharpened by §L-16): the component's value.js public-surface discipline is clean. `DockViewSelect.vue` imports nothing from `@mkbabb/value.js` at all — its only package imports are `@lucide/vue`, `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock` and `vue` — so it cannot write an import a real consumer could not. Repo-wide, `grep -rn "@src/" demo --include="*.vue" --include="*.ts" | grep -v assets/docs | wc -l` returns 0, and `vite.config.ts:37-50` GENERATES the self-alias set from `package.json#exports` (7 subpaths: ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize, mirrored 1:1 by src/subpaths/*.ts), so the runtime alias set cannot drift from the published map. Every demo value.js import goes through the exports map. Two further sub-verdicts survive as proved negatives: edict 6 (animations never deleted) PASSES — `.gold-shimmer-icon` and `.palettes-ramp-text` were consolidated to demo/styles/utils.css:162,192 rather than dropped, and the scoped `transition: --accent-view` at :159-161 is a legitimately bounded animation over a property registered at demo/styles/foundation.css:192; and edict 8 (verbatimModuleSyntax) PASSES — line 9 is the file's only type-only import and is written `import type`. Finally, one hypothesis I raised was disproved by measurement rather than left standing: the `usePopupMutex` fork's 180 ms write-transforming swap does NOT desync the `defineModel` round trip (measured swap completes cleanly at t≈240 ms, matching the uncontended control), and an earlier probe of mine that reported "the select never opens" was an instrument error — it dispatched only `click()` where reka-ui requires `pointerdown`. That correction is recorded in the report rather than shipped as a finding.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue` (area demo/shell), audited at branch tranche-u / HEAD c654824e
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant). Declared at spawn, not inherited; the receipt heads both the original report and my addendum.
result.strongestDefect: D-15 — the unconditional inline `--dock-ring` override at DockViewSelect.vue:70 writes a bare `<color>` into what glass-ui 7.0.0 defines as a *box-shadow* token (`--dock-ring: var(--focus-ring-shadow)`) consumed as `.dock-select-trigger:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--dock-ring); outline: none; }`. The substitution is invalid at computed-value time, so the trigger computes `box-shadow: none` with `outline-style: none` while `:focus-visible` matches — a total, silent, always-on loss of the keyboard focus indicator on the control through which the entire product is navigated (WCAG 2.4.7). Measured with a sibling control and photographed. It is masked in the one capture matrix that could have caught it (forced-colors, where glass-ui re-adds an outline), and it is a one-line deletion to fix.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Negatives were nonetheless proven rather than assumed, and are recorded in the report so no later seat re-runs them: no rAF loop in this component (the only dock rAF is Dock.vue:105, one-shot, cleared by @animationend.self); no ValueUnit/parseCssColor/oklch-HSV surface (this component touches no colour values — `--accent-view` arrives pre-resolved from useViewAccents.ts:144); the documented `defineModel` stale-read hazard is not exploited (`open` is written and never read back, so a local shallowRef cache would be contrivance); `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean (`import type { ViewEntry }` at :9, all other imports are value imports); reduced motion genuinely neutralises the scoped transition (twice over — demo/styles/animations.css:184 sets `transition-duration: 0.01ms !important` on `*`, and glass-ui 7.0.0's a11y-overrides.css independently restricts `transition-property` to an allow-list that excludes custom properties); the `--accent-view` transition is live, not dead code (measured, 10 distinct interpolated values across a switch); tap targets clear AA everywhere (trigger 60x32 desktop / 59x33 mobile, options 174x44) so this component contributes 0 to the matrix's 60 smallTapTargets; the trigger is named, so it contributes 0 to the matrix's 18 namelessButtons; the SFC compiles clean (`parse errors: 0`).

defects.defect: Inline `--dock-ring` override is a type error against the glass-ui 7.0.0 producer contract and destroys the keyboard focus indicator on the product's primary navigation control. Fires unconditionally — both ternary arms write a colour — on every route, for every user, in both schemes and both modes.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue:70 writes `--dock-ring: var(--color-gold) | var(--accent-view)`. Producer contract, pasted from the shipped dist: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/sizing.css → `--dock-ring: var(--focus-ring-shadow);`  and node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/index.css → `.dock-icon-button:focus-visible, .dock-tab-button:focus-visible, .dock-select-trigger:focus-visible, .dock-dropdown-trigger:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--dock-ring); outline: none; }`. Measured (probe/probe-dvs4.mjs, private chromium 1440x900, /#/): {"matchesFocusVisible": true, "dockRingToken": "oklch(0.471189 0.188448 9.83402)", "focusRingShadowToken": "0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(47.11% 0.1884 9.83deg) 30%, transparent), 0 0 8px color-mi", "boxShadow": "none", "outline": "none 3px color(srgb 0 0 0 / 0.8)"}. Control, sibling control that does NOT override the token: {"matchesFocusVisible": true, "dockRingToken": "0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(...) 30%, transparent), 0 0 8px color-mix(..."}. Reached by real Tab traversal: {"isViewSelect": true, "focusVisible": true, "boxShadow": "none"}. Photograph: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-dockviewselect/probe/dock-focus.png
defects.mechanism: producer-token trespass — the consumer writes into the design system's token namespace with a value of the wrong TYPE, hijacking an accessibility token for decoration. The code comment at :62-65 admits the producer side was never confirmed ('the producer-side ring consume is the filed L13/W7-1 ask') and shipped on the assumption; one grep of the shipped node_modules refutes it.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-dockviewselect/probe/probe-dvs4.mjs` with the dev server on :9000. By hand: load http://localhost:9000/#/, press Tab until the dock view-select is document.activeElement, observe no ring and no outline.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `--dock-ring` write entirely (one line). A decorative view-hue rim is a NEW producer primitive, not an override of the focus-ring token: relay a `--dock-trigger-rim` colour token (or a `rim` prop on DockTrigger) to the glass-ui BH inbox under the standing BH/BI relay edict and consume it when it lands. The seal→trigger continuity the comment protects is already carried by the glyph — Dock.vue:259-263 says so. Family cure: a consumer may READ producer tokens; it may not WRITE them.

defects.defect: The option set is not a total function of the route space: on 7 of the 14 named views the combobox renders value-less — blank trigger label, every option `unchecked`. Half the product's route space renders its primary nav in a state the design never specifies.
defects.evidence: useDockAdminMode.ts:26-27 holds two hand-written arrays; :34-39 returns one OR the other, never a union, never route-derived. Select is bound `:model-value="currentView"` (DockViewSelect.vue:52), so an unlisted route matches no SelectItem. Measured (probe/probe-dvs.mjs, anonymous): "P1 atmosphere trigger": {"text": "", "box": [60,32]}; "P1 options": 7 rows, every one "sel":"false"/"state":"unchecked". Same at /#/admin/users: "P5 admin/users trigger": {"text": ""}. Control: "P4 control fresh /#/gradient": {"text": "Gradient"}. Corroborated in the committed capture set — shots/safari-desktop-light/atmosphere.png and .../admin-users.png show the dock pill as icon+chevron only, against every other route's icon+label+chevron.
defects.mechanism: the menu models the view space as literal arrays maintained by hand beside VIEW_MAP instead of a projection of it; nothing makes 'the current view has a row' true by construction.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere (or /#/blob, or any /#/admin/*) in a clean profile as an anonymous visitor; the dock trigger shows an icon and a chevron and no label.
defects.proposedCure: Put the grouping on the schema (`PaneConfig.group: "user" | "admin"` in viewSchema.ts) and derive `viewEntries` by filtering VIEW_MAP / router.getRoutes() partitioned by `meta.admin`. The drift becomes unrepresentable and atmosphere/blob return to the user set the schema already puts them in (hue shifts 280/320 on the primary 40-degree fan, versus 0 for every genuine admin view).

defects.defect: `isAdminMode` is a latch: it is set true by a one-directional watcher and never cleared on the anonymous path, so one deep link disables the entire per-view chromatic voice for the rest of the session and tells an unauthenticated visitor they are an admin.
defects.evidence: useDockAdminMode.ts:55-59 sets true only; the only clears are toggleAdminMode() (its row is `v-if="pm.isAdminAuthenticated.value"`, DockViewSelect.vue:122 — absent for anonymous users) and a non-immediate `watch(isAdminAuthenticated)` at :62 that cannot fire when the value was already false. The seed at :32 reads currentView at setup, before router.isReady() resolves (useViewManager.ts:41). Measured (probe/probe-dvs.mjs): "P2 after switching to Home": {"text":"Home","styleAttr":"--dock-ring: var(--color-gold); …","goldIcon":true}; "P3 after switching to Gradient": {"text":"Gradient","styleAttr":"--dock-ring: var(--color-gold); …","goldIcon":true}; control "P4 control fresh /#/gradient": {"styleAttr":"--dock-ring: var(--accent-view);","goldIcon":false}. Consumers in this file: :80 keeps gold-shimmer-icon on the glyph, :83 withholds `color: var(--accent-view)` from it.
defects.mechanism: derived state stored in a `ref` and mutated by a one-directional watcher. There is no state here; there is only the route.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere anonymously, then pick `Home` from the dock menu: the trigger icon stays gold and never returns to the view accent for the rest of the session.
defects.proposedCure: `const isAdminMode = computed(() => VIEW_MAP[currentView.value].group === "admin" && isAdminAuthenticated.value)`. The latch, both watchers and the ref all die; the flag becomes unfalsifiable by construction.

defects.defect: With `hide-indicator` on every row and the weight marker retired, the current view is visually unmarked the instant the roving keyboard cursor moves off it — selection exists only in the accessibility tree.
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:97 sets `hide-indicator`; the comment at :99-109 records the `font-semibold` marker's retirement, leaving 'aria-selected + the producer's glass-quiet highlighted-on-open row' — but data-highlighted is the roving cursor, not the selection. Measured (probe/probe-dvs3.mjs, /#/browse, keyboard-opened, then 2x ArrowDown): {"text":"Browse","sel":"true","hl":null,"bg":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","shadow":"none","fw":"400"} — byte-identical in background, box-shadow, colour and weight to {"text":"Home","sel":"false","hl":null,"bg":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","shadow":"none","fw":"400"}, while the mark sits on {"text":"Mix","sel":"false","hl":"","bg":"oklab(0.915626 … / 0.52)","shadow":"RING"}.
defects.mechanism: two independent removals (the check indicator at T-10, the weight marker at P4-R4) each assumed the other carried the signal; nothing was left.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/browse → focus the dock view-select → Enter → ArrowDown twice → the Browse row is indistinguishable from every other row.
defects.proposedCure: One non-weight, non-hue selection mark that survives the roving cursor — a leading inset rule keyed on `[data-state="checked"]`, authored at the glass-ui SelectItem root per the root-styling edict, never per instance here. Under the anchor-based navigation cure it becomes `aria-current="page"`, which already has paint conventions.

defects.defect: On mobile the combobox exposes NO value at all to assistive technology — the accessibility node has a name and no `value` property whatsoever.
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:87 `<SelectValue v-if="isDesktop" />` removes the node that carries the value below 1024px. Measured via CDP Accessibility.getPartialAXTree (probe/probe-dvs2.mjs, 390x844 isMobile, /#/gradient): "D1 mobile trigger": {"text": "", "ariaLabel": "Select view", "box": [59,33]}; "D2 mobile AX node": [{"role": "combobox", "name": "Select view"}] — no value key. Desktop control (probe/probe-dvs.mjs): [{"role":"combobox","name":"Select view","value":"Home","nameFrom":["attribute:aria-label=Select view"]}].
defects.mechanism: the value is treated as furniture and rendered conditionally; on desktop it survives only by accident, as SelectValue's text becoming the combobox's AX value despite aria-label taking the name.
defects.reproduction: `node probe/probe-dvs2.mjs`, or load http://localhost:9000/#/gradient at 390px width and read the trigger's AX node — role combobox, name 'Select view', no value.
defects.proposedCure: Never conditionally render the value node. Mount SelectValue always and hide its TEXT responsively at the glass-ui trigger root (sr-only / container query). Pair with dropping the constant `aria-label` so the visible label is the name (WCAG 2.5.3).

defects.defect: `SelectGroup` is opened with no `SelectLabel`, so it advertises an `aria-labelledby` IDREF that resolves to nothing; and a raw `<div>` separator sits inside `role="group"` in a listbox while the design system's `SelectSeparator` ships unused.
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:91 opens SelectGroup with no label; :123 is `<div class="border-t border-border my-1">`. Measured (probe/probe-dvs2.mjs, admin-authenticated so the separator branch renders): "A1 listbox aria": {"lbLabel": null, "lbLabelledby": null, "groups": [{"label": null, "labelledby": "reka-select-group-v-60", "labelTargetExists": false, "nonOptionElementChildren": ["DIV.border-t border-border my-1"]}]}. The unused primitive: `cat demo/ui/select/index.ts` exports SelectSeparator, and `grep -rn "SelectSeparator" demo/ --include="*.vue" --include="*.ts"` returns only that declaration line.
defects.mechanism: a structural primitive used for its default styling rather than its semantics, plus a hand-rolled re-implementation of a shipped design-system component (edicts 4 and 5).
defects.reproduction: `node probe/probe-dvs2.mjs` — read `groups[0].labelTargetExists: false` and `nonOptionElementChildren`.
defects.proposedCure: There is one group — the listbox IS the group; drop SelectGroup, or give it a SelectLabel naming the navigation. Replace the div with `<SelectSeparator>`. Both disappear under the anchor-menu transposition.

defects.defect: CORRECTION to the first pass's D-10: `[&>span]:line-clamp-none` at :69 cancels nothing — the producer rule it targets does not exist on this element in glass-ui 7.0.0. It is dead code, its comment is stale, and the five-tranche-old `clampLabel` producer ask it justifies is moot for this call site.
defects.evidence: The clamp lives on glass-ui's styled SelectTrigger: `grep -o ".\{160\}line-clamp.\{80\}" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/select-BcBAyLXA.js` → '…rounded-pill px-3 py-2 text-dropdown … [&>span]:line-clamp-1 transition-control…'. But this file uses `DockTrigger for="select"`, which mounts reka's BARE SelectTrigger plus a chevron (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/dock.js:1225-1230), and the dock stylesheet has no clamp at all: `grep -o "line-clamp[^;]*;" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/controls/triggers.css` → no output; `grep -ro "line-clamp[^\"';}]*" .../dist/dock.js .../dist/components/dock/` → no output. Measured effect (probe/probe-dvs4.mjs): "H4 trigger label span": [{"text":"Home","display":"block","webkitLineClamp":"none","overflow":"visible","boxOrient":"horizontal"}] — the class only forces display:block/overflow:visible.
defects.mechanism: same family as D-15 — producer-token/producer-rule trespass decided by reading a stale comment instead of the shipped producer. Drift that the Glass 7 adoption (W44) should have swept and did not.
defects.reproduction: The two greps above against node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0, plus `node probe/probe-dvs4.mjs` for the computed span.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the class and the :57-59 comment; close the `clampLabel` row in the coordination ledger with 'producer changed shape; consumer no longer affected' rather than re-filing it into another tranche.

defects.defect: Vacuous gate: zero tests target this component's behaviour. The entire admin branch, the gold identity, the focus ring, the selection paint and the option-set derivation are unobserved by any test.
defects.evidence: `grep -rln "DockViewSelect\|useDockAdminMode\|__admin_toggle__" test/ e2e/ demo/test/` → no output. Coverage is indirect and shallow: e2e/smoke/fixtures/dock.ts:59-79 asserts only that a combobox named 'Select view' exists and that clicking a named role=option navigates; e2e/smoke/page-load.spec.ts:31-33 asserts visibility; e2e/smoke/perf/view-switch-frame-budget.spec.ts:54 uses it as a stopwatch. The admin suite never touches the selector — e2e/smoke/admin/admin-walk.spec.ts:69-71 reaches every admin view by `page.goto(path)`.
defects.mechanism: the gate tests reka-ui, not this component. Green-keeping mutations: delete the `:style` --dock-ring binding (:70); set it to any other invalid value; delete `:class="isAdminMode && 'gold-shimmer-icon'"` (:80) and the :83 accent style; delete the whole `<template v-if="pm.isAdminAuthenticated…">` block (:122-142); toggle `hide-indicator` (:97); change `entry.id === 'palettes'` (:116) to 'browse'; replace viewEntries with a hard-coded 7-row literal; drop `<SelectValue v-if="isDesktop" />` (:87) — openView() clicks options, not the label. Only renaming a view label or removing the aria-label is caught.
defects.reproduction: Apply any mutation in the list above and run `npm test && npx playwright test` — green.
defects.proposedCure: Once D-6/D-10's inject is removed the contract is small and pure — five props in, one id out. Assert: (a) for EVERY ViewId in VIEW_MAP the rendered menu contains a checked row for the current view; (b) the trigger's computed box-shadow is non-`none` under :focus-visible; (c) isAdminMode=false implies no gold; plus one e2e that reaches an admin view THROUGH the menu rather than by goto.

defects.defect: The advertised 'bounded view-switch hue sweep' interpolates in oklab (rectangular), so it cuts a chord through the desaturated middle rather than travelling the hue arc, and every intermediate frame is a colour useViewAccents never gamut-mapped or contrast-guarded.
defects.evidence: Measured per-rAF across a picker→gradient switch (probe/probe-dvs2.mjs): {"distinctValues": 10, "first": "oklch(0.471189 0.188448 9.83402)", "mid": "474ms oklab(0.471189 -0.0231664 -0.10933)", "last": "796ms oklch(0.471189 0.132793 249.834)", uniqSample includes "oklab(0.471189 0.0209336 -0.0794474)"} — chroma 0.188 → 0.082 → 0.133 while L stays pinned at 0.4712. Registration: demo/styles/foundation.css:192-198 `@property --accent-view { syntax: "<color>"; }`. The claim it contradicts: DockViewSelect.vue:155-158, 'the navigation still SWEEPS to the new view's hue'.
defects.mechanism: a `<color>`-typed registered property interpolates componentwise in oklab; hue travel requires an angle-typed axis. The W7-4 guard (gamut-map to cusp + WCAG 3:1 re-guard) is applied to endpoints only.
defects.reproduction: `node probe/probe-dvs2.mjs` and read the C1 block. (This measurement also PROVES the transition is live rather than dead code — the first pass argued it from registration alone.)
defects.proposedCure: Animate an `<angle>`-registered hue and compose the colour from it if the arc is what is wanted; otherwise correct the comment to describe the chord and state explicitly that the guard covers endpoints only.

defects.defect: `__admin_toggle__` is a magic string duplicated across two files, smuggled into the ViewId value space as a listbox `option` that can never become the listbox's value, and cast past the type system straight into `router.push`.
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:125 `value="__admin_toggle__"` and useDockAdminMode.ts:68 `if (id === "__admin_toggle__")` — two literals, no shared constant. useDockAdminMode.ts:72 `viewManager.switchView(id as ViewId)` is the only thing between an arbitrary emitted string and `router.push({ name: <that string> })`; viewSchema.ts:236 exports `isViewId()` — a predicate written for exactly this boundary — and it is unused. Measured (probe/probe-dvs2.mjs, authenticated): the row is a real role=option, permanently {"text":"Admin","sel":"false","state":"unchecked"} in user mode and {"text":"Back to app","sel":"false","state":"unchecked"} in admin mode.
defects.mechanism: a command wearing an option's role, because a value control (Select) is carrying navigation; the sentinel exists only to smuggle a non-value through a value channel.
defects.reproduction: Seed `localStorage["palette-admin-token"]` (the key e2e/smoke/admin/fixtures/admin-auth.ts:22 uses), open the dock menu, inspect the Admin row's aria-selected — false in every state.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition: this is a navigation menu, not a form field. Anchor rows (`<a href="#/browse">`) with `aria-current="page"` inside glass-ui's existing DropdownMenu primitives — then arrow keys move focus and commit nothing, cmd/middle-click opens a tab (impossible today), the mode toggle becomes a `<button>`, and the sentinel, the cast and the `if` in onViewChange all evaporate. In the interim the boundary must be `if (!isViewId(id)) return;`, never a cast.

defects.defect: Two independent sources of truth for 'is this an admin?', and the child re-injects the session port it is already given props from — a dual path that also makes the component un-mountable in a unit test.
defects.evidence: Parent: Dock.vue:37 injects SESSION_PORT_KEY and Dock.vue:44 hands isAdminAuthenticated into useDockAdminMode, which gates the list on `isAdminMode.value && isAdminAuthenticated.value` (useDockAdminMode.ts:35). Child: DockViewSelect.vue:35 injects SESSION_PORT_KEY again and gates the admin row on `pm.isAdminAuthenticated.value` alone (:122). Different predicates, one menu — and they disagree in exactly the measured D-2/D-3 state. The `!` at :35 turns a missing provider into a render-time TypeError. Type erosion alongside: `currentIcon: unknown` (:19) and `ViewEntry { icon: unknown; [k: string]: unknown }` (useDockAdminMode.ts:7-12) throw away the `icon: Component` that viewSchema.ts:74 already types correctly.
defects.mechanism: the child re-derives a fact the parent already owns and passes four other props for; the open index signature exists only to let `{ id, ...VIEW_MAP[id] }` typecheck and in doing so disables excess-property checking for every consumer.
defects.reproduction: Mount DockViewSelect in isolation without a SESSION_PORT_KEY provider: the template throws at :122 rather than failing typed. (Static; no browser needed.)
defects.proposedCure: useDockAdminMode returns the whole menu model — rows plus an optional `adminRow: { mode: "enter" | "exit" } | null` — and DockViewSelect renders it. One predicate, one place, one prop; the child's inject and its `!` both disappear. Type icon as `Component` and drop the index signature by spreading explicitly.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant). Seat explicitly declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — on mobile the layer is never mounted, yet its trigger stays named, non-aria-hidden and programmatically focusable in the accessibility tree inside a 0-width `overflow: visible` slot; activating it (as AT does) sets `activeLayer="action-bar"` against a face that does not exist, collapsing the entire dock from 254.7×59.5 to 28.1×64.7 px with all three faces inert and NO active face — destroying view nav, login and account with no recovery short of reload. `VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:141` forbids "dock collapse" by name.
result.negativeProof: Bounded negative (the verdict is DEFECTIVE, but these were tested and hold): (1) `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean — all three type-only imports are `import type` at ActionBarLayer.vue:2,5,9; (2) the `inert` binding is correct — measured, the inactive sub-layer and its descendants report `inert: true` while the active one does not, so the hidden face does not pollute the a11y tree (the D-1 failure belongs to the trigger, not this binding); (3) not a god module — 158 lines, one responsibility; (4) no animation was deleted — the `vj-morph` icon transition rides the sanctioned family with only geometry parameterised (`--vj-morph-scale: 0.7`, `--vj-morph-y: 0px`), exactly what `demo/styles/animations.css:62–65` permits a consuming site to do; (5) the provide/inject seam at :22 is a genuine re-scope, not a shim; (6) aria-labels on the toggle are present and mode-accurate (the defect is the missing state, not a missing name); (7) RTL: no defect found — the flex row and `inset: 0` mirror correctly and `--vj-morph-x` is `0px` so the icon morph is direction-neutral — but I captured no RTL frame, so this is "no defect found", not positive proof.

defects.defect: The mobile state was never designed, and asking for it collapses the entire dock. The action-bar face is not mounted below `lg`, but its trigger survives as a named, focusable, non-aria-hidden button painted outside a 0-width slot.
defects.evidence: Measured WebKit 390×844 vs 1440×900 (`D-abl-faces.mjs`): desktop {faceCount:4, gridPresent:true, colorInputW:447.5} vs mobile {faceCount:3, gridPresent:false, colorInputW:null}. Trigger at 390w: btn {x:151.4,y:32.2,w:33.3,h:33.3,tabindex:"-1",ariaHidden:null,disabled:false}; slot {w:0, gridTemplateColumns:"0px", overflow:"visible"}; `elementFromPoint(centre)` → `DIV.segmented-indicator`; `locator.tap()` → TimeoutError; `b.focus()` → activeElement===b. After activation: `.glass-dock` 254.7×59.5 → 28.1×64.7, `--dock-expanded-px` 255px→69px, all 3 faces inert width 0, `activeFace: NONE`. Figure `D2-mobile-dark-after-toggle-dock-collapsed.png`. Canon: docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:141 "No full-slab remount hole, rAF-delayed blank, or dock collapse."
defects.mechanism: Two independent presence predicates in two files: `Dock.vue:156` gates `<ActionBarLayer v-if="actionBar">` on `App.vue:38` `colorPickerRef?.actionBarContext ?? null` (undefined on mobile because the Picker pane is not mounted), while `ActionBarToggle.vue:92` keeps the trigger in the DOM/a11y tree with only a 0fr slot and tabindex=-1 hiding it. `Dock.vue:113` then selects a face id that has no face.
defects.reproduction: WebKit 390×844 → http://localhost:9000/?color=%23abcdef → wait 4s → `document.querySelector('[aria-label="Toggle action bar"]').click()` (the exact call an AT activation performs). Dock collapses to an empty 28×65 sliver; no recovery without reload.
defects.proposedCure: Make presence one derived fact, not two predicates: let `<DockCrossfade>`'s own face registry be the source (glass 7 exposes `faces: Readonly<Ref<DockFaceDescriptor[]>>` in `dockCrossfadeContext.d.ts`) so a face that never registers cannot be selected and the trigger renders from `faces`. Then actually design the mobile action bar — on 390px it is the primary action surface, not a desktop luxury (its `input` sub-layer measures 325px against a 227px mobile face).

defects.defect: Every control in this layer is unreachable by keyboard in WebKit — the app's stated first-class engine — while the same page in Chromium reaches all six.
defects.evidence: Measured with the action bar open, activeElement after each Tab. webkit first-6: ["l component value","a component value","b component value","l channel","L channel","A channel"] → 0 in dock (12 tabs also 0, ring wraps through BODY after 8 stops). chromium first-6: ["Back [IN-DOCK]","Reset color [IN-DOCK]","Copy color [IN-DOCK]","Random color [IN-DOCK]","Palettes [IN-DOCK]","Extract palette [IN-DOCK]"]. Ancestor audit of `[aria-label="Reset color"]` up to `.glass-dock`: no inert, no aria-hidden, no visibility:hidden, no content-visibility. Control dump: Back/Reset/Copy/Random/Palettes/Extract/Open color input all `tabindex: null`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:129 (horizontal Dock/rail roving focus).
defects.mechanism: Safari's shipping default keyboard mode tabs to links, form fields and elements carrying an EXPLICIT tabindex — not to bare `<button>`. Every control ActionBarLayer renders is a bare button with no tabindex. The convention exists in-repo and this file omits it: `ConsoleRail.vue:31,183` implements a roving tabindex; the sibling `ActionBarToggle.vue:92` passes `:tabindex="visible ? 0 : -1"` to the same `DockControl` primitive; `ActionBarLayer.vue:129–142` passes none.
defects.reproduction: WebKit 1440×900, open the action bar, Tab from `<body>` 12×; no activeElement satisfies `closest('.glass-dock')`. Identical script in Chromium reaches all six on the first six presses.
defects.proposedCure: Not `tabindex=0` sprinkling. The layer is a horizontal control run — implement the constitution's roving-focus law (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:129): one tab stop for the run, arrows within, Home/End at the ends, activation separate from movement. That machine already exists in this repo at `ConsoleRail.vue:183`; the design defect is inventing a control run without adopting the house rail law.

defects.defect: The component's central mechanism is a fiction: the local `useLayerTransition` schedules a 260ms crossfade window for a crossfade that never runs. The sub-layer swap is a hard cut.
defects.evidence: Sampled every ~30ms, WebKit 1440×900: t=0 [ActionToolbar opacity 1 visible, ColorInput opacity 0 hidden]; t=32 [opacity 0 is-leaving, opacity 1 is-active] — one frame; t=63..246 unchanged 214ms; t=277 `is-leaving` cleared (the 260ms timer); t=699 outgoing finally `visibility: hidden`. Computed style on both sub-layers: `transitionProperty: "visibility"`, `transitionDuration: "0s"`. `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/layers.css` declares `.dock-layer { transition: visibility 0s linear var(--duration-normal); }` and NO opacity transition; opacity is animated only under `.glass-dock[data-morphing]` (measured false throughout). The real overlap lives on `.dock-face` + `[data-crossfading]` + `--dock-t` in `crossfade.css` — a different element and scalar this component does not participate in.
defects.mechanism: `ActionBarLayer.vue:53–94` reimplements a two-ref `currentLayer`/`leavingLayer` contract whose CSS counterpart was never a CSS opacity transition. `SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS = 260` (`:62`) buys only a 260ms delay before `visibility: hidden`.
defects.reproduction: WebKit 1440×900 → /?color=%23abcdef → open Tools → click `[aria-label="Open color input"]` while sampling `getComputedStyle(child).opacity` every 30ms on `.dock-layer-grid` children. Opacity is binary at the first post-click frame.
defects.proposedCure: Delete lines 53–94 and `subLayerProps`; mount `<DockCrossfade :active="activeSubLayer" reserve="inline">` with the two sub-layers as `<DockLayer>` faces — the producer runs a real two-child opacity overlap on the one dock spring (velocity-continuous, interruptible).

defects.defect: The shim's stated retirement condition is already met and its header comment is factually false in three ways — glass 7.0.0 ships both a public component and a public composable successor, from the module specifier line 8 already imports from.
defects.evidence: `node -e "…lastIndexOf('export')…" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/dock.js` → `pt as DockControl, rt as DockCrossfade, ft as DockLayer, lt as DockLayerGroup, _t as DockSeparator`. `dist/components/dock/DockCrossfade.vue.d.ts` doc-comment: "the thin controlled face-swap core … The controlled-no-rail case (a consumer) consumes this DIRECTLY … `reserve?: \"block\"|\"inline\"` — `inline` reserves the peak WIDTH (a horizontal control run) … A dissolving focus-holding face transfers focus to its successor, else the body". `dist/components/dock/composables/dockCrossfadeContext.d.ts` exports `useDockCrossfadeContext()` returning `activeId: Readonly<Ref<string>>` and `leavingId: Readonly<Ref<string|null>>` — the "exact two-refs contract" verbatim. Contradicted claims at ActionBarLayer.vue:54–61.
defects.mechanism: The file's comment asserts "no public composable successor" and "offers no ... successor", and `:67` carries `void opts.containerEl; // signature parity with the retired producer composable` — a back-compat parameter matching a function that exists nowhere. CARRY-LEDGER §F therefore tracks a condition that was already satisfied at adoption.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a static API-surface fact, verified by reading the installed `@mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0` type declarations and export table.
defects.proposedCure: RETIRE NOW, unconditionally: delete ActionBarLayer.vue:53–94 + `subLayerProps`; wrap the two sub-layers in `<DockCrossfade :active reserve="inline">` with `<DockLayer>` faces. Withdraw glass-ui relay O-6 mark M2 as already-answered by 7.0.0, and move the CARRY-LEDGER §F row from "retire at W47 if glass ships a successor" to "retire unconditionally — the successor shipped."

defects.defect: Activating the toggle translates it ~64px out from under the pointer that just clicked it: the box is never reserved, so each sub-layer swap re-measures and re-morphs the whole centre-anchored dock.
defects.evidence: Measured WebKit 1440×900: `--dock-expanded-px` 471px (main) → 326px (actions); dock measured 466.8px in input. `.dock-layer-grid` rect x/w: 634.0/184.0 (actions) → 563.6/324.8 (input) — a +140.8px content change on a centre-anchored dock, so the left edge moves −70.4px and the toggle moves from x=831 to ≈895 (+64px). Figures `D2-desktop-light-actions.png` vs `D2-desktop-light-input.png`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:30 (the dock band is reserved).
defects.mechanism: No peak-size reserve exists on the sub-layer container; the dock's `fit-content` measurement re-runs per swap, and the local 260ms timer is on an entirely separate clock from the dock's morph — two clocks for one moment.
defects.reproduction: WebKit 1440×900, open Tools, record `[aria-label="Open color input"]` boundingBox, click it, record the new toggle box. Displacement ≈ +64px on x.
defects.proposedCure: `<DockCrossfade reserve="inline">` — the producer measures the peak face width once (documented as "MEASURE-ONCE `min-block-size` (a running max — NOT a per-swap FLIP)"), so the band never changes width and the control never moves.

defects.defect: The focus law is half-designed: the actions→input leg leaves focus on `<body>`, while the input→propose leg focuses correctly — two legs of one three-state cycle obeying two different laws.
defects.evidence: Measured across the actions→input swap: focusBefore `<body class="relative" id="app" …>`, focusAfter `<body class="relative" id="app" …>`. Across input→propose: `document.activeElement` = `<span contenteditable role="textbox" aria-label="Propose a color name" …>`. The propose focus comes from `ColorInput.vue:252–262` (`requestAnimationFrame(() => inputColorRef.value?.focus())`), not from this component. `ColorInput.vue:283` exposes `focus: () => inputColorRef.value?.focus()`; `ActionBarLayer.vue:28` declares and `:116` binds `colorInputRef` — and never reads it. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:115.
defects.mechanism: The component owns the mode machine but delegates focus by accident: only the child's own prop-watcher happens to focus, and only on one of the two transitions. The handle needed for the missing leg is declared, bound, and unused.
defects.reproduction: WebKit 1440×900, open Tools, click `[aria-label="Open color input"]`, read `document.activeElement` → `<body>`. Click again into propose, read again → the contenteditable span.
defects.proposedCure: Stop re-deriving focus per leg: inherit the producer's documented law — `<DockCrossfade>` "transfers focus to its successor, else the body (un-inert-before-focus is load-bearing)" — so every face swap has one focus rule instead of one per branch.

defects.defect: The 260ms swap window is a JS timer and is not armed for `prefers-reduced-motion`; reduced motion does not resolve directly to the final geometry.
defects.evidence: Measured with `reducedMotion: "reduce"` (WebKit): t=0 leaving 0 vis visible/hidden; t=30 leaving 1 visible/visible; unchanged through t=245; t=275 leaving 0, vis hidden/visible. Byte-identical to the normal-motion run. `demo/styles/animations.css:183–192` neutralises CSS transitions/animations app-wide but cannot touch a `setTimeout`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:144 "Reduced motion resolves directly to the final geometry and stable chromatic state."
defects.mechanism: `SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS` is enforced by `setTimeout` at ActionBarLayer.vue:76–78; reduced motion is a media fact, so a code timer can never be its arm. Result: an invisible 443px `visibility: visible` element is held over the dock for 260ms before final geometry.
defects.reproduction: WebKit 1440×900 with `reducedMotion: "reduce"`, open Tools, click `[aria-label="Open color input"]`, sample `is-leaving` presence every 30ms — present t=30..245, cleared by t=275, identical to normal motion.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the producer spring via `<DockCrossfade>`, which honours the query internally; delete the timer. Generally: motion duration belongs to the design system's clock, never to a consumer's magic constant.

defects.defect: The toggle bypasses the dock's own glyph and touch-target tokens with per-instance overrides — glyph 20% over token, operable target 9% under token.
defects.evidence: Measured (WebKit 1440×900): toggle glyph 24.0×24.0 px, control 40.0×40.0 px. Tokens in `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/sizing.css`: `--dock-icon-glyph: max(calc(2.5rem*0.5), 1rem)` = 20px (measured resolved string `max( calc(calc(2.5rem * 1) * 0.5), 1rem )`); `--dock-touch-target: 2.75rem` = 44px. `--dock-control-glyph-size: var(--dock-icon-glyph)` resolves ON this button (measured) and is overridden by the instance utility. Source: ActionBarLayer.vue:138 `class="toggle-btn w-6 h-6 stroke-foreground"`, :139 `:style="{ '--toggle-hover-color': safeAccent }"`. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:72–73 (laws 7–8). Corroborated by the visual matrix's `smallTapTargets: 8` on `/#/`.
defects.mechanism: Size was set on the glyph and the operable target was left to fall out of it — the inverse of law 7 ("Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities"). Owner edict 5 (root-level styling) is violated twice: an inline custom property for hover accent and a Tailwind size utility, both per-instance overrides of a root that owns both.
defects.reproduction: WebKit 1440×900, open Tools, `getBoundingClientRect()` on `.toggle-btn` (24×24) and on `.toggle-btn.closest('button')` (40×40); compare to the computed `--dock-icon-glyph` (20px) and `--dock-touch-target` (44px).
defects.proposedCure: Delete both overrides. Size from `--dock-control-glyph-size`; let the control seat be the producer's `--dock-touch-target`. If the dock needs an accented icon hover, that is a `DockControl` variant inside glass-ui, not a `--toggle-hover-color` invented in one consumer.

defects.defect: `:hover` written with no `@media (hover: hover)` guard on a surface that ships to touch, against a convention this codebase already keeps elsewhere.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:149–151 `.toggle-btn:hover { stroke: var(--toggle-hover-color); }` — unguarded. `demo/color-session/ColorSpaceSelector.vue:257` wraps its hover register in `@media (hover: hover)`; every hover utility glass-ui emits sits inside `@media (hover:hover)` (verifiable in `dist/styles/components.css`). `grep -rn ":hover" demo/shell/dock/*.vue demo/shell/dock/layers/*.vue` returns exactly two bare-`:hover` scoped rules in the dock: `ActionButton.vue:117` and this one.
defects.mechanism: On touch WebKit `:hover` latches after tap and persists until another element is tapped, so the toggle keeps an accent stroke that carries no meaning.
defects.reproduction: HYPOTHESIS for the latch duration — I measured the missing guard and the in-repo convention, not the persistence itself. To close: touch context (`hasTouch: true`), tap the toggle, sample `getComputedStyle('.toggle-btn').stroke` after the tap completes.
defects.proposedCure: Wrap the rule in `@media (hover: hover)` — or better, delete it entirely with D-8 and let the accent hover be a glass-ui `DockControl` variant that already carries the guard.

defects.defect: The toggle's ⋮ means "Close propose" while the identical ⋮ at the identical size in the same dock means "Menu"; the control has three modes and exposes no expanded/pressed state to AT.
