defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:47–51 cycles `Type` → `Tag`/`EllipsisVertical` → `EllipsisVertical` with labels `Open color input` / `Propose color name` / `Close input` / `Close propose`. `demo/shell/dock/menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue:41` renders `MoreVertical class="w-6 h-6"` as the real menu. No `aria-pressed`/`aria-expanded` anywhere in the component; the sibling `ActionBarToggle.vue:93` does it correctly with `:aria-pressed="active"`. Label is a 168-char nested ternary at :131. Figure `D2-desktop-light-propose.png`. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:60 (PR-16): "`…` keeps a named menu purpose plus expanded state or is removed".
defects.mechanism: A single seat changes glyph species twice (typographic literal `T` → luggage `Tag` → overflow `⋮`) and signifies "close" with the universal overflow-menu glyph, while its state lives only in a mutating label.
defects.reproduction: WebKit 1440×900, open Tools, click the toggle twice to reach propose; the trailing control renders `EllipsisVertical` with aria-label `Close propose` while the dock's mobile menu trigger uses the same glyph at the same size for `Menu`.
defects.proposedCure: One seat, one meaning: make it a disclosure with `aria-expanded`, one glyph that inverts (`Type` ↔ `X`), and promote the propose leg out of the glyph cycle into a named affordance inside the input face where it belongs. Replace the template ternary with a labelled state table.

defects.defect: An unreconciled state: `propose` outlives the `canProposeName` predicate that gates entry to it.
defects.evidence: `cycleToolbarMode` (ActionBarLayer.vue:33–45) reads `actionBar.canProposeName.value` only at click time; nothing watches it afterwards. `toolbarMode` is a plain `ref` (:30). The same toolbar's `random()` action (`ActionToolbar.vue:26–36` → `ColorPicker.vue` `random`) can move the color to a named one while propose is open.
defects.mechanism: A designed state stored as mutable local state, gated by a reactive predicate that can change beneath it — so the toggle keeps rendering `Close propose` and `ColorInput` keeps propose mode for a color that can no longer be proposed.
defects.reproduction: HYPOTHESIS — mechanism read from source, not driven end-to-end this pass. To close: enter propose on an unnamed color, invoke `random()` until a named color lands, assert `toolbarMode !== "propose"`.
defects.proposedCure: Derive rather than store: `propose` is only reachable while `canProposeName` is true, so the mode should be a `computed` clamp over the predicate, not a `ref` that can desynchronise from it.

defects.defect: `.dock-layer-grid` is a phantom class with zero CSS rules; because it sets no `position`, the hidden/leaving sub-layer resolves its containing block against the OUTER dock face and covers the dock's live controls for 260ms.
defects.evidence: Measured computed style: `{display:"block", position:"static", gridTemplateColumns:"none", overflow:"visible"}`. `grep -rn "dock-layer-grid"` across the repo and `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/` returns exactly two hits, both in this file (:91, :101). `offsetParentOfInactive: "DIV.dock-face is-active"`. Rects: container 634.0/184.0; active sub-layer 634.0/184.0; inactive 569.0/302.0; leaving 499.0/443.0 (t=32..246). glass-ui `layers.css`: `.dock-layer:not(.is-active){position:absolute;inset:0}`, `.dock-layer.is-active{position:relative}`, `.dock-layer.is-leaving{opacity:0;visibility:visible}`.
defects.mechanism: A container named "grid" that is a block box; its children carry `grid-area: 1/1` inherited from the producer's `.dock-layer` rule, which is inert in block layout. Absolute positioning then escapes to the nearest positioned ancestor — the outer `.dock-face` — so the leaving face spans the Back control and the toggle, overhanging its own container by 65px left and 53px right, `visibility: visible` at `opacity: 0` for 260ms. glass-ui carves a special `.is-press-keepalive` rule for exactly this hazard on its OWN layers; this consumer gets no such protection.
defects.reproduction: WebKit 1440×900, open Tools, `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.dock-layer-grid'))` → display block / position static; then read `offsetParent` of the non-`is-active` child → the outer `.dock-face`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the class. A real `<DockLayer>` inside a real `<DockCrossfade>` gets `position: relative` on its host by construction, so the containing block is correct without a consumer-side container at all.

defects.defect: The five-action cluster is optically off-centre in its own band — 6px asymmetry inside a 37.5px pitch — and its end gaps are far tighter than its interior rhythm.
defects.evidence: Measured glyph centres in CSS px from the DPR-2 crop `D2-desktop-light-actions.png`: ← 589.0 | sep 621.5 | 650.0 687.5 725.0 762.5 801.5 | sep 824.0 | T 850.0. Interior pitch 37.5/37.5/37.5/39.0. Separator→first action 28.5; last action→separator 22.5 (6px asymmetry); separator→toggle 26.0; back→separator 32.5. Source: `ActionToolbar.vue:2` `class="flex items-center justify-around flex-1"`. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:5 ("Every element earns its scale, interval, boundary and material from its job relative to the local protagonist").
defects.mechanism: `justify-around` derives interval from leftover space; its half-gap-at-the-ends only balances when items are equal width. Here 24px glyphs sit in variable seats inside a `flex-1` band whose width is set by the OTHER sub-layer and by the dock's fit-content measurement, so the interval is a residue rather than a designed rhythm.
defects.reproduction: WebKit 1440×900, open Tools, screenshot the dock at DPR2 and measure glyph centres; or read each ActionButton's boundingBox and diff adjacent centres against the band's inner edges.
defects.proposedCure: Replace `justify-around` on a stretched band with a fixed token gap (`--dock-layer-gap`, which the producer already sets on `.dock-layer`) and let the band hug its content, so the rhythm is declared rather than left over.

defects.defect: The toggle's focus ring collides with the DockSeparator beside it and reads as a circle on a capsule-shaped dock.
defects.evidence: Figure `D2-toggle-focus-ring.png`. Measured: `matches(':focus-visible') === true`; `box-shadow` a 2px dual ring (`oklab(...) 0px 0px 0px 1.99671px, …`); circumscribed ring ≈47 CSS px around a 40×40 control inside a ~40px inner band; the ring's left arc crosses the separator at x≈824 (the toggle glyph centre is at 850, i.e. 26px away). Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:82 ("Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier").
defects.mechanism: The control has no producer touch-target seat (D-8) and the separator sits flush, so the focus register and the grouping boundary compete for the same pixels; and a circular ring on a control with no circular resting seat is a foreign shape on a pill dock.
defects.reproduction: WebKit 1440×900, open Tools, `document.querySelector('[aria-label="Open color input"]').focus()`, screenshot the dock crop; the ring arc overlaps the vertical separator rule.
defects.proposedCure: Give the toggle the producer's 44px `--dock-touch-target` seat so the ring has room, and give the separator the dock's own gap instead of sitting flush; the ring shape should follow the control's resting capsule.

defects.defect: A consumer speaks the producer's private layer vocabulary: `dock-layer` / `is-active` / `is-leaving` are applied to arbitrary child components, silently inheriting glass-ui's entire internal layer contract including its morph stagger rule.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:91 `class: ["dock-layer", { "is-active": isActive, "is-leaving": leavingSubLayer.value === id }]`. glass-ui `dist/components/dock/styles/layers.css` styles these via the unbounded descendant selector `:where(.glass-dock, .dock-layer-group) .dock-layer`, conferring `display:flex`, `grid-area:1/1`, `min-height: var(--dock-layer-height)`, `white-space:nowrap`, `gap`, the absolute/relative flip, AND `.glass-dock[data-morphing] .dock-layer.is-active > * { opacity: var(--child-reveal); scale: calc(0.82 + 0.18 * var(--child-reveal)) }`. Measured: the ActionToolbar root carries `flex items-center justify-around flex-1 dock-layer is-active` in the live DOM.
defects.mechanism: Private CSS adopted as a public contract. Because this pseudo-layer nests inside the REAL `.dock-face` layer, the five ActionButtons are staggered as children of this fake layer while the whole run is already staggered above — a nested opacity/scale multiplication no one designed. This is also the root of D-12's containing-block bug.
defects.reproduction: HYPOTHESIS for the rendered double-stagger — I confirmed the selector applies and the classes are present in the live DOM, but did not capture a frame mid-`[data-morphing]`. To close: sample child `opacity`/`scale` during a dock expand while the action-bar layer is active.
defects.proposedCure: Stop hand-writing producer classes. `<DockLayer>` faces inside `<DockCrossfade>` get the packaging by construction — the API exists precisely so consumers never touch `.dock-layer`.

defects.defect: Dead public surface: three template refs, one `defineExpose` of three members, one passed prop and one exposed method — all with zero consumers; plus two competing template-ref idioms in 158 lines.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn` across demo/ and e2e/: `colorInputRef` occurs only at ActionBarLayer.vue:28 (decl) and :116 (bind); `actionToolbarRef` only at :29 and :103; `defineExpose({currentToggleIcon, toolbarMode, cycleToolbarMode})` at :96 with `Dock.vue:156` mounting the component with NO ref; `:can-propose-name` passed at :106 while `ActionToolbar.vue:72` declares the prop and never reads it; `clearHover` exposed at `ActionToolbar.vue:91` and never called anywhere. Idiom split: `ref<InstanceType<…>>` at :28–29 vs `useTemplateRef` at :83. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:71 (law 6, "Subtraction precedes explanation"); owner edict 7 (idiomatic Vue 3.5).
defects.mechanism: Handles were wired in anticipation and never connected — `colorInputRef` is exactly the handle D-6 needs, and `clearHover` is exactly the method that would stop a hovered action staying lit after the layer swaps away.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static; verified by exhaustive grep over demo/ and e2e/.
defects.proposedCure: Delete all four unread surfaces, or connect the two that have a job (`colorInputRef.focus()` on the actions→input leg; `actionToolbarRef.clearHover()` on swap-away). Settle on `useTemplateRef` throughout.

defects.defect: `stroke-foreground` breaks the `currentColor` chain that the house forced-colors policy depends on — asymmetrically with the toggle's own siblings.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:138 applies `stroke-foreground` (i.e. `stroke: var(--foreground)`), overriding lucide's `stroke="currentColor"`. `Dock.vue:154` renders the sibling Back arrow as `class="w-6 h-6"` with no stroke class, so it follows `currentColor`. `demo/styles/foundation.css:665–700` documents the two-tier WHCM policy: chrome stays at `forced-color-adjust: auto` "so it is visible + operable" — which works only because icons inherit `color`. Measured under `forcedColors: "active"`: `.toggle-btn` `stroke: "rgb(28, 25, 23)"`, `--toggle-hover-color: "oklch(51.9% 0.208 9.83deg)"` — both author values survive. Figure `D2-forced-colors-emulated.png`.
defects.mechanism: WHCM forces `color` but does not force custom properties or an explicit SVG `stroke`, so this one glyph keeps an author stroke while every sibling in the same dock adopts `ButtonText`.
defects.reproduction: HYPOTHESIS for the paint — Playwright/WebKit emulates the media query without applying a real forced palette, so I proved the mechanism (broken currentColor chain, asymmetric with siblings) but not the rendered black-on-black. To close: open the action bar on a real Windows High Contrast host in a dark forced theme.
defects.proposedCure: Drop `stroke-foreground` and let the glyph inherit `currentColor` like every sibling; if an accent is wanted it belongs on a glass-ui `DockControl` variant that already carries the forced-colors carve-out.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownership direction, public surface, dual paths, modularization
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (exact model ID claude-opus-5[1m], the 1M-context variant) — the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with; declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — ActionButton.vue reaches into glass-ui's dock DI context from a leaf and hand-rolls the producer's `keepDockOpen` protocol WITHOUT its latch or its onScopeDispose teardown, driving a SHARED ref-count it does not own. Measured live: one hover→click→leave cycle logged keepOpen×2 / release×4, every call attributed by stack to ActionButton.vue, with the first call being an unmatched `release`. Because glass-ui's release clamps at Math.max(0, g-1), the extra releases consumed Dock.vue's own action-bar hold: `held` went false and the dock COLLAPSED after 8s while the Tools toggle still read aria-pressed="true" — the dock folds away underneath its own open action bar. Cure is one attribute on the component it already wraps: `<Popover trigger="hover" keep-dock-open>`, deleting the import and both handlers.
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded negative results (checked, no defect found): (a) verbatimModuleSyntax is satisfied — ActionButton.vue:49 uses the inline `type Component` qualifier, GenericActionBar.vue:4 and ActionBarLayer.vue:5,9 use `import type`; (b) Vue 3.5 idioms are correct — reactive props destructure at ActionButton.vue:59, useTemplateRef used properly by neighbours (Dock.vue:74, ActionBarLayer.vue:83), no defineModel stale-read hazard exists here; (c) zero `@src/*` leakage from demo/ (`grep -rn "@src" demo/ --include=*.vue --include=*.ts` returns nothing) — the T.W1 demo-dogfood keystone holds; (d) all imports are relative to physical homes, no revived `@…` project alias — W43 RF-15 holds; (e) ActionButton imports nothing from @mkbabb/value.js, which is correct for chrome; (f) not a god module by size (137 lines) — its defect is misplacement, not bulk.

defects.defect: ActionButton hand-rolls glass-ui's dock keep-open protocol by reaching into `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock`'s DI context from a leaf, without the producer's single-token latch or its onScopeDispose release. The unbalanced acquire/release pair corrupts a shared ref-count owned by GlassDock and steals Dock.vue's own hold, collapsing the dock while its action bar is open.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ActionButton.vue:55 (`import { useOptionalDockContext } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock"`), :81-88 (`dock?.keepOpen()` / `dock?.release()`). Producer already ships the prop: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/popover/Popover.vue.d.ts:16 `/** Hold an ancestor GlassDock open while this surface is visible. */ keepDockOpen?: boolean;` and dockContext.d.ts:14 'Hover-driven dock popovers compose <Popover trigger="hover" keep-dock-open>'. Producer impl with latch+teardown: dist/popover-BQGYXZyO.js:41-47 (`let b=r(),x=!1; function S(){x&&=(b?.release(),!1)} watch([c,()=>n.keepDockOpen],([e,t])=>{e&&t&&b&&!x?(b.keepOpen(),x=!0):(!e||!t)&&S()},{immediate:!0}), onScopeDispose(S)`). Counter that clamps: dist/dock.js:332 `function I(){g.value++,T()}` / :336 `function L(){g.value=Math.max(0,g.value-1),…}`. LIVE MEASUREMENT (Playwright, http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, 1440x900, Tools open, DockContext instrumented with stack capture): after hover -> log=[release <- ActionButton.vue:71, keepOpen <- ActionButton.vue:69], held=true; after click -> +[release,keepOpen] both ActionButton.vue, held=true; after pointer leave -> +[release], held=FALSE while toolsPressed="true"; after 8s -> +[release], dock class = COLLAPSED with toolsPressed="true". Final tally keepOpen x2 / release x4, all four attributed to ActionButton.vue. (Served-SFC lines 69/71 are script-setup offsets for source lines 84/86.)
defects.mechanism: Duplicated ownership of a library-owned ref-counted protocol, implemented without the invariant (one outstanding token per owner) that makes the shared counter safe; plus a cross-boundary DI reach from a leaf component into the design system's dock context.
defects.reproduction: 1) dev server at localhost:9000, viewport 1440x900. 2) navigate #/gradient, wait for settle, hover the dock to expand. 3) click aria-label="Toggle action bar". 4) in the page, walk document.querySelector('.glass-dock').__vueParentComponent.provides[Symbol(glass-ui:dock-context)] and wrap keepOpen/release with counters + new Error().stack. 5) mouse.move onto button.action-button-wrapper[aria-label="Copy CSS"], wait 1.2s -> keepOpen fires. 6) mouse down+up in place, wait 1.8s. 7) mouse.move to (700,820), wait 1.5s -> held becomes false though the action bar is still open. 8) wait 8s -> .glass-dock gains class `collapsed` while aria-pressed="true" on the Tools toggle.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the useOptionalDockContext import and both hold handlers; declare the hold on the component already being wrapped: `<Popover trigger="hover" keep-dock-open :open-delay="300" :close-delay="0">`. The latch and onScopeDispose come from the owner of the counter. Unique semantic ownership restored: the dock hold is glass-ui's.

defects.defect: The action ActionButton fires is a three-hop optional-chained dispatch through `Ref<any>` owned by the shell router, and it is structurally dead on the mobile layout: the mobile <PaneSlot> binds no :on-mount, so all three pane refs stay null. All nine generic dock actions are silent no-ops on phones while the button still plays its 400ms success animation.
defects.evidence: Chain: ActionButton.vue:98 `emit("action")` -> GenericActionBar.vue:28 `@action="act.handler()"` -> demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:196-222 e.g. :208 `handler: () => paneRefs.gradient.value?.reset?.()` -> demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientPane.vue:12 `reset: () => visualizerRef.value?.resetGradient?.()`. Untyped: usePaneRouter.ts:106-110 `generate: Ref<any>; gradient: Ref<any>; mix: Ref<any>`; App.vue:317-319 `ref<any>(null)`; eslint.config.js:70,184 `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: off`. Layout asymmetry: demo/color-picker/App.vue:83-91 (mobile PaneSlot — NO :on-mount) vs :105 `:on-mount="onDesktopLeftMount"` and :131 `:on-mount="onDesktopRightMount"`; App.vue:315 comment 'Populated by the onMount callbacks on the desktop PaneSlots'. LIVE MEASUREMENT at 390x844 on #/gradient reading the App instance setupState: {"innerWidth":390,"innerHeight":844,"mq":false,"isDesktopSetup":false,"gradientPaneRef":"null","dockActionButtons":3}. Confirmation animation fires regardless: ActionButton.vue:92-99 sets isClicked for 400ms unconditionally.
defects.mechanism: Inverted ownership direction — a pane's own verbs are declared in the shell router, keyed by string, and dispatched onto the pane through a layout-specific template-ref capture. The capability becomes a function of which PaneSlot rendered the component, and every hop is an untyped `?.` that silently no-ops.
defects.reproduction: 1) viewport 390x844. 2) navigate http://localhost:9000/#/gradient and reload; wait 5s. 3) evaluate: walk .glass-dock __vueParentComponent up to the App instance, read setupState.gradientPaneRef (unwrapping refs) -> null; matchMedia('(min-width: 1024px) and (min-aspect-ratio: 1.1)').matches -> false; document.querySelectorAll('button.action-button-wrapper').length -> 3. 4) open Tools and click Reset/Copy CSS/Seed — handler evaluates `null?.reset?.()`, nothing happens, no console error, icon still animates.
defects.proposedCure: Invert the dependency: add `demo/shell/dock/dockActions.ts` exporting a typed `DockAction { key, icon, title, description, rotateOnClick?, iconClass?, disabled?, active?, run: () => void }` plus `DOCK_ACTIONS_KEY` and `provideDockActions()`. Each pane calls provideDockActions([...]) in its own setup, closing over its own local functions — fully typed, no refs, no `any`, no `?.`, layout-independent. Delete PaneActionRefs, the three Ref<any>, the 27 lines of handler literals in usePaneRouter, both onDesktop*Mount callbacks in App.vue, and the pure-forwarding defineExpose shims in GeneratePane/GradientPane. The mobile/desktop asymmetry is then inexpressible.

defects.defect: A bare native <button> with a hand-rolled 32x32 box and Tailwind focus ring, inside a <GlassDock> whose every sibling control is glass-ui's <DockControl>. glass-ui 7.0.0 ships both halves of exactly this component — DockControl and DockTrigger for="popover".
defects.evidence: ActionButton.vue:13-20 (native button + focus-visible utilities), :105-116 (scoped `.action-button-wrapper { width: 2rem; height: 2rem; background: none; border: none }`). Producer primitives: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/index.d.ts:8 DockControl, :9 DockTrigger; DockControl.vue.d.ts:3-16 documents glass hover, interruptible spring press, specular gleam, glass-capsule seat, and a >=44px coarse-pointer density clamp on --dock-control-size; dist/dock.js:1225 shows DockTrigger for="popover" rendering the glass PopoverTrigger with dock-trigger classes + press directive. LIVE MEASUREMENT, same dock row, #/gradient, action bar open, 1440x900: Back (dock-icon-button glass-specular-track) = 40x40; Reset / Copy CSS / Seed from palette (action-button-wrapper) = 32x32 each. Screenshot: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-actionbutton/probe-actionbar-open-desktop.png shows one glass-capsule control followed by three unseated naked strokes.
defects.mechanism: Design-system bypass — a demo-local re-implementation of a primitive glass-ui owns, opting out of its token-driven geometry (so the coarse-pointer >=44px clamp never applies) and its whole interaction register.
defects.reproduction: 1) 1440x900, #/gradient, hover dock, click aria-label="Toggle action bar". 2) evaluate over `.dock-face.is-active button`: getBoundingClientRect -> [{Back,40,40,dock-icon-button},{Reset,32,32,action-button-wrapper},{Copy CSS,32,32,...},{Seed from palette,32,32,...}]. 3) screenshot `.glass-dock` — the register mismatch is visible.
defects.proposedCure: Render `<DockTrigger for="popover">` (or `<PopoverTrigger as-child><DockControl …>`) and delete `.action-button-wrapper` plus the local focus-ring utilities entirely. No new glass-ui primitive is needed, so nothing to relay to the glass-ui BH inbox for this.

defects.defect: `activeStyle: Record<string, string>` is an unbounded inline style-bag prop used to express 'this control is active', so the active state reaches only the SVG stroke and never assistive tech — no aria-pressed, no data-active, no role state.
defects.evidence: ActionButton.vue:67 `activeStyle?: Record<string, string> | undefined;` spread inline at :30 `:style="{ ...activeStyle, … }"`. Sole use: ActionToolbar.vue:46 `:active-style="paletteActive ? { stroke: cssColorOpaque, strokeWidth: '2' } : {}"`. Producer alternative: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/DockControl.vue.d.ts:26-31 — `active` stamps aria-pressed + data-active and reads the --dock-control-active-bg tier.
defects.mechanism: Per-instance styling override channel substituting for a first-class component axis; the semantic half of the state is simply lost.
defects.reproduction: NONE (static — read ActionToolbar.vue:46 and inspect the rendered button: it carries no aria-pressed and no data-active in any state; only an inline stroke changes).
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `activeStyle` prop; pass `:active="paletteActive"` to DockControl, which stamps aria-pressed + data-active and styles at the root component level (edict 5).

defects.defect: Two import disciplines for one design system inside one 137-line file: a demo-local alias barrel onto the glass-ui ROOT export beside a direct subpath import. The demo/ui/* layer is 19 pure re-export barrels serving 48 consumers, and the glass-ui ./popover subpath has zero demo users.
defects.evidence: ActionButton.vue:50-54 `import { Popover, PopoverContent, PopoverTrigger } from "../../ui/popover"` vs :55 `import { useOptionalDockContext } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock"`. demo/ui/popover/index.ts is one line re-exporting from the ROOT `@mkbabb/glass-ui`. glass-ui package.json exports './popover' -> dist/popover.js (131 bytes) while the root './' -> dist/glass-ui.js (25,239 bytes, 47 top-level import/export statements). Census: `grep -rl 'from "\(\.\./\)*ui/'` demo -> 48 files; `grep -rl 'from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"'` demo -> 36 files; subpath usage /dock x15, /watercolor-dot x11, /dom x9, /dark x9, /aurora x9, …; `grep -rn '@mkbabb/glass-ui/popover' demo/` -> 0 hits. demo/ui/alert/index.ts even carries a comment recording it was converted from a local implementation to a re-export.
defects.mechanism: An alias/indirection layer (dual path) sitting exactly where owner edict 4 says nothing should sit (demo/ui/), so a single capability has three spellings and one file uses two of them.
defects.reproduction: NONE (static census — the greps above are reproducible verbatim from the repo root).
defects.proposedCure: Delete all 19 demo/ui/* barrels and rewrite the 48 consumers onto the glass-ui subpath that owns each symbol (mechanical, one mapping line per barrel). ActionButton becomes `import { Popover, PopoverContent, PopoverTrigger } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/popover";`. Then encode the rule structurally: an eslint no-restricted-imports ban on the bare `@mkbabb/glass-ui` root specifier under demo/**.

defects.defect: Four live implementations of 'exactly one of a set is open'. ActionButton defines a leaf-owned string-keyed mutex protocol that every parent must re-implement, while a typed mutex composable sits in the same directory, a third implementation lives in demo/palettes, and the design system's own hover-cluster transit is the documented owner.
defects.evidence: (1) ActionButton.vue:59-79 hoverKey/activeHover props + `update:activeHover` emit; parent halves duplicated at ActionToolbar.vue:85 + :13,24,35,48,60 and GenericActionBar.vue:11,29. (2) demo/shell/dock/composables/usePopupMutex.ts — same directory — whose header reads 'usePopupMutex was retired upstream from glass-ui at the D-II tranche. Local fork.' (3) demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHoverPopover.ts:16 `openIndex` singleton + leave timer. (4) glass-ui dist/popover-BQGYXZyO.js:39-47 and dockContext.d.ts:14 'Reka's hover primitives own open/close cadence and cluster transit.'
defects.mechanism: Concept duplication with inverted control — the leaf defines the coordination protocol and exports half of it as props/emits, so every new consumer re-implements the parent half; meanwhile a retired-upstream composable was forked locally rather than replaced.
defects.reproduction: NONE (static — the four sites are cited by file:line).
defects.proposedCure: Delete the ActionButton mutex entirely (hoverKey / activeHover / update:activeHover and both parent halves): `<Popover trigger="hover">` with openDelay/closeDelay already provides per-trigger open state and cluster transit, per the producer's own docblock. If a hard single-open invariant is genuinely required, use usePopupMutex — one mutex in the dock folder, not two.

defects.defect: The demo's structural import-boundary enforcement is dead config: three of its four eslint file globs point at `demo/@/**`, which no longer exists, and the surviving glob bans an `@components/...` alias that W43 also retired. Net zero effective import bans over the current demo tree — including demo/shell/, this component's home.
defects.evidence: eslint.config.js:232-238 globs `demo/color-picker/**`, `demo/@/components/**`, `demo/@/lib/**`; :275-277 globs `demo/@/composables/**`. Measured: `ls -d demo/@` -> 'No such file or directory'. The single live glob demo/color-picker/** (16 files) carries only the ban on `@components/custom/palette-browser/**/*.vue`, and that alias was retired too — vite.config.ts:66-71 'W43 (RF-15) killed the demo `@…` path aliases' and tsconfig.demo.json 'No @styles/@components/@utils/@lib/@composables/@assets project alias survives'.
defects.mechanism: Invariants encoded as file-glob config that the tree moved out from under; the prose survives and reads as enforcement while matching nothing. This is the permissive condition that allows L-1 (leaf -> producer DI reach) and L-2 (shell -> feature verbs) to exist.
defects.reproduction: 1) `ls -d demo/@` -> No such file or directory. 2) `ls demo/@/components` -> No such file or directory. 3) `grep -rn '@components' demo/ --include=*.vue --include=*.ts` -> no import specifiers (alias retired). Therefore no file in the current tree is subject to G-DEMO-1 / G-DEMO-3a / G-DEMO-3b.
defects.proposedCure: Re-key the rules onto the real tree and state the layering explicitly: demo/shell/** may not import demo/{picker,palettes,workbenches,scenes}/**; demo/{shared,platform,color-session}/** may not import demo/{shell,color-picker}/**; demo/** may not import the bare `@mkbabb/glass-ui` root (subpaths only — which retires L-5 structurally).

defects.defect: Five dead members across the component and its consumer: a `label` prop nobody passes rendering a `.action-label` class with no CSS rule anywhere, a `hidden` prop nobody passes that gates the entire template, an unused `canProposeName` prop, and a `clearHover` defineExpose with zero callers.
defects.evidence: ActionButton.vue:65 `label?: string` + :32 `<span v-if="label" class="action-label">` — `grep -rn 'action-label' demo/` returns ONLY that template line (no rule in the scoped block, none in demo/styles/). ActionButton.vue:69 `hidden?: boolean` gating :3 `v-if="!hidden"` — `grep -rn 'hidden' demo/shell/dock/ActionToolbar.vue demo/shell/dock/layers/GenericActionBar.vue` -> no hits. ActionToolbar.vue:72 `canProposeName: boolean` — the only occurrence of that identifier in the file (grep -n canProposeName ActionToolbar.vue -> line 72 only), still threaded in from ActionBarLayer.vue:106. ActionToolbar.vue:87-91 clearHover + defineExpose — `grep -rn 'clearHover' demo/ e2e/` finds only the definition.
defects.mechanism: Accreted public surface never retired; each dead prop is a decision future call sites must reason about for zero behaviour. The `hidden` gate is additionally a second, competing visibility mechanism beside the `v-if="hasAnyActionBar"` the dock already applies at Dock.vue:153.
defects.reproduction: NONE (static — the greps above are reproducible verbatim).
defects.proposedCure: Delete all five. Visibility is the dock layer's decision, not a leaf prop; a label variant, if ever wanted, is DockControl shape="tab".

defects.defect: Two CSS custom properties carrying one identical value, written inline on every icon render, fed by a four-hop prop drill of a colour that is already available by injection at the leaf.
defects.evidence: ActionButton.vue:30 `:style="{ ...activeStyle, '--flash-color': cssColorOpaque ?? 'currentColor', '--hover-color': cssColorOpaque ?? 'currentColor' }"` — the same expression twice. Drill path: ActionBarLayer.vue:24 `inject(SAFE_ACCENT_KEY)` -> :105 prop cssColorOpaque -> ActionToolbar.vue:71 prop -> :10,22,33,45,58 -> ActionButton.vue:70. SAFE_ACCENT_KEY is directly injectable (demo/color-session/keys.ts; injected at Dock.vue:35 and by several panes).
defects.mechanism: Per-instance inline styling override (edict 5) plus a redundant token pair, with the accent prop-drilled past an injection seam that already reaches the leaf.
defects.reproduction: NONE (static — read ActionButton.vue:30).
defects.proposedCure: One token set once at the action-bar root — `.dock-action-bar { --action-ink: <accent> }` — consumed by the scoped rules. The leaf then carries no colour prop at all.

defects.defect: 400ms setTimeout in handleClick with no unmount/scope-dispose cancellation, in a component that is routinely unmounted by layer and route changes.
defects.evidence: ActionButton.vue:95-97 `setTimeout(() => { isClicked.value = false; }, 400)` with no onUnmounted/onScopeDispose. Contrast the correct pattern in the same folder: demo/shell/dock/composables/usePopupMutex.ts:80 `onUnmounted(clearSwapTimer)`.
defects.mechanism: Missing teardown — the same class of omission that makes L-1 unsafe (no lifecycle-bound cleanup on an effect the component starts).
defects.reproduction: NONE (hypothesis for observable harm: the callback writes to a disposed ref if the component unmounts inside the 400ms window — e.g. clicking an action that switches views. No user-visible symptom measured.)
defects.proposedCure: Dissolves entirely once the flash becomes a DockControl press/active state owned by the design system; if kept, bind the timer to the scope.

defects.defect: The demo's declared value.js type surface has drifted from package.json#exports: the tsconfig paths list three keys the exports map does not contain (a bare root plus `parsing` and `units`) and omits two it does (`value`, `css`). The 10 demo imports of `@mkbabb/value.js/css` therefore typecheck against the registry-installed 4.0.0 tarball in node_modules while Vite runs them against this checkout's local dist — and the two artifacts already differ byte-for-byte.
defects.evidence: package.json exports = ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize (no '.' root). tsconfig.demo.json paths = '@mkbabb/value.js' -> ./dist/index.d.ts (which does not exist: `ls dist/index.d.ts` -> No such file), color, parsing (phantom), math, easing, units (phantom), transform, quantize — `value` and `css` absent. Demo usage: `grep -rho '@mkbabb/value.js[a-z/.]*' demo/` -> color x25, css x10, math x6, easing x5, quantize x4. Self-install present: node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js @ 4.0.0, package-lock.json:1336-1339 `resolved: https://registry.npmjs.org/@mkbabb/value.js/-/value.js-4.0.0.tgz`. Divergence measured: `ls -l dist/subpaths/css.js node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.js` -> 43973 B (Jul 27 11:52, local build) vs 43972 B (Jul 17 21:10, registry); `cmp` -> 'differ: char 141, line 2'.
defects.mechanism: Two hand-maintained descriptions of one public surface: vite.config.ts GENERATES its self-alias from package.json#exports (and says so), while tsconfig.demo.json's paths were hand-written and drifted — so the type-resolution and runtime-resolution halves point at different artifacts for the uncovered subpaths.
defects.reproduction: 1) `node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./package.json').exports))"` -> 7 keys, no '.'. 2) read tsconfig.demo.json paths -> 8 keys including phantom `parsing`/`units` and a root '.' mapping to the nonexistent dist/index.d.ts. 3) `cmp dist/subpaths/css.js node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.js` -> differ at char 141. Note: the SUBJECT component imports no value.js at all, which is correct; this is its neighbourhood, recorded because CHALLENGE-L asks the published-surface question.
defects.proposedCure: Single-source the TypeScript half the same way the Vite half already is: generate tsconfig.demo.json's `paths` from package.json#exports (or drop `paths` entirely and let both halves resolve through the one exports map). Then the phantom `parsing`/`units` keys and the nonexistent root mapping cannot exist, and no demo import can typecheck against a different build than it executes.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M context) — the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with; declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-01 — under prefers-reduced-motion the T-29 clip release never returns after one route round-trip, so the hover amputation the component exists to cure becomes permanent; the SFC's own written PRM premise (":29-30") is measurably false because glass-ui's a11y-overrides.css REPLACES transition-property rather than shortening it, deleting the grid-template-columns transitionend the settle stamp depends on.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Sound sub-areas checked and recorded in §4 of the report: verbatimModuleSyntax clean (`:3` `import type { Component } from "vue"` is the only type-only import); Vue 3.5 reactive props destructure idiomatic with a correct `watch(() => visible)` getter (`:38,:53`); no god module (159 lines, one concern, the W6-8 lift out of Dock.vue was correct); no new shared/ dir or wrapper; no animations deleted (no @keyframes in the file); the T-29 clip release and the S.W7-6 boot-flicker suppression BOTH measurably work on the non-PRM path (boot and re-arrival reach `is-settled`/`overflow: visible`, hover capsule renders whole); aria-label present on every viewport; overflowX 0 on all 60 Safari captures; 0 page errors across all nine live probe matrices.

defects.defect: Under prefers-reduced-motion the three-state settle machine's third state (.is-settled → overflow: visible) is unreachable after the first route round-trip, permanently restoring the hover-capsule amputation the component was built to cure.
defects.evidence: abt-probe2.mjs → prmRoundTrip (Chromium reducedMotion:"reduce", 1440x900): boot slotCls="…is-visible is-live is-settled" overflow=visible; browse slotCls="…is-live" overflow=hidden; gradient RE-ARRIVAL slotCls="…is-visible is-live" overflow=hidden; 2nd re-arrival identical. Same script WITHOUT PRM (normalRoundTrip) re-arrives at is-settled/overflow:visible. Hover in the broken state: tools rect x631.5 w115.0 h35.2 vs inner clip x619.8 w125.5 h32.0 → overflow right 1.23px, top 1.60px, bottom 1.60px CUT (abt-prm-rearrival-hover.png). Cause: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/utilities/a11y-overrides.css:1 `*:not([data-allow-motion]) { transition-property: opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow !important; }` — measured computed slot transition-property under PRM = "opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow" (no grid-template-columns).
defects.mechanism: State restored only by a transitionend keyed to a property name (ActionBarToggle.vue:70) that a producer stylesheet is free to remove, combined with a permanent early-return in the watch (ActionBarToggle.vue:59 `if (slotLive.value) return;`) that makes the re-arm dead after first arrival. The file's documented premise at :29-30 ("the global guard shortens transitions to 0.01ms, never removes them") describes demo/styles/animations.css:184-192 and is false of glass-ui's own guard.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../abt-probe2.mjs (colocated) — chromium.newContext({reducedMotion:"reduce"}); goto /#/gradient, wait 2.5s; goto /#/browse, wait 2s; goto /#/gradient, wait 2.5s; read className + getComputedStyle(.action-bar-toggle-inner).overflow. Then hover the Tools control and compare its rect to .action-bar-toggle-inner's.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the three-state machine entirely. The clip exists only to hide content during a WIDTH animation; a layout-animated width on a dock control is itself the defect. Replace 0fr↔1fr + overflow bookkeeping with a fixed-basis box that fades and scaleX's — compositor-only, needs no clip, cannot amputate, and is the 'one producer-owned glass-ui spring register' VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6 already mandates. slotLive, settled, onSlotSettled, .is-live, .is-settled and the double-rAF all die together.

defects.defect: The Tools label fails WCAG AA 1.4.3 in BOTH schemes, and the cause is two per-instance inline colour overrides on a producer control's children (owner edict 5).
defects.evidence: Two independent methods, agreement 0.01. Pixel: crop the label's own rect from the live 2x render, decode PNG to RGBA, 2nd/98th luminance percentile → light ink 0.0895 / paper 0.5131 = 4.04:1; dark 0.1741/0.8742 = 4.12:1; neutral sibling `Gradient` (same Fraunces 16.4px w400) = 7.97:1. Analytic: oklch(0.471189 0.188448 9.83402) → sRGB rgb(170,0,67), relLum 0.0892, vs paper 0.5131 = 4.05:1. Text is 16.4px w400 → normal text, threshold 4.5:1. Source: ActionBarToggle.vue:95-96 `:style="{ color: accent }"` on both the icon and the label span. Producer's --dock-active-color (light-dark(hsl(24 10% 10%), hsl(30 14% 90%))) is measurably neutralised: in the pressed state the BUTTON takes rgb(28,25,23) while icon and label still read oklch(0.471189 0.188448 9.83402).
defects.mechanism: Per-instance ink override on producer children instead of root-level styling; the seed tint is applied to a RESTING, unpressed navigation control, which VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2 restricts to ambient field / active accent / WatercolorDot / the two `Palettes` coordinates.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../abt-probe.mjs (colocated) matrices A (light) and J (dark) — clip-screenshot the label rect, decode, quantile; cross-check by converting the computed oklch to sRGB and computing WCAG contrast against the measured paper luminance.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both :style bindings and the `accent` prop. Dock chrome is neutral ink; the seed lives in the ambient field and the wax seal per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7. Dock.vue:188's `:accent="genericBar?.accentColor ?? safeAccent"` and DockActionBar.accentColor (usePaneRouter.ts:55, never set by any of the three call sites) go with it — a three-file subtraction for zero behaviour change.

defects.defect: T-36's 'true-button box-model' has never applied: --dock-compact-control-padding is structurally outranked by a two-class producer rule, so the control renders 32px where the file asserts 2.5rem = 40px.
defects.evidence: Measured (abt-probe2.json → normalRoundTrip): var on element = "0.5rem 0.75rem", computed padding = "4px", height = 32px. Counterfactual on the same live element: setting --dock-compact-control-padding:20px 30px INLINE changes padding by 0px; forcing element.style.padding="0.5rem 0.75rem" yields padding 8px 12px, height 40.0px, width 120.5px — exactly the comment's 2.5rem. Root cause from CDP CSS.getMatchedStylesForNode (abt-pad3.mjs): `.dock-icon-button--compact` (0,1,0) `padding: var(--dock-compact-control-padding, 0.25rem)` vs `.glass-dock .dock-icon-button` (0,2,0) `padding: var(--dock-icon-padding, var(--dock-control-safe-inset, 0))`; --dock-control-safe-inset = calc(var(--dock-control-size) * 0.1) = 40px*0.1 = 4px.
defects.mechanism: The consumer re-derived a producer box model through a token hook that is unreachable inside a .glass-dock. The comment at :150 promises 'never a specificity fight' — it is exactly the fight it silently lost since T.W6. NOTE: this corrects the sibling shell-dock-dock seat's D2-09, which read the same 32px and concluded 'the comment has been 8px wrong'; the number is right, the mechanism is dead.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../abt-pad3.mjs (colocated) — CDP DOM.querySelector '[aria-label="Toggle action bar"]' + CSS.getMatchedStylesForNode, filter cssProperties for padding; then in-page set the custom property inline and re-read getComputedStyle(t).padding.
defects.proposedCure: Stop re-deriving. Use DockControl shape="tab" — .dock-tab-button already ships padding-inline 0.75rem / padding-block 0.375rem, i.e. the exact scale T-36 re-derived, at a specificity the dock rule does not outrank. Delete `compact`, `dock-tools-btn`, --dock-compact-control-padding, margin-inline and gap.

defects.defect: The component hand-rolls a control glass-ui already ships: DockControl shape="tab" is an auto-sized text-tab, and the `active` prop stamps aria-pressed AND data-active from one binding. The component uses shape="icon"+compact and writes three attributes by hand, landing on the wrong active tier.
defects.evidence: glass-ui@7.0.0 dist/components/dock/DockControl.vue.d.ts verbatim: 'shape="tab" — auto-sized text-tab control with the de-red'd glass hover register'; 'active — Selected/toggled state. Stamps aria-pressed + data-active'. ActionBarToggle.vue:86-94 passes `compact` + manual :class={'is-active'} + manual :aria-pressed, and NO :active. Measured pressed background color(srgb 0.994 0.96 0.926 / 0.8) == --dock-active-bg (the .is-active branch), never --dock-control-active-bg (the [data-active] 'selected reads as glass' tier). Hover consequence: Tools is the ONLY label-bearing dock control that inflates — rest 104.5x32 → hover 115.0x35.2, scale 1.1 (icon-button register); .dock-tab-button and .dock-select-trigger carry no hover scale, and Login/@mbabb/Select view measurably do not grow.
defects.mechanism: Reaching past the design system to re-derive a primitive it already provides (edict 4), then per-instance-overriding the root (edict 5), then shipping two spellings of one state (edict 2) and a hand-fitted box (edict 3).
defects.reproduction: Read node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/DockControl.vue.d.ts and .../styles/controls/tab-button.css; compare with ActionBarToggle.vue:86-104. Hover delta: abt-probe.mjs matrix A, rest vs hover toolsBox.
defects.proposedCure: <DockControl shape="tab" :active="active" aria-label="Toggle action bar"> — one prop replaces the class, the aria attribute and the dead token, and restores the producer's intended selected-glass tier.

defects.defect: The pressed state has zero rendered pixels and is pruned from the accessibility tree — a toggle whose 'on' is unobservable in both channels.
defects.evidence: Dock.vue:113 sets activeLayer='action-bar' exactly when actionBarLayerActive is true; glass-ui layers.css gives the non-active layer opacity:0; visibility:hidden; pointer-events:none — and the main layer hosts ActionBarToggle. Measured after clicking Tools (abt-probe-cr.json → A….active): ariaPressed="true", cls contains "is-active", and the live nav ariaSnapshot contains only Back / Reset / Copy CSS / Seed from palette — pressedInAx=false. Geometry corollary: while 'pressed' the control's rect is x790.6 w104.5 while the dock pill is x627.5 w185.0 (82.6px outside its own dock); dock rest x473.7 w492.6 → active x627.5 w185.0 = dx +153.8px, dw -307.6px, unanimated.
defects.mechanism: The only state in which the control reads 'on' is a state in which the control is not rendered. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 requires explicit role/name/state; §3 law 4 forbids the dock's state changes moving the scene.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../abt-probe.mjs matrix A — after page.click('[aria-label="Toggle action bar"]'), re-read the element's attributes and page.locator('nav').first().ariaSnapshot().
defects.proposedCure: Either the toggle survives into the action-bar layer as the pressed seat that returns you (deleting the redundant `Back` at Dock.vue:154 and the whole two-arrow motif), or it drops aria-pressed and becomes what it behaves like — a one-way aria-expanded/aria-controls disclosure. Parent-seat ruling.

defects.defect: On eleven of fifteen routes the control is a named ghost: 0 painted pixels, a full accessible name in the AT tree, and programmatically focusable.
defects.evidence: /#/browse (abt-probe-cr.json → E-desktop-browse-absent): toolsPresent=true, toolsBox={w:104.5,h:32}, slot grid-template-columns="0px" opacity="0", inner overflow="hidden", tabindex="-1", clickable={hitIsSelf:false, focusable:TRUE}. Live nav ariaSnapshot on that route contains: `- button "Toggle action bar": - img - text: Tools - img`. Routes where visible is true: /#/generate, /#/gradient, /#/mix (usePaneRouter.ts:191,203,215) and /#/ (ColorPicker.vue:315) — the other 11 of 15 render the ghost.
defects.mechanism: 'Absent' was implemented as 'still mounted, just transparent and clipped'. opacity:0 + a 0px grid column removes it from sight and tab order but not from the accessibility tree, and element.focus() still succeeds — so any focus-restoration path can park focus on an invisible control (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.1).
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../abt-probe.mjs matrix E — goto /#/browse, then page.locator('nav').first().ariaSnapshot() and in-page t.focus(); document.activeElement===t.
defects.proposedCure: Absence is v-if. Dock.vue:182 already computes hasAnyActionBar and passes it down as a styling prop instead of using it as a mount condition. With D-01's transform-based presence nothing requires the element to stay mounted.

defects.defect: The visible label is keyed to viewport width, so 200% zoom and every phone reduce the control to an unlabelled tinted glyph; and `compact` opts the control out of the producer's coarse-pointer 44px target floor.
defects.evidence: Measured: desktop 1440 → 104.5x32, label "Tools", arrow 12x12, separator 1x27.5. 200% zoom (720 CSS px @2dpr) → 32x32, toolsLabelText=null, arrow 0x0, separator display:none. Mobile 390 → 33.3x33.3, label null, arrow 0x0. Confirmed visually in shots/zoom-200-desktop/gradient.png: the dock reads [rainbow ⌄] [bare magenta brush] [Gradient|Palettes] [⋮]. Producer floor: glass-ui/.../controls/touch-floor.css `@media (pointer: coarse) { .dock-icon-button:not(.dock-icon-button--compact):not(:where(.glass-dock *)) { min-block-size: var(--dock-touch-target, 2.75rem) …` — --compact is EXPLICITLY excluded; DockControl's own typing promises 'the HIT CELL stays the full --dock-control-size (≥44px on coarse)'. Measured 33.3x33.3 = 57% of 44x44 area. REPORT.json's smallTapTargets threshold is sub-24px so it passes silently on all four mobile rows.
defects.mechanism: A breakpoint fork (isDesktop = min-width:1024px, Dock.vue:71) used as a content gate rather than container-scaled layout, plus opting into a producer variant whose defined semantics include forfeiting the coarse-pointer floor.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../abt-probe.mjs matrices F (720x450 @2dpr) and I (390x844, isMobile, hasTouch) — read toolsBox, toolsLabelText, toolsSvgBoxes, seps.
defects.proposedCure: shape="tab" is auto-sized and label-bearing at every width — drop the isDesktop prop entirely and let the label live or wrap by container query. If the label genuinely cannot fit at 312px of dock aperture, the icon-only fallback must supply a visible boundary and meet the coarse floor, which shape="icon" WITHOUT compact does for free.

defects.defect: The focus indicator is a 1.65:1 hairline coloured by the user's own live seed, with outline-style: none; and in forced-colors the control has no boundary at all.
defects.evidence: Clean keyboard focus, mouse parked at (20,700) (abt-probe2.json → focus): matchesFV=true, outlineStyle="none" (outlineWidth 3px declared then killed by .dock-icon-button{outline:none}), boxShadow = color(srgb 0.665504 0.000101 0.261748 / 0.3) 0 0 0 2px + /0.15 0 0 8px. Composited over the measured dock paper L 0.5131 that ring is 1.65:1 — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 requires ≥3:1. abt-focus.png shows a faint pink whisper at 2x DPR. Forced-colors (Chromium forcedColors:"active", abt-probe-cr.json → G.rest): background-color rgba(255,255,255,0), box-shadow none, no border — bare text, while Login/@mbabb (Button primitives) retain theirs. Coverage note: shots/forced-colors-desktop/*.png were captured on WebKit which ignores forcedColors emulation and are NOT forced-colors witnesses.
defects.mechanism: Producer control whose focus affordance is a low-alpha shadow rather than an outline, tinted from the live seed so its contrast is a function of whatever colour the user happens to be editing — an unguarded, user-variable focus indicator.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../abt-probe2.mjs — page.mouse.move(20,700); blur; Tab x2; read getComputedStyle(document.activeElement).{outlineStyle,boxShadow}; composite the ring colour at its alpha over the measured paper luminance and compute WCAG contrast.
defects.proposedCure: Producer-owned focus ring at the root (shape="tab" inherits .dock-tab-button's), never seed-derived; ≥3:1 against the dock in both schemes and a non-colour delta under forced colors.

defects.defect: Type-jurisdiction violation: the control label is Fraunces (display family) at 16.4px, identical in family, size and weight to the route protagonist beside it — the hierarchy is inverted.
defects.evidence: ActionBarToggle.vue:96 `class="text-small font-display"`; measured toolsLabelCS = {font-family: 'Fraunces, "Fraunces Fallback", serif', font-size: "16.4px", font-weight: "400"}. Sibling `Select view` label "Gradient" measures identically (abt-probe2.json → siblings). --type-small resolves to clamp(0.875rem, 0.8rem + 0.25vw, 1.25rem) = 16.4px at 1440 — 'small' is body size here. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4: 'control or label, including dropdown options → text-small → Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold'; 'Fraunces owns display/identity'. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 13 restates it.
defects.mechanism: A secondary layer toggle takes the protagonist's typographic rung and then adds the only saturated hue in the band on top of it (PROPORTION-AUDIT §1: scale is earned relative to the local protagonist).
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../abt-probe2.mjs → siblings: read fontFamily/fontSize/fontWeight of the first text span inside [aria-label="Select view"] and [aria-label="Toggle action bar"].
defects.proposedCure: Plus Jakarta Sans at a genuine text-small rung, one adjacent golden step below the route identity; shape="tab" supplies font-size: var(--type-small) and color: var(--muted-foreground) at the root.

defects.defect: Three glyph rungs in the dock, two of them inside this one control at a non-golden 2:1 ratio, both per-instance overrides of the producer token.
defects.evidence: Measured glyph boxes: Tools icon 24x24 (`w-6 h-6`, ActionBarToggle.vue:95), Tools arrow 12x12 (`w-3 h-3`, :103), Dock.vue:143 Check 20x20 (`w-5 h-5`). Producer rung --dock-icon-glyph = max(calc(2.5rem*0.5),1rem) = 20px, applied by `.dock-icon-button > svg` in @layer components and beaten by the Tailwind utilities. 24:12 = 2:1; adjacent phi rungs off 24 are 14.8 or 38.8.
defects.mechanism: Per-instance override of a producer glyph token (edict 5) plus a non-adjacent-rung interval inside a single control (PROPORTION-AUDIT §1).
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../abt-probe.mjs matrix A → rest.toolsSvgBoxes = [{w:24,h:24},{w:12,h:12}]; tokens['--dock-icon-glyph'].
defects.proposedCure: Delete w-6 h-6 and w-3 h-3; consume --dock-icon-glyph. Honest note: DockViewSelect also renders 24px, so the 20→24 override is a dock-wide habit and belongs to the parent seat; the 12px arrow is this component's alone and dies with D-11.

defects.defect: A one-way ArrowRight affordance on a two-way aria-pressed toggle, pointing at motion that does not occur and pointing the wrong way in RTL.
defects.evidence: ActionBarToggle.vue:99-103 justifies ArrowRight as the layer-swap affordance mirroring the action-bar ArrowLeft. The control is aria-pressed (a toggle): pressing again is how you return. Measured motion on toggle: dock x473.7 w492.6 → x627.5 w185.0 — nothing moves right; the pill collapses inward 307.6px. RTL: shots/rtl-desktop/{gradient,picker}.png — items mirror, glyphs do not, so the arrow points away from its content. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1: 'chrome, navigation and layout → logical inline/block direction follows the document.'
defects.mechanism: A directional navigation register applied to a reversible state. The producer's dock-select-trigger__chevron (rotate 180deg on [data-state=open]) is the correct register for a state that reverses.
defects.reproduction: Read shots/rtl-desktop/gradient.png; and abt-probe.mjs matrix A rest.dockBox vs active.dockBox for the actual geometry delta.
defects.proposedCure: Remove the arrow. A named, plated tab with a producer `active` seat needs no directional ornament — PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 6, 'Subtraction precedes explanation'. (Corroborates sibling seat D2-07; the toggle-semantics and no-rightward-motion halves are new.)

defects.defect: The folded separator is one of three dividers for four seats in a row where two seats already draw their own capsule; and the control's own material tier is neither of the two tiers beside it.
defects.evidence: ActionBarToggle.vue:82 `<DockSeparator class="hidden lg:block" />`. Measured visible separators in the main layer at 1440: x = 625.8 (this component's), 757.3, 864.8 — one between every adjacent pair, the maximum possible duplication.
