Frame samples arm A: t=30ms trackW=0px clipW=0 paintW=104.5 spill=121.5px; t=209ms trackW=93.3 spill=29.0px. This violates the component's own header invariant at lines 30-31 ('the stamp drops the moment presence drops') and lines 137-142 ('the clip returns ... during any width transition').
defects.mechanism: A settle LATCH written from two independent deferred writers (a 2-frame-old rAF and a transitionend), neither of which re-validates the predicate it depends on, instead of a settle DERIVATION from state that is already in the DOM.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-actionbartoggle/probe/C2-stale-settle-repro.mjs webkit (and chromium) — 6 fresh loads of http://localhost:9000/#/browse each, 6/6 stale on both. Harm A/B: node probe/C2-ab-control.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `settled` as an independently-written latch and let CSS own the clip release from state already in the DOM (`is-visible` + not-animating), which removes both writers and the whole race class. If the ref must stay: keep one `armFrame` id, `cancelAnimationFrame(armFrame)` on every watcher entry and in `onScopeDispose`, and guard the inner callback with `if (!visible) return;` before stamping.

defects.defect: `aria-pressed` and `.is-active` are set only while the button sits under `aria-hidden="true"` + `inert` + `opacity: 0`, so the toggle's state is unobservable to both AT and sighted users; activation also destroys focus with no restoration and no live announcement.
defects.evidence: ActionBarToggle.vue:89 (`:class="{ 'is-active': active }"`) and :91 (`:aria-pressed="active"`). `active === true` is exactly the condition under which DockLayerGroup swaps the main layer out. Measured at the instant aria-pressed is "true": {btnAriaPressed:"true", btnClass:"... dock-tools-btn is-active", btnCS:{background-color:"color(srgb 0.994 0.96 0.926 / 0.8)", pointer-events:"none"}, hiddenAncestor:"dock-face"} with that face carrying inert + aria-hidden="true". Producer CSS node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/crossfade.css: `.dock-face { opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; }` and `.dock-face.is-leaving { opacity: calc(1 - var(--dock-t)); }` — the active register paints only during the ~300ms exit crossfade. Focus trace: B_tab_reached_tools → BUTTON.dock-tools-btn; B_after_enter_activeEl → DIV.dock-face is-active (unnamed, roleless, text "lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)"); B_after_back_activeEl → DIV.dock-face is-active (text "HomeToolsPickerAbout Login  @mbabb"). Focus is never returned to the trigger and no aria-live announces the swap.
defects.mechanism: A `role=button` + `aria-pressed` toggle pattern applied to what is structurally a disclosure that swaps a region — and hand-rolled in the consumer instead of using glass-ui DockControl's own `active` prop, which already emits aria-pressed + data-active + the glass-capsule register.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/, expand the dock, Tab to `.dock-tools-btn`, press Enter; read `document.activeElement` and the button's `closest('[aria-hidden="true"]')`. Captured in probe-abt steps B_tab_reached_tools / B_after_enter_snap / B_after_enter_activeEl / B_after_back_activeEl.
defects.proposedCure: Speak the producer's API (edict 4): pass `:active` to DockControl and delete the hand-rolled class + aria-pressed. Re-shape the ARIA to the real behaviour — `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls` pointing at the action-bar layer — and add a focus contract: move focus to the action-bar layer's Back control on open, restore it to the Tools trigger on close.

defects.defect: Two sources of truth for one breakpoint, one of them a form this repo has already ruled dead.
defects.evidence: ActionBarToggle.vue:82 (`<DockSeparator class="hidden lg:block" />`) and :103 (`<ArrowRight ... hidden lg:block />`) gate on the Tailwind width utility while :96 (`<span v-if="isDesktop">`) gates on the injected prop, which is `useMediaQuery("(min-width: 1024px)")` at Dock.vue:71. demo/color-picker/App.vue:66-70 rules: "MOB-1 (T round-4) SUPERSEDES the width-only lg:* display witnesses with the .app-layout [data-layout] stamp (the single isDesktop truth); the D6-03 exception + D8-1 note die".
defects.mechanism: A ruled-superseded mechanism surviving alongside its replacement inside one component that already receives the ruled truth as a prop; they diverge under any container-vs-viewport mismatch or forced layout.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static, but the ruling is cited verbatim and both call sites are line-identified.
defects.proposedCure: `v-if="isDesktop"` on both the separator and the arrow; delete `hidden lg:block`. One breakpoint truth, the one the repo ruled.

defects.defect: The double-rAF chain has no returned id, no cancelAnimationFrame, and no scope teardown, so superseded chains still run and still write, and writes can land after unmount.
defects.evidence: ActionBarToggle.vue:60-65 — bare `requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(() => {...}))`, no `onScopeDispose`/`onUnmounted` anywhere in the SFC. The `slotLive` guard at :59 is checked at SCHEDULE time only, never at RUN time, so rapid flapping schedules multiple chains that all fire.
defects.mechanism: Unowned deferred write — the local shape of the constellation-wide PRM-RAF family. It is not a per-frame loop (no rAF re-entry, so no ongoing frame cost), but it is the enabling condition for C-3.
defects.reproduction: NONE as an isolated symptom — its observable consequence is C-3, reproduced 12/12.
defects.proposedCure: One `armFrame` id, `cancelAnimationFrame(armFrame)` at the top of every watcher invocation and in `onScopeDispose`, plus the `if (!visible) return;` re-check inside the inner callback (same patch as C-3).

defects.defect: Per-instance styling of a design-system control's box model, plus a doubled inline colour binding for one inherited property.
defects.evidence: ActionBarToggle.vue:154-158 `.dock-tools-btn { --dock-compact-control-padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; margin-inline: 0.25rem; gap: 0.5em; }` — the mechanism (a producer token hook) is honest but the placement is a consumer overriding one instance of a design-system control (edicts 4 + 5). ActionBarToggle.vue:95 and :96 bind `:style="{ color: accent }"` twice, once on the icon and once on the label span, for a single inherited property. Measured consequence: the trigger renders 32×32 CSS px at 390px viewport vs 44×44 for the non-compact dock controls (`Back`, `Save edit`) in the same run — clears WCAG 2.5.8 AA (24px), fails 2.5.5 AAA (44px). Recorded not charged: glass-ui's own coarse-pointer floor (dist/components/dock/styles/controls/touch-floor.css) excludes EVERY control inside `.glass-dock` via `:not(:where(.glass-dock *))`, so the 44px question is producer-wide.
defects.mechanism: Design-system variance expressed at the consumption site rather than in the design system.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-actionbartoggle/probe/C3-route-census.mjs (mobile-390 leg) reports w/h 32×32 for `.dock-tools-btn`; the sibling comparison came from the same probe run at isMobile viewport (Back / Save edit at 44 unscaled).
defects.proposedCure: Move the box-model step-up into glass-ui as a DockControl shape/size variant and relay it to the active glass-ui BH inbox per the standing relay edict. Set `color` once on the control root (or one `--dock-tools-accent` custom property on `.dock-tools-btn`) and let the icon and label inherit — one binding instead of two.

defects.defect: Vacuous gate: five named mutations keep the entire test suite green, the component's stated raison d'être (the S.W7-6 boot-flicker cure) has no test at all, there is no unit test, and the suite demonstrably steers around the condition that produces C-1.
defects.evidence: e2e/smoke/oracles/o15-dock-register.spec.ts is the only spec inspecting this component; all four Tools cases `page.goto("/")` — the one route where `visible` is true at boot. It asserts only: is-visible/is-settled present (L75-76), inner overflow visible (L78), non-none box-shadow under keyboard focus (L100), padding/margin/gap (L126-129), zero [title] (L141/146), one separator (L163-165). Green-keeping mutations: M1 delete `:tabindex` (L92) — no spec reads tabindex, C-1/C-2 get worse and nothing fails; M2 `settled.value = visible` → `= true` (L71); M3 delete the departure reset (L55-58); M4 delete `slotLive` and hardcode `is-live` — the boot-flicker cure vanishes untested; M5 delete `:class="{ 'is-active': active }"` (L89). And e2e/smoke/oracles/o10d-display-voice-census.spec.ts:339-350 navigates to Home FIRST with the comment "on HOME, where the picker action bar lives (the toggle is view-dependent)" before clicking Toggle action bar — the suite steers around C-1 rather than asserting against it. No unit test: vitest.config.ts:21 includes `test/**/*.ts` and `demo/test/**/*.ts`; `grep -rn 'ActionBarToggle|dock-tools-btn|action-bar-toggle' test/ demo/test/ | wc -l` → 0.
defects.mechanism: Oracles written against the single happy route and the single happy state, asserting attribute PRESENCE rather than the state machine's transitions or its negative cases.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'ActionBarToggle|dock-tools-btn|action-bar-toggle' test/ demo/test/ → 0 hits. Read e2e/smoke/oracles/o15-dock-register.spec.ts:62-167 (all four Tools cases start `page.goto("/")`).
defects.proposedCure: One negative oracle on a no-action-bar route: `await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Toggle action bar' })).toHaveCount(0)` on /#/browse. It fails today and passes the moment `:inert="!visible"` lands, closing C-1 and C-2 with a single assertion. Add a mid-transition assertion that inner `overflow` is `hidden` while `grid-template-columns` is animating, which is the only gate that would have caught C-3.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) under demo/shell/dock/DockStatusLamp.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m]; the tier explicitly declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — DockStatusLamp/status-lamp.ts and demo/palettes/browser/status/ApiOfflineChip.vue are one concept implemented twice (byte-identical labels and roles, 11-of-13 byte-identical CSS declarations, twin keyframes under two names), and the duplication is STRUCTURALLY FORCED: the pure resolver was homed in the consumer's directory (demo/shell/dock/status-lamp.ts) instead of beside the state it resolves (demo/platform/transport/availability.ts), so the second seat cannot reuse it without an illegal palettes→shell lateral edge.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded as verified-clean sub-axes: (1) NO deep src/ reach and NO library import — DockStatusLamp.vue imports only vue, ../../platform/transport/useApiClient, ./status-lamp; its full transitive cone (useApiClient.ts → client.ts, availability.ts → api-problem.ts) imports only vue and its own siblings; zero @src/*, zero @mkbabb/value.js at any depth, so the T.W1 demo-dogfood keystone holds for this component. (2) verbatimModuleSyntax satisfied — the one type-only import, status-lamp.ts:31 `import type { ApiAvailability }`, is correctly typed. (3) No god module — 123 lines of which 88 are CSS and 11 comment; script block is 8 lines; status-lamp.ts is one pure total function. (4) Animations preserved — lamp-dot-pulse is a component-scoped keyframe (edict 6 permits) with a correct prefers-reduced-motion guard; every proposed cure moves it, never deletes it. (5) Idiomatic Vue 3.5 — computed over an injected Ref is the right shape; nothing needs useTemplateRef/shallowRef. (6) No back-compat shim/alias/migration path; the dead DevMisconfigBanner was genuinely deleted with a working negative watch at o22-status-lamp.spec.ts:37. (7) Visual audit: 0 blankOrNearBlank / 0 pageErrors / 0 horizontalOverflow / 0 darkClassMissing across all 60 captures; the single consoleError is the blob WebGL context loss, unrelated.

defects.defect: One concept, two homes: DockStatusLamp.vue + status-lamp.ts and ApiOfflineChip.vue are the same component written twice. The pure resolver is homed in the consumer's feature directory rather than beside the transport state it resolves, which forces the duplication.
defects.evidence: Labels byte-identical: demo/shell/dock/status-lamp.ts:54 `label: "dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`"` vs demo/palettes/browser/status/ApiOfflineChip.vue:17; status-lamp.ts:60 `label: "backend offline — saved locally"` vs ApiOfflineChip.vue:25. Roles identical (status-lamp.ts:39 alert|status; ApiOfflineChip.vue:13,21). Measured CSS declaration-set intersection: lamp .dock-status-lamp = 18 decls, chip .api-offline-chip = 13 decls, IDENTICAL = 11; only-in-chip = ['border-radius: var(--radius-pill)','padding: 0.3rem 0.7rem']. Twin keyframes: DockStatusLamp.vue:110-118 `lamp-dot-pulse` vs ApiOfflineChip.vue:82-89 `offline-dot-pulse` — identical bodies (0%,100%{opacity:1} 50%{opacity:.35}), identical `2.4s var(--ease-standard) infinite`. Duplication is documented not cured at status-lamp.ts:8-9 and DockStatusLamp.vue:41-42 ("one status language, two seats").
defects.mechanism: Module placement error — a pure resolver homed in the consumer directory (demo/shell/dock/) instead of beside its state (demo/platform/transport/availability.ts). Reuse from the second seat would require a palettes→shell lateral feature edge (the demo otherwise has only two such edges, both `import type`: usePalettePorts.ts:19, ColorPicker.vue:130), so the second implementation is structurally forced. Unique semantic ownership violated by placement.
defects.reproduction: grep -c comparison of the two SFCs plus the normalized declaration-set diff (pasted in the report). ApiOfflineChip.vue:36-37 re-derives the matrix inline (`availability.value === "unavailable"` / `=== "misconfigured"`) and is covered by zero rows of test/status-lamp.test.ts. HYPOTHESIS (not reproduced): with ≥1 saved colour on /#/palettes both seats render simultaneously as two role="alert" nodes with identical text — measured document.querySelectorAll('[role="alert"]').length === 1 on an empty session because CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:116's `v-if="savedColorStrings.length > 0"` gate was false.
defects.proposedCure: Move the resolver to demo/platform/transport/api-status.ts as `resolveApiStatus(availability, isDev) → ApiStatusFace | null` (state/role/label, using glass-ui's StatusDotState vocabulary); delete demo/shell/dock/status-lamp.ts and ApiOfflineChip.vue; both seats render ONE new demo/shared/ui/ApiStatusPill.vue built from glass-ui Chip + StatusDot. Every edge becomes downward (shell→shared→platform, palettes→shared→platform).

defects.defect: The demo's declared value.js type surface does not match the published export map: three tsconfig paths targets do not exist, two published subpaths (including the demo's second-most-used) have no paths entry and typecheck against a stale installed copy of the package inside the repo that IS the package.
defects.evidence: package.json#exports keys = ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize (7, NO "."). tsconfig.demo.json paths keys = @mkbabb/value.js @mkbabb/value.js/color /parsing /math /easing /units /transform /quantize (8). `test -f dist/index.d.ts` → MISSING; dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts → MISSING; dist/subpaths/units.d.ts → MISSING (against a dist built 2026-07-27 11:52). Demo import counts: @mkbabb/value.js/color ×25, /css ×10, /math ×6, /easing ×5, /quantize ×4 — /css and /value have NO paths entry. node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js is a real installed 4.0.0 tarball (readlink → not a symlink; own package.json/LICENSE/README/dist dated Jul 17 21:10). Drift measured: dist/subpaths/css.d.ts = 12490 B vs node_modules copy = 10910 B; diff shows `declare type Alpha_2`, `Channel_2`, `ChannelsBySpace_2` present live and absent installed. dist/subpaths/css.js 43973 B vs 43972 B.
defects.mechanism: Two independent declarations of one public surface. vite.config.ts:44-51 GENERATES its runtime alias set from package.json#exports; tsconfig.demo.json#paths is hand-maintained and has drifted. Where a paths entry is absent, TS falls through to node_modules — and a self-installed copy of the repo's own package sits there, so vue-tsc checks a stale .d.ts while Vite bundles the live dist. The `.` root paths entry types an import no real consumer can write (an exports map without a "." key yields ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED).
defects.reproduction: node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./package.json').exports).join(' '))"; then the tsconfig paths key dump; then `test -f` on the three missing targets; then `ls -l` + `diff` of dist/subpaths/css.d.ts against node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts. All commands and outputs pasted in the report.
defects.proposedCure: Generate tsconfig.demo.json#paths from package.json#exports with the same script that generates the Vite aliases — one source of truth, drift structurally impossible. Remove @mkbabb/value.js from the repo's own node_modules so exactly one copy of the library exists in the graph. Add a `.` export to package.json#exports or delete the bare-specifier paths entry; do not type an import no consumer can write.

defects.defect: `--type-mono-caption` is a phantom CSS custom property with zero definition sites anywhere, masked at three consumption sites by three different fallbacks; the lamp consequently paints at a fixed 11px outside the design system's fluid caption scale.
defects.evidence: `grep -rlo -- "--type-mono-caption:" demo/ src/ node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` → no output (zero definition sites). Live: getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--type-mono-caption') === ""; --type-caption === "clamp( 0.75rem, 0.71rem + 0.21vw, 1rem )". Computed .dock-status-lamp fontSize = 11px. Three consumers with three masks: DockStatusLamp.vue:54 `var(--type-mono-caption, 0.6875rem)`, ApiOfflineChip.vue:47 same, ComponentSliders.vue:310 `var(--type-mono-caption, var(--type-caption))`. glass-ui ships the recipe as `@utility text-mono-caption { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--type-caption); letter-spacing: var(--type-tracking-caps); text-transform: uppercase }` (dist/styles/typography/utilities.css), already used at 8 demo sites including demo/shell/dock/menus/ProfileSection.vue:132 and PaletteCardMenu.vue:37. --type-tracking-caps = 0.1em vs the lamp's hand-rolled 0.06em.
defects.mechanism: A Tailwind @utility NAME was read as if it implied a matching custom property. The literal fallback then hid the broken contract permanently — a masking fallback (edict 2) over a design-system recipe the demo already owns elsewhere (edict 4).
defects.reproduction: Navigate http://localhost:9000/#/ and evaluate getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--type-mono-caption') → ""; getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.dock-status-lamp')).fontSize → "11px". Static: the grep above returns zero definition sites.
defects.proposedCure: Delete all three `var(--type-mono-caption, …)` sites and apply glass-ui's `text-mono-caption` utility (paired with `fira-code` as at ConsoleRail.vue:75). Also drop the dead `, 9999px` and `, oklch(0.58 0.19 25)` fallbacks — both --radius-pill and --destructive resolve live, and the sibling chip already writes --radius-pill bare.

defects.defect: Three glass-ui primitives the design system already exports (StatusDot, Chip, Pulse) are hand-rolled in demo scoped CSS — twice, once per duplicate seat.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json exports include ./status-dot, ./chip, ./pulse. StatusDot props (dist/components/status-dot/StatusDot.vue.d.ts): { state?: "online"|"warning"|"error"|"unknown"; size?: "sm"|"md"; label?: string } with JSDoc "Accessible identity. Omit when adjacent text already names the state." Chip (dist/components/chip/types.d.ts + chipVariants.d.ts): mode "static", shape "pill", SIZE.sm = "gap-1 px-2.5 py-1 text-caption". DockStatusLamp.vue:43-62 hand-rolls the pill, :79-86 + :104-107 the dot, :109-122 the pulse. Demo already imports Chip from @mkbabb/glass-ui/chip at demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:14 (house precedent); StatusDot and Pulse have ZERO demo consumers.
defects.mechanism: Design-system bypass (edict 4). The primitive's own accessibility affordance (StatusDot's `label` prop) exists precisely to prevent the failure this component then hit in L-4.
defects.reproduction: cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/status-dot/StatusDot.vue.d.ts and .../chip/chipVariants.d.ts; grep -rn 'glass-ui/chip|glass-ui/status-dot|glass-ui/pulse' demo/ → one hit only (EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:14).
defects.proposedCure: <Chip mode="static" shape="pill" size="sm" :tone="face.tone" :role="face.role"><StatusDot :state="face.state" :label="face.label" />{{ face.label }}</Chip>, with misconfigured→"error" and unavailable→"unknown" mapped in the moved resolver. If the filled-vs-open-ring distinction is not expressible in StatusDotState, that variant belongs IN glass-ui, not in a demo [data-variant] override.

defects.defect: role="alert" with an empty accessible name below 1024px: the only text in the live region is display:none, which removes it from the accessibility tree — and the in-file comment asserts the opposite.
defects.evidence: DockStatusLamp.vue:67-69 `.lamp-label { display: none }`, lifted only at :70-74 `@media (min-width:1024px){ display:inline }`; dot is aria-hidden at :18; root carries :role="lamp.role" at :16. Comment at :65-66 claims "The role + label stay in the accessibility tree (visually-hidden, not v-if'd)" — false: CSS Display §1.3 (display:none generates no boxes, contents not rendered) and HTML-AAM exclude non-rendered subtrees from accessibility APIs. MEASURED at innerWidth 430: labelDisplay "none", role "alert", lamp.innerText === "", rect 25.99×17.99. At innerWidth 1440: labelDisplay "block", innerText "dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`". Coverage gap: test/status-lamp.test.ts asserts only the pure matrix; e2e/smoke/oracles/o22-status-lamp.spec.ts:56-83 asserts data-variant/role/geometry at desktop only, never the accessible name; the visual audit's a11y probe records only smallTapTargets/imgNoAlt/namelessButtons (REPORT.json results[].probe.a11y), and namelessButtons inspects buttons — an unnamed alert is invisible to it.
defects.mechanism: The accessible name is a property of the resolved face (status-lamp.ts:40 already carries `label`), but the rendering decision that destroys it lives in an unrelated media query in the SFC with no contract between the two modules. Three test suites, zero coverage of the pairing.
defects.reproduction: Playwright: browser_navigate http://localhost:9000/#/ ; browser_resize 430×900 ; evaluate → { labelDisplay: "none", role: "alert", lampInnerText: "" }. Then resize 1440×900 → innerText restored. Full outputs pasted in the report.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt glass-ui StatusDot's `label` prop (L-3), or replace display:none with sr-only/clip-rect. Never display:none the only text in a live region. The compact/expanded decision belongs in the shared ApiStatusPill's `compact` prop, tested once, not in each seat's media query.

defects.defect: Two paths to @mkbabb/glass-ui/dock in adjacent lines of the same file; the barrel that provides the second path exists to serve exactly one import line and re-exports a third-party package.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:4 `import { GlassDock, DockLayerGroup, DockLayer } from "./";` sits directly above Dock.vue:5 `import { DockControl, DockSeparator } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock";`. demo/shell/dock/index.ts is 2 export lines: the glass-ui re-export plus `export { default as Dock } from "./Dock.vue"`. Ten other demo sites use the direct specifier: GradientVisualizer.vue:13, MixResultDisplay.vue:3, ExtractWorkbench.vue:187, ExtractControls.vue:98, ImageEyedropper.vue:95, ConfigSliderPane.vue:20, ActionButton.vue:55, DockViewSelect.vue:3, Dock.vue:5, ActionBarToggle.vue:5. Dock.vue:4 is the ONLY consumer of the barrel's re-export. The `Dock` export has one consumer, App.vue:167. DockStatusLamp is NOT in the barrel (Dock.vue:14 imports it relatively) — 2 of the directory's 9 components are published by no stated rule.
defects.mechanism: A pass-through barrel with no added value creates a second specifier for an already-public package; the directory then imports its own index from within itself (Dock.vue → ./ → ./Dock.vue). Dual path (edict 2) plus contrivance (edict 3).
defects.reproduction: cat demo/shell/dock/index.ts; sed -n '4,5p' demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue; grep -rn '@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock' demo/ (10 direct sites) and grep -rn 'from "\./"' demo/ (1 relevant site).
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/shell/dock/index.ts. Rewrite Dock.vue:4 to the direct @mkbabb/glass-ui/dock specifier (merging with line 5) and App.vue:167 to `import Dock from "../shell/dock/Dock.vue"`. Net −1 file, −1 indirection, one path to the design system everywhere.

defects.defect: The api-client provide/inject seam is unsubstitutable — a DI wrapper around module singletons with one provider, no parameters, and no test double — and its only measurable effect is to make the component un-mountable in tests, which is what forced the resolver extraction that L-1 then mislocated.
defects.evidence: useApiClient.ts:36-44 `createApiClient()` takes NO parameters and returns { request, adminRequest, sessionToken: sessionTokenRef, availability: apiAvailability, baseUrl: BASE_URL } — `availability` IS the module ref exported at availability.ts:47. One provider: App.vue:189 provideApiClient(). Three consumers, all reading only `availability`: DockStatusLamp.vue:30, ApiOfflineChip.vue:35, PaletteCardMenu.vue:216. useApiClient.ts:56-60 throws when no provider stands above. Yet the docs claim "never a hard module-singleton import" (useApiClient.ts:2-16, echoed at DockStatusLamp.vue:28-29). test/status-lamp.test.ts never mounts the SFC — it imports the extracted pure function only.
defects.mechanism: An abstraction with exactly one implementation and no injection point is not a seam; it is indirection. Its cost is real (the component cannot be mounted without an App-root provider), and paying that cost produced the extracted-resolver pattern that was then homed in the wrong directory — L-6 is the proximate cause of L-1.
defects.reproduction: Read useApiClient.ts:36-44 (zero-parameter factory closing over module state) and grep -rn 'provideApiClient|createApiClient' demo/ → exactly one provider site (App.vue:189) and zero substitutions anywhere in demo/, test/, or e2e/.
defects.proposedCure: Either give the seam a reason to exist — `createApiClient(deps)` with an injectable transport so tests can drive faces through the mounted component — or delete it and import `apiAvailability` directly at the three consumers (three one-line edits). Do not keep a seam that cannot seam.

defects.defect: Demo unit tests have two homes: the library test tree test/ (documented as mirroring src/) contains 11 files importing 21 distinct demo modules, while demo/test/** exists as the declared demo-suite home.

defects.defect: The component's layout correctness depends on a positioning context authored in a third module and mounted by a fourth, with nothing enforcing it; the containing box is overflow:hidden, so the failure mode is silent disappearance.
defects.evidence: DockStatusLamp.vue:44-47 is `position: absolute; inset-inline-end: 0; top: 50%; translate: 0 -50%` with no positioned ancestor of its own. MEASURED live: lamp.offsetParent.className === "dock-band overture-dock-land". The context is demo/styles/shell.css:39-40 `.dock-band { position: relative; … }` (whose comment names the dependency: "position: relative seats the band-chrome instruments (the W6-6 status lamp)"), mounted at demo/color-picker/App.vue:26 `<nav class="dock-band">`. defects.defect: The slug-login error surface is dead end-to-end through FOUR independent breaks: a failed sign-in produces no error, no spinner, and no retry affordance anywhere in the app.

(c) `slugError` is written at SlugEditLayer.vue:18,43,49,59-62 and read NOWHERE; the template (75-119) has no error node (contrast PaletteSlugBar.vue:124-126 which does render it). (d) useSlugMigration.ts:78-81 reports via `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)`; slugBarRef (line 30) is never assigned — demo/color-picker/App.vue:153-156 consumes only showMigrateDialog/migrateMode/onMigrateRespond — so it is permanently null and `?.` swallows all four branches.
defects.mechanism: Error is modelled as an imperative push into a component instance rather than as state on the identity port. Nothing type-checks the obligation to render a Ref that does not exist, so the display could die without any consumer noticing.
defects.reproduction: Read the four cited spans. Corroborating: the S.W2 W2-6 comment at useSlugMigration.ts:73-77 documents that HTTP-status substring matching on e.message never matched and was replaced with `e instanceof ApiProblem ? e.status : undefined` — SlugEditLayer.vue:57-62 re-introduces the exact cured defect.

defects.defect: Layering inversion plus a module-tree cycle: demo/shell (the shell) depends on demo/palettes (a feature) at 5 edges, while demo/palettes depends back on demo/shell — and demo/platform/auth/ already exists as the correct home for the identity port.

result.strongestDefect: L-2 — the slug-login error surface is dead end-to-end through four independent breaks (unawaited async call at SlugEditLayer.vue:54; unreachable catch at 57-62 because useSlugMigration.ts:53-83 can never reject; write-only `slugError` never rendered in the template; and useSlugMigration.ts:78-81 reporting into a `slugBarRef` that App.vue never binds, so it is permanently null). A user whose slug or admin token is rejected sees the field close, the input clear, and nothing else — no error, no spinner, no retry affordance. No test, type, or lint rule observes any of the four. The mechanism is that error is modelled as an imperative push into a component instance instead of as state on the identity port, which is precisely why the display could die unnoticed.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but nine live hypotheses on this axis were killed by evidence and are recorded so the next seat does not re-spend the probes: (1) NO deep-src imports — `grep -rn 'from \"../../../src|@src|value.js/src\"' demo/` returns zero; the demo speaks only published @mkbabb/value.js subpaths and the T.W1 dogfood boundary holds. (2) The inert layer does NOT steal focus — first-load probe: all three controls inertAncestor:true, slugInputFocusable:false, focusableCount:12 with the slug input excluded; the producer's DockLayer applies inert correctly. (3) The inert layer does NOT steal pointer events — inactive .dock-face computes pointer-events:'none'; a mid-probe Playwright 'intercepts pointer events' error came from the app being legitimately in slug-edit mode after my own earlier synthetic click, not a z-order defect, confirmed by the layer dump. (4) The three 22x22 controls PASS WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (AA) via the spacing exception — measured center distances 47.00/75.00/28.00 px, all >= 24, so the 24px-diameter circles do not intersect; MT-F004's 'below the 24x24 minimum' premise is a harness heuristic that does not implement the exception and is overstated for this component. (5) `npx eslint demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue` is CLEAN with zero output — proving none of L-1..L-8 is reachable by the existing lint gate. (6) verbatimModuleSyntax is satisfied: the SFC imports no types and SESSION_PORT_KEY is a value, so no `import type` is missing. defects.mechanism: ApiOfflineChip lives inside a palette Card (an opaque specimen well, VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2 tier 4) where a 55% `--background` film sits on a known neutral and reads as a real chip. DockStatusLamp copies that exact declaration onto the ambient field (tier 1). The register was transposed; its substrate was not. The scheme switch retunes `--background`/`--foreground`/`--destructive`, none of which describe what is actually behind the chip, so dark mode changes nothing perceptually — a red hairline on a salmon field. Breaches §2 'Dark chrome uses the restrained neutral pole' and §4.1 'a token name is not evidence'.
defects.reproduction: Same as D-1; the field-vs-chip columns are sampled in scratchpad/png3.mjs at y in [0.42h,0.62h], x in [1190,1400] (interior) and [1080,1150] (field).
defects.proposedCure: Same transposition as D-1 — give the component a substrate by seating it in the dock plate. Do not add a local backdrop-filter or a hardcoded neutral: that forks the glass ladder (the exact class of fork demo/styles/shell.css:141-216 documents as a booked-swap interim).

defects.defect: Below 1024px the lamp is a `role="alert"` with an EMPTY accessible name and zero rendered content — the user is shown a 6.4px dot and told nothing by any channel. The component's own comment claims the opposite.
defects.evidence: Live at 390x844: role="alert", aria-label=null, textContent="dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`", innerText="" (empty), labelDisplay="none", lampRect 26x18 CSS px. Source: DockStatusLamp.vue:67-69 `.lamp-label { display: none }`; the dot at :18 is aria-hidden="true". The comment at DockStatusLamp.vue:64-66 asserts "The role + label stay in the accessibility tree (visually-hidden, not v-if'd)" — display:none removes a subtree from the a11y tree, so the claim is false. Frame: frames/band-390.png.
defects.mechanism: The compaction strategy deletes the only named channel instead of hiding it. Accessible-name computation excludes non-rendered nodes; with no aria-label and an aria-hidden dot, the live region's name resolves to the empty string. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 requires that failed/pending states are 'never color-only' and that 'role, accessible name, state/value ... are explicit' — under 1024px this state is both colour-only AND nameless.
defects.reproduction: Live dev server, resize to 390x844, evaluate: document.querySelector('.dock-status-lamp').innerText === '' while .textContent is the full sentence. Reproduced 2026-07-27.
defects.proposedCure: `display:none` must become a visually-hidden idiom (`position:absolute; clip-path: inset(50%)`) so the label survives in the accessibility tree at every viewport — and, under the D-6 cure, the compaction decision moves to the dock's own container/overflow logic where a truncation can be announced rather than deleted.

defects.defect: The component is a fork of ApiOfflineChip.vue — 17 of 26 style declarations byte-identical, plus a duplicated keyframe and both label strings copied verbatim — and both chips render simultaneously from the same latch, telling the user the identical sentence twice on one screen.
defects.evidence: comm -12 over the two scoped style blocks: chip 26 decls, lamp 34, 17 byte-identical (align-items, background x3, border x2, color x2, display, font-size, font-variant, gap, height, letter-spacing, line-height, white-space, width). Copy fork: status-lamp.ts:54 vs ApiOfflineChip.vue:17 and status-lamp.ts:60 vs ApiOfflineChip.vue:25. Keyframe fork: `lamp-dot-pulse` (DockStatusLamp.vue:110-118) vs `offline-dot-pulse` (ApiOfflineChip.vue:82-85) — same two stops, same `2.4s var(--ease-standard) infinite`. Both read useApiClient().availability. The tranche already knew: T-9 relayed 'the dock status-lamp primitive' to glass-ui at docs/tranches/T/letters/GLASSUI-T-COMMUNIQUE-2026-07-11.md:60 and GLASSUI-T-ASKS.md:104; never answered, fork shipped anyway.
defects.mechanism: One status language written down twice with no shared source. DockStatusLamp.vue:42 calls it 'one status language, two seats' and status-lamp.ts:8 calls it 'the instrument register the per-surface ApiOfflineChip already speaks' — the prose asserts a sharing that does not exist in code. Breaches owner edicts #3 (KISS/no contrivance), #4 (glass-ui is the design system), #5 (root-level styling), and PROPORTION-AUDIT register row PR-06 (duplicated species => REMOVE) plus §5.6 'subtraction precedes explanation'. Drift has already started: padding-inline 0.55rem vs 0.7rem, `var(--radius-pill, 9999px)` vs bare `var(--radius-pill)`.
defects.reproduction: Navigate to /#/palettes with the backend unreachable in dev — the dock lamp and the per-surface chip both render the same sentence. Structural evidence is the diff above (deterministic, no browser needed).
defects.proposedCure: One primitive, two seats — for real. Primary: the glass-ui dock status seat (C-1), consumed by both sites, so the register lives at the producer. Floor: collapse the two demo SFCs into a single status-chip component that takes a `LampState`; the label strings live once, in status-lamp.ts (which is already the right module and should survive unchanged).

defects.defect: The annotation is orphaned from what it annotates: at one viewport its interval to the dock pill measures 56.2px, 230.6px and 426.2px depending on the dock's own morph — pure residue, oscillating 195.6px per collapse/expand — and it reserves no space at all.
defects.evidence: Live at 1440x900, .glass-dock rect vs lamp rect in the same second: resting/collapsed pill [689.2,750.8] w=61.6, lamp [1177,1424] => gap 426.2px; expanded pill [493.6,946.4] w=452.8 => gap 230.6px; expanded nav layer pill right=1120.8 => gap 56.2px. Lamp never moves. Lamp occupies 17.5% of the 1408px band and is the only content in its right third (frames/band-1440-light.png). Collision threshold measured at 1024x768: band 992px, lamp 247px => any dock layer wider than 498.1px overlaps the pill; signed-out nav layer is 309px (94.5px clearance), but measured dock widths across states range 258.7-452.8px and the action-bar/slug-edit layers are wider.
defects.mechanism: `position: absolute; inset-inline-end: 0` on `.dock-band` anchors the lamp to the band's edge, not to the pill; the interval is therefore `viewportWidth − dockWidth`, an accident. DockStatusLamp.vue:38-42 claims it 'reads as an instrument annotation etched into the chrome' — there is no chrome at the band's inline-end to etch into. Breaches PROPORTION-AUDIT §1 ('every element earns its ... interval and material from its job relative to the local protagonist') and §5.8 ('real rendered relation wins over token intent'). Dock.vue:124's T-31 claim that occlusion is 'impossible by construction — grid rows do not overlap' does not cover an absolutely-positioned child inside row 1.
defects.reproduction: Live: measure .glass-dock and .dock-status-lamp rects at 1440x900 before and after the 5s collapse. Reproduced 2026-07-27. The overlap sub-case (a >498px dock layer at <=1100px) was NOT reproduced and is filed as a hypothesis; the zero-reservation design is the defect and is proven.
defects.proposedCure: Seat it inside the pill (C-1): the interval to the protagonist becomes zero because the lamp IS the protagonist's chrome — no absolute positioning, no residue, no unreserved overlap, and the dock's own layout owns the reservation.

defects.defect: The compaction decision asks the wrong question: a `min-width: 1024px` viewport media query, not the band's actual free space. The lamp steps 26.0px -> 247.0px (9.5x) across one pixel of window width.
defects.evidence: DockStatusLamp.vue:70-74 `@media (min-width: 1024px) { .lamp-label { display: inline } }`. Measured widths: 26.0px at <1024, 247.0px at >=1024. At 1024 the lamp consumes 247 of the 341.5px free right of the pill = 72.3% of that side's free space. Corroborated by the tranche's own outbound mail, docs/tranches/V/coordination/INBOX.md:72 (O-10 §A, sent 2026-07-27): 'DockStatusLamp carries a wrong-question viewport fallback instead'. `.dock-band` (demo/styles/shell.css:39) has no `container-type`, so a container query is not available today.
defects.mechanism: The constraint that matters is 'is there room beside the pill', which depends on the dock's content width — a quantity a viewport media query cannot see. glass-ui already ships the right mechanism (`@container dock` in dock/styles/density.css) and per O-10 we consume it at 0 sites. Breaches VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.7: 'Spacing is container-scaled from glass-ui tokens ... no breakpoint pile.'
defects.reproduction: Live: resize 1023 -> 1024 and read .dock-status-lamp getBoundingClientRect().width (26.0 -> 247.0). Reproduced 2026-07-27.
defects.proposedCure: Under C-1 the question disappears — the dock's own overflow/density logic decides. Floor arm: add `container-type: inline-size` to `.dock-band` and drive compaction from the band's free space; never from `min-width`.

defects.defect: An infinite opacity blink with no pause, stop, or hide mechanism — WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.2 failure and a direct breach of the constitution's motion-termination law.
defects.evidence: Computed animation on .lamp-dot: `2.4s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) infinite lamp-dot-pulse-45530b34`; keyframe DockStatusLamp.vue:110-118 pulses opacity 1 -> 0.35 -> 1. No pause control exists anywhere. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6: 'Continuous ... motion terminates within five seconds or exposes one persistent keyboard-operable still/pause control whose state is announced and remembered. Paused, parked and offscreen mean no animation work.'
defects.mechanism: The pulse was adopted as an 'instrument register' flourish and given no terminator. It runs for the entire session, on a region that never changes. Sub-defect: `2.4s` is a raw literal while only the easing half is tokenized — owner law #6 requires motion be tokenized, not half-tokenized.
defects.reproduction: Live: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.lamp-dot')).animation contains 'infinite'. Reproduced 2026-07-27. (No flash risk: 0.42Hz, far below the 3Hz threshold.)
defects.proposedCure: Terminate the pulse at 5s (`animation-iteration-count` bounded), or expose one persistent keyboard-operable stop whose state persists. Under C-1 the producer's own dock motion register owns this and the duration comes off the ladder.

defects.defect: `role="alert"` is both the wrong register for a permanent state and inert in the exact scenario the component was designed for: the alert exists at first paint, so no screen reader announces it.
defects.evidence: demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:159-166 — initApiEnvironment() sets apiAvailability.value='misconfigured' synchronously at client init, before any fetch. DockStatusLamp.vue:3-6 states the design goal: the misconfigured state is 'guaranteed visible the moment the shell paints'. ARIA live regions announce mutations observed after the region is registered; a live region present in the initial render is not announced. DockStatusLamp.vue:16 binds :role="lamp.role" from status-lamp.ts:52 ('alert'). Combined with D-4, two live regions carry the same sentence.
defects.mechanism: The a11y role was chosen as a semantic label for loudness ('the a11y role IS the register', status-lamp.ts:38) rather than for the announcement behaviour it actually specifies. A permanent, non-dismissible, never-updating dev-config state is not an alert. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 gives the house rule for this shape — 'never a routine live region: ordinary text uses aria-live="off"' — and §5.1 forbids duplicate live-region echo.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the announcement claim as a live AT capture (hypothesis, grounded in the ARIA live-region spec and the synchronous-init source path); the synchronous first-paint presence IS reproduced — availability.ts:164 runs at client init and the lamp renders at first paint on localhost:9000.
defects.proposedCure: Retire role="alert". Use role="status" at most, or plain named text with aria-live="off", and let the loud channel stay where it already works — the console.error at availability.ts:166, which is the honest dev-facing alarm. Exactly one region across the two seats.

defects.defect: `font-variant: small-caps` is applied to the whole label including a case-sensitive shell command, so the user is instructed to run `NPM RUN DEV`; and the Markdown backticks paint as literal stray glyphs.
defects.evidence: Rendered: '● DEV MISCONFIGURED — RUN ˋNPM RUN DEVˋ' (frames/lamp-1440-light.png, frames/band-1440-light.png). Source string status-lamp.ts:54 is "dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`"; DockStatusLamp.vue:52 sets font-variant: small-caps on the container; :19 interpolates {{ lamp.label }} as text. Computed font-variant-caps = 'small-caps', font-family Fira Code (no smcp table on this path, so the engine synthesizes by scaling capitals).
defects.mechanism: A caption-wide typographic sledgehammer applied over content that contains code. The message's entire job is to be actionable and its casing is load-bearing; the styling destroys it. Markdown is being used in a medium with no markup. Breaches VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4 type jurisdiction ('value, code, or provenance -> text-mono-small ... Fira Code') — code needs its own run, not a container-level font-variant.
defects.reproduction: Live dev server at 1440, screenshot `.dock-status-lamp` — the command renders in synthesized small caps with two literal backticks. Reproduced 2026-07-27, frame committed.
defects.proposedCure: Split the code run: the command becomes its own `<code>` span with `font-variant: normal` (and the type role it deserves); the backticks come out of the string entirely. The label becomes structured content, not a Markdown-flavoured string literal.

defects.defect: The quiet `unavailable` face also fails AA in dark — computed 4.33:1 against the 4.5:1 floor — and, like D-1, has no floor at all because both operands are functions of the user's seed colour.
defects.evidence: Arithmetic over MEASURED inputs (tokens from getComputedStyle, field pixels from frames/band-1440-*.png): light fill = 0.55*rgb(253,250,244)+0.45*rgb(244,136,92) = rgb(249,199,176) L=0.6396; ink = 0.72*rgb(28,26,25)+0.28*fill = rgb(90,74,67) L=0.0752 => 5.51:1, fill-vs-field 1.62:1. Dark fill = 0.55*rgb(11,10,9)+0.45*rgb(242,129,95) = rgb(115,64,48) L=0.0747; ink = 0.72*rgb(233,229,222)+0.28*fill = rgb(200,183,173) L=0.4903 => 4.33:1, fill-vs-field 3.24:1.
defects.mechanism: Same as D-2 — DockStatusLamp.vue:59-60 composites a 72%-alpha foreground over a 55%-alpha background over the aurora. Light passes today only because the default seed happens to be light. Breaches VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1.
defects.reproduction: NONE as a direct pixel capture — the latch was 'misconfigured' on this host so the unavailable face could not be forced live; the numbers are arithmetic over measured tokens and measured field pixels. Labelled a computed result, not a rendered measurement. Forcible via the e2e route-abort recipe in e2e/smoke/oracles/o22-status-lamp.spec.ts:44-47.
defects.proposedCure: Same substrate cure as D-1/D-2, plus a pi row asserting >=4.5:1 ink-vs-fill and >=3:1 fill-vs-field at BOTH schemes across the seed extremes — a measured floor, not a token claim.

defects.defect: Zero rendered witnesses: the component appears in none of the tranche's 60 Safari captures nor any state matrix, and its shipping face is structurally unrenderable by its own gate — so the O-22 GREEN seal carries no information about anything in this report.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md covers 4 matrices x 15 routes = 60 captures; the lamp is absent from all, verified directly in safari-desktop-{light,dark}/picker.png, forced-colors-desktop/picker.png, rtl-desktop/picker.png — yet it renders live on the same origin (localhost:9000). e2e/smoke/oracles/o22-status-lamp.spec.ts header: 'HARNESS BOUND (recorded, not fudged): the `misconfigured` variant CANNOT fire under this suite — the e2e webServer sets VITE_API_URL'. test/status-lamp.test.ts: all 18 expect() calls assert variant/role/label strings and the transport contract — no geometry, no contrast, no accessible name, no viewport arm.
defects.mechanism: The gate was built entirely around the resolver's truth table and the transport contract, both of which are sound, and never around the rendered artefact. Breaches VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §8 ('a visual claim without a tracked frame pair and a named delta is incomplete') and PROPORTION-AUDIT §3, which requires a `current witness` real frame for every status species. This is the process defect that let D-1 through D-9 survive four tranches.
defects.reproduction: grep the shots tree and read the four named PNGs — the lamp is in none. Read the oracle header. Deterministic, reproduced 2026-07-27.
defects.proposedCure: Add a capture-matrix arm that forces the latch to each variant (route-abort for `unavailable`, unset VITE_API_URL for `misconfigured`) at 1440 and 390 in both schemes, so the component stops being invisible to its own audit. Frames, not assertions about strings.

defects.defect: `--type-mono-caption` does not exist anywhere in the tree — three consumers, zero definitions — so the lamp's type size is an untracked 11px literal wearing a token's name; two further masking fallbacks hide a second hardcoded red and a second radius.
defects.evidence: grep -rn -- '--type-mono-caption *:' demo/ src/ node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/ | wc -l => 0; grep -rn -- 'var(--type-mono-caption' demo/ | wc -l => 3. Live: getComputedStyle(documentElement).getPropertyValue('--type-mono-caption') === '' and getComputedStyle(lamp).fontSize === '11px' (the 0.6875rem fallback). Also DockStatusLamp.vue:57,83 `var(--radius-pill, 9999px)` and :92,95,100 `var(--destructive, oklch(0.58 0.19 25))` — both tokens DO resolve (9999px; light-dark(hsl(0 72% 50%), hsl(0 80% 60%))), so the fallbacks are dead branches that would silently substitute a different red if the token moved.
defects.mechanism: Masking fallbacks — owner edict #2 forbids them exactly because they convert a broken token reference into a silent, untracked literal. The type ladder can never reach this component, and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4's named `mono-caption` role does not in fact apply to it. The sibling has already drifted (ApiOfflineChip.vue:50 writes bare `var(--radius-pill)`).
defects.reproduction: The two greps above plus the live getPropertyValue. Deterministic, reproduced 2026-07-27.
defects.proposedCure: Delete all three fallbacks. Either define `--type-mono-caption` in the ladder (its two other consumers are broken the same way — demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:310) or consume the existing `--type-caption`. A token reference must either resolve or fail loudly.

defects.defect: The box is built from raw magic numbers on no ladder, and has already diverged in density from the chip it forked.
defects.evidence: DockStatusLamp.vue: gap 0.4rem (:51), letter-spacing 0.06em (:53), padding 0.3rem 0.55rem (:56, computed 4.8px 8.8px), dot 0.4rem square (:81-82), border 1.5px (:84), animation 2.4s (:120). ApiOfflineChip.vue:49 uses padding 0.3rem 0.7rem (11.2px) — the two seats already render at different inline densities.
defects.mechanism: Six literals standing in for the spacing, sizing and motion ladders. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.7 separates glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation as three distinct quantities; here all three are one hardcoded box, and §5.8 requires real rendered relation over token intent — there is no relation to any rung.
defects.reproduction: Read the two files. Deterministic.
defects.proposedCure: Under C-1 the geometry comes off the producer's dock density ladder. Floor arm: every value resolves from a named rung, and the two seats share one box because they share one component.

defects.defect: No forced-colors arm; below 1024px the only surviving distinction between a dev-config error and an offline backend would be a 6.4px open-ring vs filled-dot shape.
defects.evidence: No `@media (forced-colors: active)` anywhere in DockStatusLamp.vue (123 lines read in full). Under forced colors the UA replaces `background` and `border-color` with system colours, leaving only the dot's ring/fill difference (DockStatusLamp.vue:79-86 vs :104-107) at 6.398px measured. Combined with D-3 (label display:none under 1024px), that 6.4px shape is the sole remaining channel.
defects.mechanism: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 requires state to survive forced colours and reduced transparency with an explicit name and state. The design's two-variant distinction rests on hue plus a sub-7px shape, and the naming channel is deleted at exactly the viewport where the shape channel becomes the only one.
defects.reproduction: NONE — the tranche's forced-colors-desktop matrix contains no lamp to measure (see D-11), so this is a HYPOTHESIS grounded in the source and the measured dot size.
defects.proposedCure: Fix D-3 first (the name must survive at every viewport), then add an explicit forced-colors arm asserting a non-zero, non-colour delta between the two variants — or, under C-1, inherit the producer's forced-colors treatment for dock status seats.

result.strongestDefect: D-1/D-2 (one mechanism, two faces): the loud `misconfigured` alert — the face that actually ships on every `npm run dev:web-only` session — renders at a MEASURED 1.79:1 in light and 1.38:1 in dark against a 4.5:1 AA floor, and its own chip surface measures 1.112:1 / 1.059:1 against the field behind it. The root is a single design error: the ApiOfflineChip register (a 55%-alpha film designed for an opaque specimen well inside a Card) was photocopied onto the ambient aurora field, which VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2 defines as the user's own live colour. The register was transposed; its substrate was not. The result is an alert that is, literally, invisible — and whose contrast has no computable floor because the backdrop is user data. Frame: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-dockstatuslamp/frames/band-1440-light.png.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so no negative proof is claimed for the component as a whole. Recorded here so the cure does not destroy what is sound, each item positively verified rather than assumed: (1) `demo/shell/dock/status-lamp.ts` is a genuinely good module — pure, total, `isDev` threaded as an argument instead of read from import.meta, closed-form testable; the `misconfigured != unavailable` distinction is real and correctly preserved. Keep it unchanged through the cure. (2) The transport seam is right: DockStatusLamp.vue:30 injects via useApiClient(), never a module-singleton import, and never re-derives availability.ts. (3) verbatimModuleSyntax clean — status-lamp.ts:31 is `import type { ApiAvailability }`; the SFC imports only values. Edict #8 satisfied. (4) Vue 3.5 idiom clean — no props, no defineModel, no stale-read hazard; edict #7 satisfied with nothing to change. (5) The reduced-motion gate is CORRECTLY authored: both the @keyframes and the animation live inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so `reduce` resolves to the static final state with no override needed — edict #6 satisfied (scoped keyframe in the component is permitted). (6) The animated property is `opacity` — compositor-only, no layout or paint invalidation; no motion-performance finding exists. (7) RTL was CHECKED, not assumed: at dir=rtl / 1440 the lamp correctly mirrors to [16,263] (`inset-inline-end` is properly logical), and I rendered the label under RTL (frames/lamp-rtl-1440.png) — the string is all strong-LTR Latin with only neutral `—` and backticks between LTR runs, so the bidi algorithm leaves the order intact. The VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1 LTR-isolation concern does not manifest for this string: NO FINDING, proven negative. (8) `pointer-events: none` with tabIndex -1 is correct — the lamp is not operable and does not steal hits from the dock, so its 26x18px mobile box is expressly NOT a tap-target defect. (9) Not a god module: 123 lines, one job, colocated resolver; edict #1 satisfied.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue (shell/dock)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m] (1M-context variant), the tier declared at spawn
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — the classifier `isAdmin = !looksLikeSlug(normalized)` (SlugEditLayer.vue:46) declares EVERY string that is not exactly four lowercase words an admin token, and the admin branch is destructive: useSlugMigration.ts:52-56 runs clearUserSlug() + adminLogin(garbage), which wipes `palette-user-slug` and the persisted session token (useUserAuth.ts:43-47) and flips the UI into admin mode (`isAuthenticated = !!adminToken`, useAdminAuth.ts:33). A one-word typo — or a single `"` character — permanently destroys the user's only handle on their account, with no error, no confirmation and no undo (the error surface is dead, C-3; the placeholder that would warn "or token" is clipped off-screen, C-6).

defects.defect: Inverted-default input classifier: anything that is not a 4-lowercase-word slug is treated as an ADMIN TOKEN and routed into the destructive admin branch, which clears the user's session identity.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:26,45-46,54 → demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:51-57 (`deps.clearUserSlug(); deps.adminLogin(value);`) → demo/platform/auth/useUserAuth.ts:43-47 (`clearAuth()` nulls the slug ref, removes `palette-user-slug`, clearPersistedToken()) and demo/platform/auth/useAdminAuth.ts:33-38 (`isAuthenticated = computed(() => !!adminToken.value)`). Server slugs are always 4 lowercase words (api/src/modules/session/slugWords.ts:83-89). Executed classifier table (17 inputs, verbatim transcription of lines 25-37/45-46): 'azure-flowing-jade' -> isAdmin true; 'azure-mist' -> true; 'azure--flowing-jade-otter' -> true; '"' -> normalizes to '' -> true; only exact 4-word forms -> false.
defects.mechanism: Overloaded single field with an inverted default — the classifier's UNKNOWN bucket is the DESTRUCTIVE action.
defects.reproduction: Open the dock Login layer, type `azure-flowing-jade` (one word dropped from a real slug) and press the → control. Executed: the classification half (node harness, output pasted in the report). NOT executed: the destructive half, deliberately — it would wipe the owner's live dev session; the chain is traced line-by-line instead.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the overload: this control accepts a SLUG only, validated against the one grammar the server mints, and refuses anything else in place with a rendered message. The admin token is an operator credential and belongs behind /#/admin/* in its own labelled field. If the overload must survive, invert the default — `isAdmin` becomes a POSITIVE test on the token grammar, never `!looksLikeSlug`.

defects.defect: The async port call is never awaited, so the try/catch is unreachable, the `slugSwitching` spinner and disabled-guard are never observably true, and the layer closes + clears itself before any outcome exists.
defects.evidence: SlugEditLayer.vue:42-65 calls `pm.onSlugSwitch(...)` (line 54) with no `await`; the target is `async function onSlugSwitch` at demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:51. Live WebKit probe with a MutationObserver on the form: {"t50":{"spinnerSeen":0,"spinnerInDom":false,"inputValue":"","faceActive":false},"after":{"spinnerSeen":0,"spinnerInDom":false},"dialogOpen":true,"net":[]} — at t+50ms the layer is already closed and the input cleared while ZERO network requests had fired and the port had merely opened the 'What about your palettes?' modal.
defects.mechanism: Fire-and-forget across an async boundary; the local UI state machine advances on CALL rather than on OUTCOME.
defects.reproduction: Live at http://localhost:9000: open the Login layer, submit any slug-shaped value, observe with a MutationObserver — `.animate-spin` never enters the DOM (0 insertions over 1.5s) and the face goes inactive at t+50ms with 0 network requests issued.
defects.proposedCure: `await pm.onSlugSwitch(...)` and close/clear only on success. The port must stop lying about its contract too: it resolves as soon as it opens a dialog, so it should return a discriminated result ({kind:'done'}|{kind:'awaiting-migration'}|{kind:'error',problem}) that this component renders.

defects.defect: `slugError` is written 6 times and rendered 0 times — the whole login error surface is dead, including the synchronous 'Already signed in.' path which makes the primary button a silent no-op.
defects.evidence: grep -n slugError SlugEditLayer.vue → lines 13,18,43,49,59,60,61,62 (all writes); `awk 'NR>=75' … | grep -c slugError` → 0 (template reads). The sibling path is dead by a second mechanism: useSlugMigration.ts:84-87 pushes into `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)` and `slugBarRef` is never bound to any template ref (grep -rn slugBarRef demo/ → declaration + return only); PaletteSlugBar is mounted nowhere. This overturns docs/tranches/S/audit/lanes/legacy-sweep-demo-components.md:239-245, which ruled the same catch block 'BEFITTING-KEEP … routes the error into a user-visible field'.
defects.mechanism: State written but never rendered — an error vocabulary with no output device; plus optional-chained routing into a ref that is never bound.
defects.reproduction: Submit your own slug (SlugEditLayer.vue:48-52 sets slugError='Already signed in.' synchronously and returns): the button press produces no message, no close, no spinner, no network — a fully silent dead end. Confirmed by grep (0 template reads) and by the live DOM having no error node in the dock.
defects.proposedCure: The layer owns a rendered role="status"/aria-live="polite" error slot (glass-ui already ships the register via Input invalid states / FeedbackMark), and the port returns its ApiProblem to the caller instead of pushing into a ref bound to a component that does not exist.

defects.defect: The retired `e.message.includes("409")` error idiom survives verbatim here after being cured in the sibling — dead branches plus a `catch (e: any)` in a strict repo.
defects.evidence: SlugEditLayer.vue:57-62 vs the ruling of record at demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:77-88: 'S.W2 W2-6: branch on the typed ApiProblem.status, not .message substrings — the server titles … never contain "409"/"404"/"429", so those branches matched nothing and the authored copy below never showed.'
defects.mechanism: Migration remnant that survived its own migration (edict 2, no legacy code); dead by two independent mechanisms (unreachable per C-2, non-matching per W2-6).
defects.reproduction: NONE needed — the branches are unreachable by construction (C-2) and, were they reached, provably non-matching per the W2-6 ruling quoted in the sibling file.
defects.proposedCure: Delete lines 57-62; errors arrive as typed ApiProblem from the awaited port (C-2's cure) and are rendered by status in the new error region (C-3's cure).

defects.defect: Three 22×22 controls and a 20-22px input — below the WCAG 2.5.8 24×24 floor — charged on every route because the layer is always mounted; this one component is 240 of the app's 398 small-tap-target defects.
defects.evidence: Live measurement with the layer ACTIVE at vw=1024 and vw=390: [{'label':'Switch to slug','w':22,'h':22,'pad':'4px','minW':'0px'},{'Generate new slug',22,22},{'Cancel',22,22}], input 160×21.5. Corpus arithmetic over docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json: 'total small tap targets across 60 captures: 398 / slug-layer attributable: 240 → 60.3%' (4 rows × 60 captures). Prior undischarged work order: docs/tranches/N/audit/lanes2/D5.md:50 measured the same 22×22, and docs/tranches/N/waves/N.W17.md:371 booked WO-D5-2 'hit-target floor on the 22/24px bespoke sites … under the WCAG 2.5.8 24px floor'.
defects.mechanism: Geometry authored per-instance (w-3.5 h-3.5 glyphs + 4px producer padding, min-width 0) under the design system's floor, on a layer that is never v-if'd out.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000 → dock Menu → Login → measure the three buttons' getBoundingClientRect: 22.0×22.0 at both 390px and 1024px viewports (pasted in the report).
defects.proposedCure: Per edicts 4+5 the floor belongs on the producer: `.dock-icon-button--compact` in glass-ui gets min-block-size/min-inline-size: 24px (or `--dock-compact-control-padding` is raised to clear it) so every compact consumer inherits it — never a per-instance class here. Relay to the glass-ui BH inbox per the standing fond.

defects.defect: The input has no accessible name (no label, no aria-label) and its only fallback name — the placeholder — is clipped 29% off the screen, hiding the very affordance ('or token') that makes C-1 destructive.
defects.evidence: Live: hasAriaLabel false, input.labels.length 0. Canvas metrology in the resolved font: {"font":"16.58px Fira Code…","placeholder":"enter slug or token...","placeholderWidthPx":224.5,"inputContentWidthPx":160,"overflowPx":64.5,"visiblePrefix":"enter slug or t","textOverflow":"clip"}. Screenshot evidence-slug-layer-open-1024.png (this directory) shows the field rendering 'enter slug or tc'. `w-40` is authored at SlugEditLayer.vue:85. At the measured 10.2px/char mono advance, a real 24-char slug needs ≈245px in a 160px box.
defects.mechanism: Fixed `w-40` box + placeholder-as-accessible-name; the label register the design system ships was bypassed by a hand-rolled input (already booked at docs/tranches/S/audit/lanes/glassui-consume-map.md:165,208).
defects.reproduction: Open the slug layer at any viewport and read the field — 'enter slug or t' is all that fits; measured 224.5px of text in a 160px content box.
defects.proposedCure: A real label via the glass-ui `Input` primitive (edict 4), `min-w-0 flex-1` instead of the fixed `w-40`, and a placeholder short enough for the narrowest aperture. If the token affordance survives C-1's cure at all it must be labelled, not smuggled into a truncated hint.

defects.defect: The open-focus is a race against reka-ui's dropdown close/focus-restore: about half of cold-load opens leave activeElement on BODY, so the caret is nowhere and the first keystrokes are lost. No focus restoration on close either.
defects.evidence: SlugEditLayer.vue:19-22 (`slugEditMode.value = true; nextTick(() => slugInputRef.value?.focus())`), entered from a reka DropdownMenu item (ProfileSection.vue:77 → Dock.vue:61). Four live cold-load trials sampling activeElement: A 30ms:INPUT…800ms:INPUT (lands); B 50ms:DIV(dropdown-menu-content) 150/300/600ms:BODY (lost); C same as B, then 2nd and 3rd opens on the same page land at 50ms. Losing-trial focusin log contains no INPUT entry within 400ms while the face is active and has no inert ancestor; `manualFocusWorks: true` at t+420 proves the element was focusable. Prior record: docs/tranches/A/audit/HARDEN-5-coverage-gaps.md:41-48 — 'SlugEditLayer.vue:21 … No focus trap, no focus restore-on-close.'
defects.mechanism: Single-nextTick imperative focus racing a foreign library's asynchronous focus restoration across a defineModel parent round-trip + a layer crossfade — the component cannot know when its own input became focusable.
defects.reproduction: Cold-load http://localhost:9000, dock Menu → Login, sample document.activeElement at 50/150/300/600ms: ~half of trials give DIV(dropdown-menu-content) then BODY, never the input (timelines pasted in the report).
defects.proposedCure: Bind focus to the layer's ARRIVAL rather than a guessed tick: an autofocus/@after-enter contract on the producer's DockLayer (the right home per edict 4), or locally a `watch(slugEditMode, …, {flush:'post'})` with a bounded retry until document.activeElement === el, plus an explicit restore of the prior activeElement on close.

defects.defect: Escape dismisses the layer only when the input happens to hold focus — the handler is bound to the input alone, and `.stop` blocks any ancestor fallback.
defects.evidence: SlugEditLayer.vue:86 `@keydown.escape.stop="slugEditMode = false"` on the <input>; the layer has four focusable controls. Live: focus the 'Generate new slug' control and dispatch Escape → {"escapeFromButton":{"btnFocused":true,"layerStillActive":true}}.
defects.mechanism: Dismissal bound to one element instead of the layer root; compounded by C-7 (in a lost-focus open, Escape is dead everywhere).
defects.reproduction: Open the layer, Tab or click to the ⟳ control, press Escape — the layer stays open (measured, pasted).
defects.proposedCure: Bind the key at the layer root, or better let the producer's DockLayer own dismissal for every layer — one grammar, one owner.

defects.defect: `void writeClipboard(...)` discards the library's CopyResult.ok, so a failed 'Copy slug' is silent — while the neighbouring 'Share color' row in the same menu shows a Copied! affordance.
defects.evidence: SlugEditLayer.vue:68-70. The library returns a result for exactly this: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts:35-37 — 'for identical call ergonomics: const { ok } = await writeClipboard(text)'. Asymmetry inside one menu: ProfileSection.vue:155-156 (Share color → linkCopied ? Check : Share2, 'Copied!') vs ProfileSection.vue:77-78 (Copy slug → this component, no feedback). Three siblings already use the right primitive: MixResultDisplay.vue:31, GradientEasingEditor.vue:94, App.vue:191.
defects.mechanism: Result of an async operation discarded (same family as C-2/C-3).
defects.reproduction: NONE executed (a clipboard denial needs a permission-denied context); the discarded return value is visible at the call site and the missing feedback is visible in ProfileSection's two adjacent rows.
defects.proposedCure: Use `useClipboard({ resetMs })` with a `status`, feeding the same Copied! affordance the neighbouring row already renders.

defects.defect: `onCopySlug` has nothing to do with slug EDITING; it lives in this layer because `pm` was in scope, and the dock reaches through defineExpose + an optional call to invoke it while the layer is not even displayed.
defects.evidence: SlugEditLayer.vue:68-72 and Dock.vue:62 `function onCopySlug() { slugEditRef.value?.onCopySlug(); }`, wired from ProfileSection.vue:77-78 / MobileMenuDropdown.
defects.mechanism: Cheapest-encapsulation break: behaviour homed where the injection already was, reached through a component instance ref that silently no-ops if null.
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural). The silent-no-op hazard is latent: add a v-if to the layer and copy-slug dies without a sound.
defects.proposedCure: Copy-slug is session-port behaviour: put `copySlug()` on the session port beside `userSlug` and let the menu that offers it call it directly. This layer then owns exactly one concern.

defects.defect: `defineExpose` publishes `slugSwitching`, which no caller reads and which (per C-2) is never observably true.
defects.evidence: SlugEditLayer.vue:72 `defineExpose({ onStartSlugEdit, onCopySlug, slugSwitching })`; Dock.vue:61-62 uses only the two functions.
defects.mechanism: Dead public API surface.
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural; grep of the sole consumer).
defects.proposedCure: Expose only what the parent calls; better, retire the imperative surface entirely by driving the layer from the model the parent already owns.

defects.defect: A pasted admin token survives dismissal: Escape and Cancel close the layer with the typed value intact in reactive state and in the DOM until the next open.
defects.evidence: `slugInput` is cleared only at SlugEditLayer.vue:17 (onStartSlugEdit) and :55 (successful submit); the Escape binding (:86) and the Cancel control (:115) only flip `slugEditMode`.
defects.mechanism: Clear-on-open instead of clear-on-close for a field whose documented purpose includes pasting a secret.
defects.reproduction: Type a token, press Cancel, inspect the (inert) input — the value is still there.
defects.proposedCure: Clear on close as well as on open; with C-1's cure the field stops carrying secrets at all.

defects.defect: Root-barrel import for a symbol the narrow subpath exports — line 6 pulls `@mkbabb/glass-ui` while line 4 correctly uses `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock`.
defects.evidence: SlugEditLayer.vue:4,6. The narrow path exists: `grep -o "export {[^}]*}" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/dom.js | tr ',' '\n' | grep -i clip` → ' o as useClipboard' / ' a as writeClipboard }'. Fleet-wide idiom (37 root-barrel imports under demo/).
defects.mechanism: Barrel import widening the dock chunk's module graph.
defects.reproduction: NONE (static).
defects.proposedCure: Fleet-level: move dom-composable imports to `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dom`. Not a single-file fix — recorded for the library seat.

defects.defect: Vacuous gate: the component has zero unit and zero e2e coverage, and the mutation that keeps every suite green destroys user accounts.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "SlugEditLayer\|Switch to slug\|Generate new slug\|enter slug or token\|slugEditMode\|onStartSlugEdit" test/ e2e/ | wc -l` → 0. `grep -rln "@vue/test-utils\|mount(" test/ demo/test/` → no output (no SFC mount test exists anywhere; vitest.config.ts:21 includes only test/**/*.ts and demo/test/**/*.ts). e2e/smoke/flows/login-register.spec.ts:6-8 states it deliberately tests a different surface. The only gate touching the file is the structural `expect(nav.locator('[title]')).toHaveCount(0)` at e2e/smoke/oracles/o15-dock-register.spec.ts:141, whose own comment (line 149) declares the slug layer out of scope.
defects.mechanism: No behavioural gate at any level — which is why C-1..C-9 have survived three tranches of audits and why the S-tranche marked C-3 'BEFITTING-KEEP'.
defects.reproduction: Mutation: replace `looksLikeSlug`'s body with `return false;`. Every login — including a perfectly typed slug — then runs clearUserSlug() + adminLogin(<the user's own slug>), and vitest (2222), vue-tsc, eslint and the full Playwright smoke suite all stay green, because nothing references this component's behaviour (proved by the zero-hit greps above).
defects.proposedCure: Lift `looksLikeSlug`/`normalizeTokenInput` into a pure module beside the port (they ARE the contract) and table-test them against generateSlug()'s grammar plus the malformed corpus; then one e2e leg: open the layer from the profile menu, submit a bad slug, assert a RENDERED error and that localStorage['palette-user-slug'] is unchanged.

result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Soundness checks that did pass, recorded in the report's negative-proof table: `type=\"submit\"` genuinely forwards through DockControl to the rendered <button type=submit> — matched live by form.querySelector('button[type=submit]'); no rAF/timers/observers/listeners, so no PRM-RAF hazard and nothing to clean up; no WebGL, no ValueUnit, no oklch/HSV, no reka slider — those local hazards are N/A here; no read-after-write on the defineModel; useTemplateRef matches ref=\"slugInputRef\" (edict 7 met on that axis); no type-only import needed (edict 8 met); the always-mounted inactive layer IS inert + aria-hidden=\"true\" so it does not leak into the tab order or the a11y tree; pageOverflowX measured 0 at 390 and 1024 with the layer open; no <style> block, so edict 6 is untouched.)

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model ID `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M context). Declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the failure state does not exist. A rejected slug login produces zero feedback anywhere in the document: the layer closes synchronously, `slugError` is written in four places and rendered in none, the catch block is unreachable (un-awaited port call), and the real error copy is posted to `PaletteSlugBar`, a component that is exported from two barrels and rendered by nothing. Live: type `brave-swift-red-fox`, press the arrow — `errorCopyVisible: []`, `loginButtonStillThere: true`.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this field records what was interrogated and found SOUND, so a later seat does not re-litigate it. (1) The inert layer does not leak: inactive `.dock-face` measures `{inert:true, ariaHidden:"true", opacity:"0", pointerEvents:"none"}`, `checkVisibility({checkOpacity:true}) === false` — the slug rows in `audit/visual/REPORT.json` are an artifact of that harness's nonzero-rect filter (`capture.mjs:83-98`), not a live defect. (2) The hidden layer does not inflate the dock: intrinsic max-content widths slug 285 vs main 447.5, group measures 447.5 — main governs. (3) Tab order inside the active layer is correct (chromium): input → Switch to slug → Generate new slug → Cancel, all `:focus-visible` with a painted 2px ring (`ring-focused.png` vs `ring-unfocused.png`). (4) 200% zoom is sound: `documentElement.style.zoom=2` gives input 320×45.9, controls 44×44, `overflowX: 0`. (5) `prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured globally — `.animate-spin` in the dock subtree computes `{animationDuration:"1e-05s", iterationCount:"1"}` under `reducedMotion: reduce`; the animation is transform-only, no layout thrash, and nothing was deleted (edict 6 satisfied). (6) Mobile focus handoff works (`isInput:true` at 100/400/1200ms) — the drop is desktop-only. (7) Mobile never auto-collapses (`always-expanded="!isDesktop"`), so D-2 is desktop-only. (8) Zero console/page errors from this component in all five arms (`pageErrors: []`). (9) Type jurisdiction is correct — `text-mono-small`/Fira Code on a slug matches VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4 "value, code, or provenance". (10) Micro-rhythm is systematic: form gap 6px = parent DockLayer gap 6px; glyphs vertically centred at a symmetric 4px inset. (11) `useTemplateRef` used idiomatically (`:14`) and all type-only imports are `import type` — edicts 7 and 8 satisfied. (12) MT-F004 as briefed is overstated: WCAG 2.5.8's spacing exception rescues AA conformance (measured centre distances 47/28 desktop, 50.4/30.4 mobile, all ≥24) — I concur with the sibling library seat's correction; the design defect (D-7) survives that correction on different grounds.

defects.defect: The failure state does not exist. A rejected login says nothing, anywhere — no error copy, no status region, no live announcement, no visual delta at all.
defects.evidence: Live repro output (probe2 §A4): `{"alerts":["dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`"],"errorCopyVisible":[],"slugLayerStillActive":false,"inputValue":"","loginButtonStillThere":true}`. Source: `demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:13` declares `slugError`, `:49,:59,:60,:61,:62` write it, template `:75-119` references it ZERO times. `:54` calls `pm.onSlugSwitch(...)` un-awaited; `demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:51-89` catches its own failures internally so `:57`'s catch is unreachable. `useSlugMigration.ts:84-87` routes 409/404/429/other into `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)`; `grep -rn "PaletteSlugBar" demo` returns barrel exports only (`browser/index.ts:44`, `browser/slug/index.ts:3`) and NO template usage, so `slugBarRef` is permanently null. The only rendered error region in the repo is `demo/palettes/browser/slug/PaletteSlugBar.vue:124-125`, in that unmounted component.
defects.mechanism: State-without-surface: the error state was authored in script and never given a rendered region, then its data path was re-routed to a component that is not mounted. Compounded by the layer self-dismissing at `:56` in the same synchronous tick the request is fired, so even a correct region would be unmounted before the outcome arrives.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/ at 1440x900 → click `Login` → type `brave-swift-red-fox` → click `Switch to slug` → wait 2.5s. The dock returns to its pre-login appearance, still signed out, with no statement of what happened.
