defects.proposedCure: Architectural, not a patch: retire the dock layer and move sign-in into the Account Dialog that VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 already assigns to W23, where an error region, a pending region and a real field all have room. Delete `useSlugMigration`'s `slugBarRef` limb and the unmounted `PaletteSlugBar` with it so exactly one error owner exists. Minimum honest in-place repair: await the port, keep the layer mounted until it resolves, render one `role="status"` region under the field.

defects.defect: The dock auto-collapses out from under the user mid-edit after 5 seconds of idle, expelling focus and discarding the typed slug.
defects.evidence: `demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:86` — `shouldKeepOpen = actionBarLayerActive || anyEditActive || isAnyOpen`; `slugEditMode` is NOT a driver. `Dock.vue:132` `:collapse-delay="5000"`. Measured (slug-probe6): `t=4000ms {slugFaceActive:true, faceOpacity:"1", groupW:285}` → `t=6000ms {slugFaceActive:false, faceOpacity:"0", groupW:56, sealVisible:true}` with `value:"brave-swift-red-fox"` still in the detached DOM. Inactive faces measure `{inert:true, ariaHidden:"true"}`, so focus is expelled. `Dock.vue:76` then clears `slugEditMode`; re-opening runs `SlugEditLayer.vue:16-17` whose first statement is `slugInput.value = ""`.
defects.mechanism: A text-entry surface hosted inside an idle-collapsing container that never registers itself as a keep-open driver. The authors wrote a cleanup watcher for the collapse (`Dock.vue:76`) instead of a hold — i.e. the collapse was known and the data loss was not.
defects.reproduction: 1440x900 → `Login` → type `brave-swift-red-fox` → move the pointer away from the dock → wait. Between 4s and 6s the dock collapses to the 56px wax seal; the input is gone and the value is discarded on re-open. Desktop only (`always-expanded="!isDesktop"` exempts mobile; measured 8s idle at 390/320 leaves it intact).
defects.proposedCure: The producer already exposes the right primitive — GlassDock's ref-counted `keepOpen()/release()` pair, which `Dock.vue:87` already drives. Add `slugEditMode` to the `shouldKeepOpen` disjunction at `Dock.vue:86`. One word. (Moot under the gestalt cure — a Dialog does not evaporate on a wall-clock timer.)

defects.defect: The field is optically absent in every state including focus, and its only label — the placeholder — is truncated mid-word in every viewport.
defects.evidence: Rendered frames show `enter slug or to` (1440 light AND dark) and `enter slug or toker` (390, 320) against the authored `enter slug or token...` (`SlugEditLayer.vue:84`). Arithmetic: Fira Code advance 0.6em; measured font-size 16.4px desktop → 9.84px/char × 22 chars = 216.5px required vs `w-40` = 160px measured; ⌊160/9.84⌋ = 16 chars predicts `enter slug or to` exactly; mobile 14px → ⌊160/8.40⌋ = 19 chars predicts `enter slug or toker` exactly. Field styling measured: `border-width:0px`, `background-color:rgba(0,0,0,0)`, `outline-style:none`, `box-shadow:none`, `::before/::after content:none`, `min-height:auto`, padding 0 → height 22.9px desktop / 19.6px mobile is pure line-box. Focus proof: `shots/input-unfocused.png` ≡ `shots/input-focused.png` after an 800ms settle with `:focus-visible === true`; webkit pre/post computed-style snapshot returns `{"same":true,"activeIsInput":true}`. Accessible name: `{ariaLabel:null, id:"", hasLabelEl:false, labelledBy:null}` — matches REPORT.json's `{"w":160,"h":23,"tag":"input","label":""}`. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 ("Focus remains visibly distinct… in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency") and WCAG 2.4.7.
defects.mechanism: A hand-rolled `<input>` carrying `bg-transparent border-none outline-none w-40` (`SlugEditLayer.vue:85`) deletes boundary, fill and focus ring with nothing put back, and fixes a width that was never held up against the string it must hold. The donor twin uses `enter slug...` (13 chars, fits) inside a composed `SearchBar` (`PaletteSlugBar.vue:5-12`).
defects.reproduction: Open the layer at 1440x900 → read the dock: the label reads `enter slug or to`. Blur, screenshot, focus the input, wait 800ms, screenshot again — the two crops are identical.
defects.proposedCure: Consume the design system's field primitive: `<Input>` from `demo/ui/input` (a one-line re-export of `@mkbabb/glass-ui/forms`), or the `SearchBar` + `:icon` composition the twin already uses. Promote the placeholder to a real label; the placeholder then carries an example, not the name.

defects.defect: At the canonical 320px arm the Cancel and Generate controls are rendered outside the dock's visible aperture; at their own geometric centres the hit test returns the band behind or nothing.
defects.evidence: slug-probe7 at vw=320, layer active: `cancel rect 314.8…338.1 centre 326.4 insideViewport:false elementFromPoint → null`; `regen rect 284.4…307.8 centre 296.1 elementFromPoint → nav.dock-band`. Scroll host `.dock-layer--full` measures `scrollWidth 295 / clientWidth 234` — 61px beyond the port. At 390 it is already over: `scrollWidth 295 / clientWidth 290`. Frame: `shots/narrow-320-slug-active.png` shows the pill ending after the submit arrow with `↻`/`✕` absent. 320px is a binding arm per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.2 and PROPORTION-AUDIT §2.
defects.mechanism: A fixed 160px field plus five controls at a fixed 6px rhythm produces a 285px intrinsic layer that was never sized against the dock aperture it must live in. The producer's overflow track engages (`[data-dock-overflow]` present) so it degrades to horizontal scroll rather than a hard trap — but the degraded control is the only exit on a touch device, where there is no Escape key (`SlugEditLayer.vue:86` is the sole other dismissal) and the dock never auto-collapses.
defects.reproduction: 320x720, touch context → open the Menu → `Login` → attempt to tap the ✕. Its centre is off-screen; a horizontal swipe inside the 46px pill is required to reach it.
defects.proposedCure: Remove the form from the aperture entirely (the Dialog transposition). If the layer survives review, the field must be fluid (`min-w-0` with a flexible basis) rather than a fixed `w-40`, and the layer must be measured against the 320 arm the constitution names.

defects.defect: The open transition drops focus on the floor on desktop, and closing never restores it to the opener.
defects.evidence: slug-probe5 §C, after clicking `Login` at 1440x900: `focus @50ms {"active":"div[]","isInput":false}`, `@300ms` same, `@1000ms` same — focus rests on an unnamed `<div>` (the dock face container). Mobile is the opposite: `B. mobile focus @100ms {"isInput":true}`. Escape (probe2 §A3): `{"active":"div[HomeToolsPickerAbout]","isBody":false,"layerActive":false}` — a container div, not the `Login` button. `docs/tranches/A/audit/HARDEN-5-coverage-gaps.md:45` booked this against `SlugEditLayer.vue:21` ("No focus trap, no focus restore-on-close") and it is still open.
defects.mechanism: `onStartSlugEdit` (`SlugEditLayer.vue:20-22`) focuses on `nextTick`, which fires while the incoming `.dock-face` is still `inert` during the crossfade, so `.focus()` is a silent no-op with no retry. The layer behaves as an overlay (it marks every sibling face `inert` + `aria-hidden="true"`) while implementing none of the overlay focus contract in VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.1 ("producer initial-focus rule on open; exact connected opener on close").
defects.reproduction: 1440x900 → click `Login` → check `document.activeElement`: an anonymous `div`, never the input. Then press Escape from the input: focus lands on another anonymous div, not the `Login` button.
defects.proposedCure: A Dialog gets initial-focus and opener-restore from the producer for free; that is the cure. In-place, the focus handoff must wait for the face's settle seam (the same `transitionend`/`.is-settled` stamp the dock already uses at `Dock.vue:76`'s sibling machinery) rather than `nextTick`, and dismissal must return focus to the connected opener.

defects.defect: One undifferentiated field carries two authorities — user slug and admin token — with no mode indication, and renders the elevated secret in plaintext in the persistent top band.
defects.evidence: `SlugEditLayer.vue:25-27` `looksLikeSlug()` is a four-word-lowercase regex; `:46` `const isAdmin = !looksLikeSlug(normalized)` — anything that is not four hyphenated lowercase words is treated as an admin token and passed to `pm.onSlugSwitch(..., true)` at `:54`. Field config measured: `{type:"text", autocomplete:null, spellcheck:null, inputmode:null, name:null}`. Frame `shots/desktop-light-slug-long.png` shows `ADMIN_TOKEN=a-ve` rendered unmasked in the dock; `scrollWidth 749 / clientWidth 160` — silently clipped with no ellipsis, fade or boundary. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 Admin: "Elevated authority is communicated by labeling and scope, not by a fourth visual system"; §7 Account: "secret retention temporarily replaces its action region".
defects.mechanism: Two acts with different consequences share one affordance, discriminated by an invisible regex. The design provides no mode selector, no state indication and no secret treatment, so authority elevation is indistinguishable from ordinary sign-in both before and after the fact.
defects.reproduction: Open the layer at 1440x900 and paste `ADMIN_TOKEN=a-very-long-administrative-secret-token-value-0123456789abcdef`. The secret renders as plaintext in the top band, clipped mid-string with no visible field edge.
defects.proposedCure: Split the two authorities into two affordances inside the Account Dialog, per canon: slug sign-in as the primary path with a real label, admin elevation as a scoped, labelled, masked field whose region communicates the elevation. Delete the regex-as-mode-switch.

defects.defect: `compact` discards the producer's own hit-cell guarantee, shipping 23.3px targets on coarse pointers where glass-ui guarantees ≥44px.
defects.evidence: `SlugEditLayer.vue:92,105,113` all pass `compact`. Producer contract, `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/DockControl.vue.d.ts`: "the painted plate insets via the dock-scoped `--dock-control-safe-inset` fold, while the HIT CELL stays the full `--dock-control-size` (≥44px on coarse via the density clamp) — hit box ≠ paint box", and `compact?: boolean` — "Compact icon variant: auto-sized instead of fixed square". Measured: 22.0×22.0 at 1440; **23.3×23.3** at 390 and 320 touch contexts = 53% of the producer's coarse floor. Register provenance: `docs/tranches/N/audit/lanes2/D5.md:50` ("Slug-edit layer buttons | 22×22"), `D5.md:92` ("move to `DockIconButton compact` minimum 28px"), `docs/tranches/N/waves/N.W17.md:371` (WO-D5-2) — ruled twice, executed zero times.
defects.mechanism: The producer already implements PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-12 ("Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities") by separating paint box from hit box. `compact` opts out of that separation and collapses the hit cell onto the paint box, defeating the density clamp on exactly the pointer class the clamp exists for.
defects.reproduction: 390x844 touch context → open the Menu → `Login` → measure `getBoundingClientRect()` on the three controls: 23.3×23.3 each. At `zoom:2` on desktop the same controls measure 44×44, proving 22px is a choice, not a constraint.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the word `compact` three times. The producer's default is the design. (Honest scope: WCAG 2.5.8's spacing exception rescues AA conformance — measured centre distances 47/28 desktop and 50.4/30.4 mobile, all ≥24 — so MT-F004 is not an AA failure here, per the sibling library seat's correction; the defect is the defeated producer guarantee, not the WCAG number.)

defects.defect: The pending state is structurally unreachable, and the disabled state is opacity-only.
defects.evidence: Pending: `SlugEditLayer.vue:97` renders `Loader2` on `slugSwitching`, but `:42` sets it true, `:54` fires an un-awaited promise and `:64`'s `finally` sets it false — all in one synchronous execution, so Vue never paints between. MutationObserver armed across the whole submit (probe2 §A5): `{"sawSpinner":false,"spinnersNow":0}`. Disabled: measured `disabled {opacity:"0.5", color:"color(srgb 0 0 0 / 0.8)", bg:"rgba(0,0,0,0)", boxShadow:"none", cursor:"default"}` vs `enabled {opacity:"1", color:"color(srgb 0 0 0 / 0.8)", bg:"rgba(0,0,0,0)", cursor:"pointer"}` — the entire rendered difference is alpha 0.5 vs 1.0. Under forced-colors the disabled control still measures `opacity: "0.5"` with `forced-color-adjust: auto`, so opacity (not a forced-colors property) survives and the rescue mode does not rescue it. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 "Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only."
defects.mechanism: A pending affordance authored against an imagined `await` that was never written — the state exists in the diff as reassurance and cannot exist at runtime. The disabled treatment is a post-hoc alpha attenuation, the degenerate case of color-only state.
defects.reproduction: Open the layer, fill the input, arm a MutationObserver for `.animate-spin`, click `Switch to slug`, wait 1.2s: the spinner is never inserted. Separately, screenshot the submit control empty vs filled: the only delta is opacity.
defects.proposedCure: Await the port so the pending state can exist, and give disabled a non-alpha channel (shape/boundary/glyph change) at the producer root so every `DockControl` inherits it — not a per-instance override here.

defects.defect: The surface is a constitutional orphan: canon assigns sign-in to the Account Dialog owned by W23, not to a dock layer — and hosting it in the dock is the common cause of six other findings.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 Account: "Account is one modal side Dialog opened from the Dock, not a route chassis or second main. It owns registration/recovery when signed out… secret retention temporarily replaces its action region… W23 owns the rendered composition and journey while W15 supplies auth/outbox state." Measured cost of the dock hosting: activating the layer marks every sibling `.dock-face` `{inert:true, ariaHidden:"true", opacity:"0"}`, so route selector, Tools and profile all vanish for the duration — against §7 Shell: "Direct route changes keep its full navigation identity." Layer intrinsic width 285px (2nd widest of four) inside an aperture that measures `clientWidth 290` at 390 and `234` at 320.
defects.mechanism: A fragment of `PaletteSlugBar.vue` was transplanted into the dock without its field primitive, error region, state-bearing accessible names or content-fitted placeholder. D-1 (no room for an error region), D-3 (no room for a real field), D-5 (no overlay focus contract), D-6 (no secret region), D-2/D-8 (no persistence) are not five independent oversights — they are five things a Dialog supplies and a 46px inert-able strip of navigation chrome cannot.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a canon-conformance judgement, not a runtime failure. Its consequences are the reproductions in D-1..D-8.
defects.proposedCure: Retire the component. The dock keeps one control (`Login` / the slug pill) that opens the Account Dialog; the `slug-edit` DockLayer, `Dock.vue`'s `slugEditRef`/`onStartSlugEdit`/`onCopySlug` three-hop round-trip and the `activeLayer` branch die together. The Dialog composes the field from glass-ui, gives the two authorities two affordances, owns one `role="status"` error region, and awaits the port so pending is real. Delete `useSlugMigration`'s `slugBarRef` limb and the unmounted `PaletteSlugBar` in the same cut.

defects.defect: RTL: the submit arrow does not mirror and the slug value is not direction-isolated.
defects.evidence: Measured with `dir="rtl"`, value `brave-swift-red-fox`: `{"direction":"rtl","textAlign":"start","unicodeBidi":"normal"}` on the input; row order mirrors correctly (loginIcon x=846.5 → input 680.5…840.5 → submit 652.5 → cancel 577.5). Glyphs are hard-coded physical directions: `SlugEditLayer.vue:98` `ArrowRight` (submit) and `:80` `LogIn` (also a right-pointing arrow). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1: "CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance | render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose"; §5.2 last row repeats it for `slug`.
defects.mechanism: The layout mirrors because the producer's flex is logical; the iconography and the value's bidi context were never given a direction jurisdiction, so a right-pointing arrow reads as "back" in RTL and a latin slug inherits RTL paragraph direction.
defects.reproduction: 1440x900 → set `document.documentElement.dir = "rtl"` → open the layer → type a slug. The submit arrow points away from the reading direction; the input computes `direction: rtl` with `unicode-bidi: normal` and no `dir="ltr"`.
defects.proposedCure: Mirror the directional action glyph with the document direction (or use a non-directional commit affordance), and give the slug/token value an explicit `dir="ltr"` isolation as §6.1 requires for slugs and IDs.

defects.defect: Under forced colors the field has no boundary to force, so it disappears entirely.
defects.evidence: Chromium `forcedColors: "active"`, layer active, input measured: `{color:"rgb(0,0,0)", bg:"rgba(255,255,255,0)", border:"none 0px rgb(0,0,0)", opacity:"1", forcedColorAdjust:"auto"}`. Frame `shots/fc-slug.png`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: "Focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency."
defects.mechanism: Forced-colors normally rescues a text field by forcing its border to the system `ButtonBorder`. `border-none` (`SlugEditLayer.vue:85`) removes the border box, so there is nothing for the forced palette to paint — and per D-3 there is no focus ring either.
defects.reproduction: Launch chromium with `forcedColors: "active"` → open the layer → the input has no boundary, no fill and no focus ring; it is an unmarked run of text on the band.
defects.proposedCure: Same as D-3 — consume the glass-ui field primitive, which carries a real border box that forced-colors can repaint.

defects.defect: Register incoherence: four glyph scales across the dock's four layers, two identical right-arrows 170px apart meaning different things, an unhidden decorative glyph larger than the actions beside it, and two colliding `Cancel` names.
defects.evidence: Measured glyph boxes in this one 210px form: `LogIn` 16×16 (`SlugEditLayer.vue:80`, `w-4`) vs `ArrowRight`/`RefreshCw`/`X` 14×14 (`:98,:109,:117`, `w-3.5`). Across layers: 14 here, 20 at `Dock.vue:143-144` (`w-5`), 24 at `Dock.vue:154` (`w-6`) — a 71% scale swing with no change of meaning. Both svgs measure `{ariaHidden:null, role:null}` live, while the donor twin sets `aria-hidden="true"` on all three of its glyphs (`PaletteSlugBar.vue:26,27,38`). Names: `aria-label="Cancel"` (`:114`) shares a dock with `aria-label="Cancel edit"` (`Dock.vue:144`); the twin said `Cancel slug edit` (`PaletteSlugBar.vue:35`) and made submit state-bearing — `:aria-label="slugSwitching ? 'Signing in…' : 'Sign in with slug'"` (`:24`). PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.5 forbids unnamed decorative marks; §5.8 "Real rendered relation wins over token intent".
defects.mechanism: Per-instance glyph sizing chosen layer-by-layer with no shared rung, and accessible names degraded during the transplant from the donor surface.
defects.reproduction: Open the layer at 1440x900 and measure the svg rects: 16,14,14,14. Switch to the action-bar layer: 24. Switch to the mobile-edit layer: 20.
defects.proposedCure: One dock glyph rung at the producer root (the `--dock-icon-glyph` hook already exists per `N.W17.md:371`), `aria-hidden` on decorative marks, and scoped, state-bearing accessible names restored from the twin.

defects.defect: Design-system boundary crossed at the field, plus resurrected legacy the repo already proved dead — both booked in earlier tranches and never closed.
defects.evidence: `SlugEditLayer.vue:85` hand-rolls `class="text-mono-small bg-transparent border-none outline-none w-40 min-w-0 placeholder:text-muted-foreground"` while `demo/ui/input/index.ts` re-exports glass-ui's `Input` from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/forms` and four surfaces already consume it (`AdminTagsPanel.vue:115`, `AdminAuditPanel.vue:97`, `CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:174`, `SearchFilterBar.vue:130`). Booked at `docs/tranches/S/audit/lanes/glassui-consume-map.md:165` and `:208` (P1), and deferred at `docs/tranches/S/audit/pi/w5a-after/DELTA.md:50` ("`SlugEditLayer.vue:81` (dock — W7's per §File bounds)"); W7 came and went. Separately `:57-62` catches `e: any` and branches on `msg.includes("409"|"404"|"429")` — the exact idiom `demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:78-82` documents as already proven dead ("the server titles… never contain '409'/'404'/'429', so those branches matched nothing and the authored copy below never showed").
defects.mechanism: Owner edict 4 (glass-ui is the design system) and edict 5 (style at the root, never per-instance) violated in one attribute — and `border-none outline-none` is the precise per-instance override that produces D-3 and D-10. Owner edict 2 (no legacy code) violated by a copy of a known-dead error idiom that was corrected next door and left uncorrected here.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the styling row (static, file:line). The dead-branch row is reproducible as D-1: no status-derived copy ever renders.
defects.proposedCure: Replace the raw `<input>` with `<Input>` (or the twin's `SearchBar` + `:icon` composition) so boundary, focus ring and forced-colors behaviour come from the root, and delete the `catch (e: any)` substring-matching block outright rather than porting it — the typed `ApiProblem.status` path already exists.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/shell/dock/menus/ProfileSection.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context variant) — the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with; declaration honoured, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — the live "chrome" surface probe in demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:151-153 reads getComputedStyle(".glass-dock").backgroundColor, which glass-ui 7 leaves at rgba(0,0,0,0) because the band is painted on a child .dock-plate. The probe therefore returns undefined permanently and the static producer model in demo/color-session/ink.ts:118-122 serves — a model whose "chrome" case body is byte-identical to "floating", so ProfileSection's two-referent D6 apparatus (lines 22-31) is provably inert. The demo models the dock band at alpha 0.88 while the real painted plate measures alpha 0.4544 (glass-ui already publishes the correct --glass-bg-dock token at 0.52). Delivered contrast misses the 5.75 design target in both schemes: 5.365 light, 8.259 dark. Root cause is a boundary defect — value.js's demo owns a reverse-engineered replica of glass-ui's paint model.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (The one clean sub-claim: this component's transitive reach into @mkbabb/value.js is entirely through real published subpath keys — ink.ts:1-11 uses @mkbabb/value.js/color and @mkbabb/value.js/css, both present in package.json#exports; `grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/value.js"' demo/ src/` returns zero bare-root imports and no demo file on this graph reaches src/ internals.)

defects.defect: The live "chrome" ink probe is permanently dead, collapsing ProfileSection's two ink referents into one, and the fallback static model misstates glass-ui's dock band by 0.4256 absolute alpha. The demo owns a reverse-engineered replica of the design system's paint model.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:151-153 probes document.querySelector('.glass-dock') → getComputedStyle().backgroundColor. Measured live at localhost:9000 (Chromium 1440x900): dockBgRead = "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)"; the band is painted by child .dock-plate = "oklab(0.946496 0.00678277 0.0150976 / 0.808)". Producer source node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/dock.css: `.dock-plate { position:absolute; inset:0; z-index:-1; background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--glass-bg-dock, var(--glass-bg-resting)), var(--glass-tint-source) var(--glass-tint-strength)); }`. alpha===0 → useContrastSafeColor.ts:217 returns undefined → static model demo/color-session/ink.ts:118-122 where `case "floating": case "chrome":` share ONE body. Dark-scheme live probe: --glass-bg-dock alpha 0.52, --glass-bg-floating alpha 0.88, real .dock-plate alpha 0.4544; ink.ts:31 RUNG_ALPHA.floating.dark = 0.88 → error 0.4256. Composited-L error (node against local dist): light MODEL 0.9397 vs REAL 0.8791 (+0.0606); dark MODEL 0.3251 vs REAL 0.3416 (-0.0165). Delivered contrast vs the 5.75 target (ink.ts:15-17, 4.5+1.25): light 5.365, dark 8.259.
defects.mechanism: wrong-owner / consumer models producer internals — value.js's demo maintains a hand-copy of glass-ui's material-ladder recipe (ink.ts RUNG_ALPHA/FLOATING_TINT_L/CARD_L) plus a DOM scraper for glass-ui's private class names and custom properties (useContrastSafeColor.ts TIER_BG_TOKEN/resolveLiveTint). glass-ui owns the paint, so glass-ui owns the composited lightness; the replica goes stale on every producer refactor, silently.
defects.reproduction: Dev server live at http://localhost:9000/#/. In the console: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.glass-dock')).backgroundColor → "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)"; getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.dock-plate')).backgroundColor → the actual painted band. Reproducing useContrastSafeColor's resolveCssColorAlpha on the first value yields alpha 0 → the resolver's undefined branch.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition: glass-ui exports `resolveRungLightness(rung: GlassRung, ambientL: number): number` from @mkbabb/glass-ui/tokens — the package that paints the rung resolves the rung's composited lightness from its own element and its own token. Delete from the demo: ink.ts:24-36 (PRODUCER_TINTS, RUNG_ALPHA, FLOATING_TINT_L, WELL_FOREGROUND_FRACTION), ink.ts:93-127 (resolveSurfaceLightness), useContrastSafeColor.ts:50-54 (TIER_BG_TOKEN), :80-221 (the whole canvas/probe instrument), :234-251 (liveTintCache). ~200 demo lines become one producer call; useContrastSafeColor shrinks 376 → ~40 lines. File as mark M2 on the glass-ui BH relay alongside the existing M1 passive-DarkModeToggle ask.

defects.defect: Dock.vue feeds the already-resting-certified accent into a prop named `cssColorOpaque`, so ProfileSection certifies an already-certified colour a second time against a different surface. Two owners of one concept, composed in series, with the name lying about which is which.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:34 `const cssColorOpaque = inject(CSS_COLOR_KEY)!` (the raw colour, available), :35 `const safeAccent = inject(SAFE_ACCENT_KEY)!` (= certifyAccentInk(raw, resting), useContrastSafeColor.ts:302-311), :220 `:css-color-opaque="safeAccent"`. ProfileSection.vue:30-31 then applies chromeSafeCss/floatingSafeCss. Measured against the local dist (ambient L 0.62, light), certify(raw,chrome) vs certify(certify(raw,resting),chrome) over 5 probe colours: DIRECT 5.751/5.750/5.752/5.750/5.750 vs ACTUAL 7.262/7.262/7.262/7.262/7.269 — +26.3% over the 5.75 design target on every colour. Live confirmation of the short-circuit case: Login trigger computed color "oklch(0.454991 0.15 30)" is byte-identical to --accent-live "oklch(45.499144080095% 0.15 30deg)" — the ink painted on the dock band IS the resting-plate ink; the surface-specific certification never fires. Same defect reaches MobileMenuDropdown.vue:24 via Dock.vue:209.
defects.mechanism: wrong referent crossing a component boundary + duplicated ownership of "certified ink" — the prop's name asserts the raw opaque colour while the wiring supplies a derived, already-guarded value, so the guard runs twice against two different surfaces.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/ with the dock visible; in the console compare getComputedStyle(<Login button>).color against getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--accent-live') — structurally equal, proving the chrome certification was a no-op on an input that was already resting-certified. Static path is unambiguous from Dock.vue:220 → ProfileSection.vue:30.
defects.proposedCure: Dock.vue:209,220 pass `cssColorOpaque`, not `safeAccent`. Better: ProfileSection stops taking the colour as a prop entirely and injects CSS_COLOR_KEY itself (it already injects SESSION_PORT_KEY, so the prop buys no decoupling). One raw referent in, exactly one certification per surface that actually paints.

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is nineteen directories of pure re-export alias over @mkbabb/glass-ui — a shadow shadcn namespace, a live dual path, and a root-barrel detour past thirteen dedicated glass-ui subpath exports.
defects.evidence: Every demo/ui/*/index.ts is a bare re-export, e.g. demo/ui/button/index.ts = `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`, demo/ui/avatar/index.ts, demo/ui/dropdown-menu/index.ts (14 names). Measured: 48 demo files import through the shim, 79 import glass-ui directly (37 root-barrel + 42 subpath across 17 subpaths). Against node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json#exports, 13 shims have a matching subpath (badge button card collapsible dialog dropdown-menu label popover select separator slider switch tooltip) and 6 do not (alert avatar checkbox input radio-group skeleton). ProfileSection.vue speaks three dialects in one file: subpath at :6 and :8, shim→root-barrel at :7 and :12, shim→root-barrel-with-no-alternative at :13.
defects.mechanism: legacy alias layer / dual path — a migration-era shadcn namespace kept alive as pass-through indirection after glass-ui became the design system, violating the no-aliases and glass-ui-is-the-design-system edicts simultaneously.
defects.reproduction: `for d in demo/ui/*/; do cat "$d/index.ts"; done` — every file is a single re-export line with zero added behaviour. `node -e "const e=require('./node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json').exports; e['./button']"` confirms the bypassed subpath exists.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ whole; rewrite the 48 consumers to the producer's own specifiers. ProfileSection lines 7/12/13 become `import { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/button"`, `import { DropdownMenu, … } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dropdown-menu"`, `import { Avatar, AvatarImage } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"`. File the six missing subpaths (avatar, alert, checkbox, input, radio-group, skeleton) as mark M3 on the glass-ui BH relay — six one-line exports-map additions close the last root-barrel reach.

defects.defect: Wrong direction of dependency: the shell imports a feature to learn who is logged in. Five demo/shell files reach into demo/palettes/usePalettePorts for a session-identity key whose implementation lives in demo/platform/auth.
defects.evidence: ProfileSection.vue:14 `import { SESSION_PORT_KEY } from "../../../palettes/usePalettePorts";`. demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts is 275 lines statically importing 15 palette composables (lines 4-18: usePaletteStore, useBrowsePalettes, useAdminUsers, useColorNameQueue, useSlugMigration, usePaletteActions, useFilteredList, useAdminAudit, useAdminFlagged, useAdminTags, useVersionHistory, useTagEdit). ProfileSection needs one Symbol() (:271) and one type. The identity implementation is imported by that same file from elsewhere — usePalettePorts.ts:5-7: useAdminAuth/useUserAuth/useSession from ../platform/auth/. Five shell files take the edge: Dock.vue:18, DockViewSelect.vue:8, layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:5, menus/ProfileSection.vue:14, menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue:13.
defects.mechanism: wrong home for a shared concept — session identity is a platform service re-exported by a feature, so the chrome layer (shell) is forced to depend on a feature layer to reach the platform layer; layering runs shell → feature → platform instead of shell → platform.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "SESSION_PORT_KEY" demo/` — 5 shell consumers, provider and key both in demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:242,271, while the underlying auth composables are in demo/platform/auth/.
defects.proposedCure: Move SESSION_PORT_KEY and the SessionPort type to demo/platform/auth/session-port.ts. usePalettePorts imports the key like every other consumer and provides it. Zero behaviour change; the edge inverts to shell → platform, and demo/palettes stops being on the shell's static module graph.

defects.defect: Every demo import-boundary lint rule globs directories that no longer exist, so the demo module lattice has zero structural enforcement — which is why L-4 passes CI clean.
defects.evidence: eslint.config.js carries four no-restricted-imports objects globbing demo/@/components/**, demo/@/lib/**, demo/@/composables/** and demo/color-picker/**. Measured: `for d in demo/@ demo/@/components demo/@/lib demo/@/composables; do [ -d "$d" ]; done` → GONE for all four (deleted by the W43/RF-15 restructure; the tree is now demo/{shell,palettes,color-session,platform,picker,workbenches,scenes,ui,shared,styles}). The one surviving object bans `@components/custom/palette-browser/**/*.vue` — `grep -c "@components" vite.config.ts` → 0 (the alias was killed; tsconfig.demo.json's single occurrence is a comment recording the removal). Confirmed: `npx eslint demo/shell/dock/menus/ProfileSection.vue demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue` → ESLINT-EXIT=0 with the shell→palettes edge present.
defects.mechanism: dead structural enforcement — the guardrails were written against a directory layout that a later restructure deleted, and nothing failed loudly when they stopped matching, so the boundaries they encoded silently ceased to exist.
defects.reproduction: `ls demo/@` → No such file or directory. `npx eslint demo/shell/dock/menus/ProfileSection.vue` → exit 0 despite the shell→feature import at line 14.
defects.proposedCure: Re-express the bans against the current tree as layer rules, not path blacklists: demo/shell/** may not import demo/{palettes,workbenches,scenes,picker}/**; demo/platform/** may import nothing above itself; demo/color-session/** may not import demo/color-picker/**. Four no-restricted-imports objects, each glob-matched to a directory that exists, so L-4 cannot silently recur.

defects.defect: ProfileSection.vue and MobileMenuDropdown.vue are two implementations of one menu — 88 identical lines — and they have already drifted: the admin-identity state renders gold on desktop and grey on mobile.

defects.defect: The component constructs the ink instrument twice and registers two onMounted hooks that each increment a module-global epoch counter, invalidating a module-global tint cache shared by every ink consumer in the app — twice per ProfileSection mount.
defects.evidence: ProfileSection.vue:28-29 calls useSafeAccentFn twice; each call runs useGlobalDark() + inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY) + bumpProbeEpochOnMount() (useContrastSafeColor.ts:345-348). Line 43 calls useGlobalDark() a third time. useContrastSafeColor.ts:68 `const probeEpoch = ref(0)`, :77 `if (getCurrentInstance()) onMounted(() => probeEpoch.value++)`, :239 `const liveTintCache = new Map<InkSurface, TintCacheEntry>()`, :245 validity keyed on `hit.epoch === epoch`. Measured consumer census: 8 useSafeAccentFn call sites plus useContrastSafeColor, ConsoleRail.vue:133 and useViewAccents.ts:89 — every one writes the shared epoch. useGlobalDark itself is a createGlobalState singleton (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/dark-z_P5QwqI.js: `var o, s = r(() => {…})`) so its repetition is free; the epoch bump is not.
defects.mechanism: unowned global mutable state — a cache-validity epoch with no owner that every consumer is required to write, so each mounting component forces a full getComputedStyle + canvas-readback re-probe of every cached surface for every other consumer.
defects.reproduction: NONE (static; hypothesis for the perf magnitude). The double registration is direct from ProfileSection.vue:28-29 → useContrastSafeColor.ts:348; the cache-invalidation consequence follows from useContrastSafeColor.ts:245.
defects.proposedCure: Dissolves entirely once L-1 lands — with the rung lightness coming from glass-ui there is no probe, no epoch and no cache. Until then: one useSafeAccentFn call in this component, and move the epoch bump to the boot writer (one owner) instead of every consumer.

defects.defect: --accent-live is a third home for the certified ink and desynchronises from the rendered ink across a scheme flip; the tint cache keys validity on a direct documentElement.classList read (the DOM effect) while the recompute is driven by isDark (the cause) — one concept, two scheme signals.
defects.evidence: Live flip driven through ProfileSection's own "Dark mode" row (ProfileSection.vue:167 @click="toggleDark()"), sampled at +0ms / +1 frame / +600ms: before dark=false ink=oklch(0.454991 0.15 30) --accent-live=oklch(45.499144080095% 0.15 30deg); nextFrame dark=true ink=oklab(0.454991 0.129904 0.075) --accent-live unchanged; settled(+600ms) dark=true ink=oklch(0.848306 0.0831763 30) --accent-live STILL oklch(45.499144080095% 0.15 30deg) — the light-mode value in a .dark document, ΔL 0.393. demo/styles/foundation.css:222 documents that --primary re-points onto --accent-live, so everything on that token paints the light ink for that window. Mechanism site: useContrastSafeColor.ts:242 `const darkClass = document.documentElement.classList.contains("dark");`. MT-F009 CORRECTION: measured 21 useGlobalDark() call sites all resolving to one createGlobalState singleton, and exactly ONE direct classList reader; the two vueuse useDark stores named in the brief are retired — useMarkdownHighlighting.ts:68-80 and useMarkdownColors.ts:16-19 are comments recording their removal, and `grep -rn "useDark\b" demo/` returns only those two comment lines.
defects.mechanism: duplicated ownership of a derived value (the component's own computed vs the boot writer's :root mirror) plus a split scheme signal (reactive cause vs DOM effect), so the two mirrors transit independently with no ordering guarantee.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/ — click @mbabb, click "Dark mode", and within ~600ms read getComputedStyle(<Login/Profile button>).color against getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--accent-live'). They disagree by ΔL 0.393; they reconverge seconds later, so this is transient rather than permanent.
defects.proposedCure: One owner for the ink: the boot writer computes it and mirrors it; components read the token or the injected ref, never recompute it. Replace useContrastSafeColor.ts:242's classList read with the reactive isDark from the single useGlobalDark singleton so cause and effect cannot disagree. Measured DOM (scratchpad/psec-probe-a.mjs): the Login trigger carries `data-emphasis="secondary"`, `class="button tap-squish focus-ring glass-wash glass-capsule glass-capsule-hover …"` AND a literal `variant="outline"` attribute; `document.querySelectorAll('[variant]').length` = 2. Visual: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png shows Login and @mbabb as the same filled pill. Measured `border-top-width: 0px` on the Button in all four states, so the `borderColor: triggerInk` half of the :style at :63/:115 is inert (it IS live on .slug-pill — measured 1px, probe e).
defects.mechanism: Glass 7 adoption residue: an API that was renamed away (variant -> emphasis/tone) left the call sites untouched, and Vue fallthrough attributes make the dead prop invisible at runtime and at typecheck. The same class of defect as a silent fallback.
defects.reproduction: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` exits 0 with no output (the hard CI gate does not see it). In the browser: `document.querySelector('[data-o18="profile-trigger"]').getAttribute('variant')` -> "outline" and `.getAttribute('data-emphasis')` -> "secondary". Repo-wide: `grep -rn 'variant="' demo --include="*.vue" | wc -l` -> 103.
defects.proposedCure: One mechanical repo-wide sweep to the Glass 7 axes (emphasis/tone), not 103 local patches: `emphasis="secondary"` + certified ink for the two triggers, `emphasis="text"` for the @mbabb wordmark so it stops painting a capsule; delete the now-fictional :103-110 comment (it reasons about the Glass-6 outline variant's inset-shadow border) and the dead `borderColor` channel at :63/:115.

defects.defect: `@click="pm.onRegenerateSlug()"` — a destructive, un-confirmed floating promise. With the API unreachable it DESTROYS the user's slug (identity key to their published palettes), reports nothing, and leaves the UI showing an intact account.
defects.evidence: ProfileSection.vue:87. Measured (scratchpad/psec-probe-e.mjs — seed localStorage['palette-user-slug'], abort every off-origin request, click the row): `{"slug": null, "dialogOpen": false, "liveRegions": ["off:92.0%","off:88.8","off:20.0","off:82.7%"], "triggerStillThere": true}` plus console `[Vue warn]: Unhandled error during execution of native event handler at <Primitive … role="menuitem" …>`. Root ordering: demo/platform/auth/useUserAuth.ts:112-127 removes SLUG_KEY + clears the token BEFORE `createSession()`; demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:101-103 awaits it with no try/catch on the zero-saved-palettes branch; useUserAuth.ts:118 deliberately does not null the slug ref ('avoids UI flash'), so the trigger still reads 'Profile'.
defects.mechanism: Unguarded async invocation from a template event expression (no await, no .catch, no pending state, no announcement) over a port that clears persisted state before the replacement is obtained — clear-then-create instead of create-then-swap.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/psec-probe-e.mjs: seed `localStorage['palette-user-slug']='audit-seat-c'`, `page.route(/^https?:\/\/(?!localhost)/, r => r.abort())`, load http://localhost:9000/#/, expand the dock, open the Profile menu, click `Regenerate slug`, then read localStorage — it is null and nothing was announced.
defects.proposedCure: Port: create-then-swap, never clear-then-create (the owning seat's fix, BLOCKER-class there). Component: route the zero-palettes branch through the migrate dialog `useSlugMigration` already owns (the >0-palettes branch already does — no new component, no new dir), and surface failure on an aria-live region. Destructive rows never fire as bare floating promises.

defects.defect: The Dark-mode row is a checkbox rendered as a plain command: `role="menuitem"` with `aria-checked` null; the only state carrier is an aria-hidden glyph, so screen-reader users get an unknowable toggle.
defects.evidence: ProfileSection.vue:167-177. Measured rendered row (scratchpad/psec-probe-a.mjs step B): `{"tag":"div","role":"menuitem","text":"Dark mode","ariaChecked":null,"w":200.6,"h":44}`. The Moon/Sun glyphs at :174-175 are correctly `aria-hidden="true"`, so no accessible state exists at all.
defects.mechanism: Wrong primitive: a stateful toggle expressed with the stateless primitive, with the state pushed into decoration.
defects.reproduction: Open the @mbabb menu at http://localhost:9000/#/ and evaluate `document.querySelector('[role="menu"] [role^="menuitem"]:last-of-type').getAttribute('aria-checked')` -> null while the row is a live dark-mode toggle.
defects.proposedCure: Use `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` — already exported by the very barrel imported at ProfileSection.vue:9-12 (demo/ui/dropdown-menu/index.ts) — `<DropdownMenuCheckboxItem :model-value="isDark" @select.prevent @update:model-value="toggleDark()">`, which renders reka's role="menuitemcheckbox" + aria-checked. This also dissolves D58.i: value.js no longer needs Glass to ship a `passive` DarkModeToggle variant, so the outstanding W47 ask (mark M1) can be WITHDRAWN rather than folded.

defects.defect: The `chrome` live-tint probe behind this component's triggerInk is DEAD under Glass 7: it reads `.glass-dock`'s backgroundColor, which is fully transparent, so the guard silently degenerates to the static model — and the O-18 census's ground model omits the same painter, so guard and gate agree on a ground neither of them measures.
defects.evidence: useContrastSafeColor.ts:151-153 queries `.glass-dock` and reads getComputedStyle(...).backgroundColor. Measured in all four scheme states (scratchpad/psec-probe-c.mjs and -d.mjs): `.glass-dock` backgroundColor = `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`; the band is painted by the CHILD `.dock-plate` = `color(srgb 0.931227 0.845921 0.816039 / 0.5392)` (light) / `color(srgb 0.376885 0.293161 0.253837 / 0.5776)` (dark). alpha 0 -> resolveLiveTint returns undefined -> the static producer MODEL serves. Also measured: `plate.contains(loginButton)` === false and every ancestor of the trigger from `button` to `body` is `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`; the census (e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:142-172) composites ANCESTOR backgrounds over `oklch(--ink-ambient-l 0 0)`, and `--ink-ambient-l` is 0.7900 in BOTH schemes — so the census ground for every dock control is the same flat neutral grey in light and dark.
defects.mechanism: Selector-based DOM probe whose failure mode is a silent fallback: Glass 7 moved the band's paint from `.glass-dock` to the child `.dock-plate`, the probe resolved alpha=0, and `resolveLiveTint` returned undefined instead of erroring — exactly the failure the :56-66 epoch comment says the machinery exists to prevent.
defects.reproduction: At http://localhost:9000/#/ evaluate `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.glass-dock')).backgroundColor` -> "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" and `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.dock-plate')).backgroundColor` -> the real material; `document.querySelector('.dock-plate').contains(document.querySelector('[data-o18="profile-trigger"]'))` -> false.
defects.proposedCure: Read the chrome referent off the element that actually paints (`.glass-dock .dock-plate`), or better: have glass-ui PUBLISH the band's composited tint as a token the consumer reads — the 'tiers publish effective lightness' stake D6 already declares, which ends selector coupling entirely. And make the probe fail loudly on alpha=0 instead of degenerating to the model: a silent fallback inside a contrast guard is a defect generator. The census's ground model must include the sibling plate for chrome-seated rows.

defects.defect: Vacuous gate: nothing tests this component. No unit test exists; the sole automated coverage is one contrast row that is scheme-COLD by construction (so C-1 is invisible) and censuses against a ground that omits the band painter (C-5).
defects.evidence: `grep -rln "ProfileSection" test/ demo/test/` -> nothing. Only e2e hit: e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:629-630 (`[data-o18="profile-trigger"]`) + `.slug-pill`; the describe block uses `test.use({ colorScheme: scheme })` at :590-592, i.e. each scheme is booted COLD and the runtime flip this component owns is never exercised. Zero coverage of the Dark-mode, Logout, Regenerate slug, Switch account, Copy slug, Share color rows, the admin-pill branch, and the logged-out Login trigger (which carries the same ink and has no data-o18 hook).
defects.mechanism: The oracle measures a state the component can only be in at boot, so every defect that requires an interaction — including the one this component's own control causes — is out of the gate's reach.
defects.reproduction: Green-keeping mutations (each leaves `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit`, vitest and the o18 census passing): (1) swap Moon and Sun at :174-175; (2) `@click="toggleDark()"` -> `@click` at :167; (3) delete `borderColor: triggerInk` from :63/:115; (4) `variant="outline"` -> `variant="banana"`; (5) `useSafeAccentFn("chrome")` -> `useSafeAccentFn("floating")` at :28.
defects.proposedCure: Add a FLIP leg to the O-18 census (boot light, toggle at runtime through the shipped control, re-census both schemes and assert the certification EQUALS the cold-boot certification for that scheme) — that single oracle kills C-1's whole family, and it belongs in the census that already owns the ink contract. Plus a component-level test for the menu's semantics (menuitemcheckbox state, destructive-row confirmation, failure announcement).

defects.defect: The @mbabb wordmark wears `text-foreground/70` — post-hoc alpha de-emphasis, the idiom this repo explicitly RETIRED in favour of the certified `--ink-muted` rung — and it is uncensused.
defects.evidence: ProfileSection.vue:138. Measured raw ink: `oklab(0 0 0 / 0.7)` light, `oklab(0.999994 0.0000455677 0.0000200868 / 0.7)` dark (scratchpad/psec-probe-b.mjs). Doctrine: useContrastSafeColor.ts:317-319 — 'the plate-caption / parse-echo voice; post-hoc opacity de-emphasis is retired'; the O-18 census asserts caption/echo IDENTITY with `--ink-muted`. Previously booked at docs/tranches/T/audit/w3-ink-lane-record.md:125 and never landed.
defects.mechanism: A de-emphasis role expressed with an abolished mechanism (opacity multiplication on the ink) rather than the certified token, so its contrast is unguarded and unmeasured.
defects.reproduction: At http://localhost:9000/#/ evaluate `getComputedStyle([...document.querySelectorAll('.glass-dock button')].find(b=>b.textContent.trim()==='@mbabb')).color` -> `oklab(… / 0.7)` in both schemes.
defects.proposedCure: `color: var(--ink-muted)` (or the chrome-rung certified muted ink) and drop the alpha, joining the class the census already certifies by identity.

defects.defect: The avatar has no fallback and reaches a hard-coded third-party host: on network failure it renders a permanently empty 28x28 circle.
defects.evidence: ProfileSection.vue:145-147. Measured with the image request aborted (scratchpad/psec-probe-e.mjs / -c.mjs): `{"imgPresent":true,"imgComplete":false,"avatarBox":{"w":28,"h":28}}` and the rendered subtree `` — no fallback child. `AvatarFallback` IS exported by the barrel imported at :13 (demo/ui/avatar/index.ts) and unused. The absolute URL `https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/2848617?v=4` is duplicated at MobileMenuDropdown.vue:81.
defects.mechanism: An unhandled load-failure state for a remote asset: the component imports two of the three Avatar parts and omits the one that exists for exactly this path.
defects.reproduction: Route-abort `https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/**`, open the @mbabb menu: the avatar slot is an empty circle for the life of the session.
defects.proposedCure: Add `<AvatarFallback>` (already exported by the imported barrel) with the initials/glyph, and single-source the avatar URL as a constant consumed by both menus rather than a literal in two files.

defects.defect: The mobile twin has silently drifted from the 'verbatim' copy it claims to be: the same application state renders two different identities depending on viewport.
defects.evidence: MobileMenuDropdown.vue:21-22 claims 'the desktop twin's cure, verbatim (ProfileSection.vue)'. Deltas: admin pill ProfileSection.vue:96 (`gold-shimmer`, `var(--color-gold)`) vs MobileMenuDropdown.vue:67 (`--muted-foreground`, no shimmer); separator before 'Regenerate slug' present at ProfileSection.vue:86, absent in the mobile twin; ink rungs chrome+floating (ProfileSection.vue:28-29) vs floating only (MobileMenuDropdown.vue:23).
defects.mechanism: Two ~90%-identical SFCs maintained by copy-paste with no shared source of truth, so every subsequent fix lands in one and drifts the other.
defects.reproduction: Diff demo/shell/dock/menus/ProfileSection.vue against demo/shell/dock/menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue: identical row sets and identical state (`pm.userSlug` / `pm.isAdminAuthenticated` / share / dark) with the three deltas above.
defects.proposedCure: One row set, one component; express the desktop/mobile difference as the trigger and the ink rung (props), not as a second file. No new shared/ dir is needed — the menus dir is already the home.

defects.defect: Two import paths to one design system inside one file — the alias/dual-path the no-legacy edict forbids.
defects.evidence: ProfileSection.vue:6 `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock` and :8 `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dark` (direct) vs :7 `../../../ui/button`, :9-12 `../../../ui/dropdown-menu`, :13 `../../../ui/avatar` — each a one-line re-export (`demo/ui/button/index.ts` is literally `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`). Already booked as 'architecturally a pass-through shim' at docs/tranches/N/audit/lanes/E2.md:132.
defects.mechanism: A migration-era barrel that was never dissolved, so both the shim path and the direct path are live simultaneously.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static reading of the import block; the shim files are 1-line re-exports (verified by cat of every demo/ui/*/index.ts).
defects.proposedCure: Dissolve demo/ui/* and import from @mkbabb/glass-ui subpaths at every consumer — one sweep, then the directory is deleted (not kept as an alias).

defects.defect: `inject(SESSION_PORT_KEY)!` fails as an undefined-property render crash rather than a named wiring error, and the component constructs two live-ink instruments, each registering a global-cache-invalidating mount bump.
defects.evidence: ProfileSection.vue:42 (`const pm = inject(SESSION_PORT_KEY)!`) and :28-29 (two `useSafeAccentFn` calls -> two `useGlobalDark()`, two `inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY)`, two `bumpProbeEpochOnMount()` -> two onMounted `probeEpoch.value++`). Each bump invalidates the GLOBAL `liveTintCache` for every surface (useContrastSafeColor.ts:239-251). Call-site census: `grep -rn "useSafeAccentFn(" demo` -> 9 sites across 5 SFCs; `bumpProbeEpochOnMount` -> 7.
defects.mechanism: Non-null assertion on an injection substitutes a generic runtime TypeError for a diagnosable wiring failure; and per-instrument mount bumps make cache lifetime a function of unrelated components' mount order.
defects.reproduction: NONE (hypothesis for the crash path — no provider-less mount exists in the shipped tree). The double instrumentation is directly readable at :28-29.
defects.proposedCure: One `useSafeAccentFn` per component returning a rung-parameterised `safeCss(css, rung)`, so a component holds one instrument; and let the injection throw a named wiring error (the composable's own documented 'surfaced loudly' contract) instead of `!`.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M context) — the model this seat was explicitly spawned with; declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-01 — the menu has no width law: the slug string sets the popover width, putting 270.8 CSS px off-screen at the canon-bound 320px arm and 154.5 px off-screen at 200% zoom, with document.scrollWidth === clientWidth so the lost region is unreachable by any gesture.
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND, but the sound half is recorded so the verdict is not an artefact of only hunting faults: reactive props destructure + defineModel + typed defineEmits are idiomatic Vue 3.5; all six imports are value imports so verbatimModuleSyntax is satisfied; 115 lines, no god module; the component authors ZERO motion (correct — surface motion is producer-owned) and reduced-motion is honoured end-to-end (measured: content transition collapses from `scale,translate,opacity,filter,display,overlay @0.35s` to `opacity @0.15s`); keyboard is correct (ArrowDown sets data-highlighted on "Copy slug"; Escape closes and restores focus to the exact opener — measured activeEl = BUTTON.dock-dropdown-trigger[aria-label="Menu"], satisfying VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.1); the menu carries aria-labelledby → trigger and aria-orientation="vertical"; the trigger exposes aria-expanded false→true, aria-haspopup="menu", data-state closed→open; Avatar `decorative` works (rendered img alt="" aria-hidden="true"); six of seven rows are exactly 44.0px; the trigger is vertically centred in the dock plate to −0.05px and the plate insets are symmetric 14.1/14.1; forced-colors renders legibly (bg → rgb(255,255,255), pill ink rgb(112,89,66)); RTL mirrors correctly (trigger x 81.7, menu x 82.5). The root REPORT's horizontalOverflow=0 is also NOT contradicted — the document never scrolls, the menu overflows off it.

defects.defect: The menu has no width law. `DropdownMenuContent class="min-w-menu"` (line 43) is a MINIMUM only, and the slug pill (line 48) is `whitespace-nowrap` with no max-inline-size, no truncation and no overflow rule — so the user's slug string sets the popover width, which sets the viewport overflow.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue:43,47-50. Measured (frames/mmd-probe.json, mmd-probe2.json, WebKit 26.4): 390px logged-out → menu {x:92.5,w:214.6} correct; 390px 35-char slug → {x:0,w:349.5} = 89.6% of viewport, flush-left, align="end" collision-defeated; 320px 35-char slug → 29.5px off-screen; 390px 62-char slug → w:590.8, 200.8px off-screen; 320px 62-char slug → 270.8px off-screen; 195x422 (390 @200% zoom) → 154.5px off-screen. docScrollW === docClientW in every case (390/390, 320/320) so the lost region is unreachable. Producer's vertical clamp DOES work (max-height 506.4px@390, 384px@320, overflow-y:auto) — there is no horizontal counterpart because the content, not the container, is at fault. Frame: frames/D-320-longslug-open.png.
defects.mechanism: unbounded intrinsic content width inside a container with a min- but no max- constraint; identity data of unbounded length treated as chrome
defects.reproduction: localStorage.setItem("palette-user-slug","a-very-long-generated-slug-name-for-overflow-testing-1234567890"); reload http://localhost:9000/#/ at 320x640 WebKit isMobile; tap `.dock-dropdown-trigger`. Or: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-mobilemenudropdown/frames/mmd-probe2.mjs → sections longSlug_390 / longSlug_320 / zoom200.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition, not a local max-w: the slug is provenance data of unbounded length in fixed chrome, which is exactly glass-ui's `./chip` primitive's job (dist/components/chip/ ships today). Retire the `.slug-pill` recipe (foundation.css:585, whose own comment concedes it institutionalises per-instance overrides) in favour of producer `Chip` with a producer-owned max-inline-size + middle-ellipsis and the full slug as accessible name. The menu then has a width law by construction and no consumer can break it — and this same move closes D-04 (one admin tone) and D-14 (one override mechanism).

defects.defect: `as-child` on `DropdownMenuItem` (line 92) is inert — the prop does not exist in the producer's contract — so the `<a>` becomes a `display:block` CHILD of the `role="menuitem"` div rather than being it. 73.2% of the GitHub row's area is a dead zone that swallows the tap and dismisses the menu without navigating, and the icon/label break onto two lines.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue:92-99. Producer contract quoted: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenuItem.vue.d.ts — `export interface DropdownMenuItemProps { disabled?; textValue?; inset?; class?; }` — no asChild. The attribute never reaches the DOM (measured rendered attrs: data-reka-collection-item, role=menuitem, tabindex=-1, data-slot=dropdown-menu-item, class — no as-child). Measured (frames/mmd-probe3.json): anchorIsItem:false, anchorParentIsItem:true; item {x:99.5,y:223.3,w:200.6,h:55.4}, anchor {x:107.5,y:229.3,w:68.6,h:43.4}, deadFractionOfRow:0.732; anchorDisplay:"block" with svg y=400.6 and text y=417 → sameLine:false; row 55.4px vs 44.0px for all six siblings; label x=15 vs x=37 for all six siblings. Behaviour: click at (itemRight−20, itemMidY) → {"newPages":0,"menuStillOpen":false,"url":"http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=…"} — menu closed, nothing happened.
defects.mechanism: consumer relies on an undeclared producer prop; silent no-op produces a false affordance and a nested interactive inside role=menuitem
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-mobilemenudropdown/frames/mmd-probe3.mjs → sections asChild and githubRowClick. Manually: 390x844 WebKit, tap ⋮, tap the GitHub row 20px from its right edge — the menu dismisses and no navigation occurs.
defects.proposedCure: Stop making a menu row a link through a prop the producer does not publish. Either (a) BH/BI relay to glass-ui for a first-class DropdownMenuItem link arm (`href`, or a genuine asChild) and consume it, or (b) make it an ordinary DropdownMenuItem whose @select opens the URL, so the producer's own full-row hit target and row-height rhythm apply unmodified. ProfileSection.vue:158-165 carries identical markup, so one producer-side cure closes both sites.

defects.defect: Two copy verbs in the same list: `Share color` flips its icon+label to Check/"Copied!", `Copy slug` writes the clipboard and reports nothing. Both use `@select.prevent` to hold the menu open — one to show a result, one to show the user the unchanged row they just tapped.
defects.evidence: MobileMenuDropdown.vue:52-54 vs :88-90; the props type (:16-19) has `linkCopied` but no `slugCopied` — the feedback channel was never built. Handler: SlugEditLayer.vue:68-70 `void writeClipboard(pm.userSlug.value)` — promise discarded, so rejection is also silent. Measured with the clipboard stubbed (probe 5): tap "Copy slug" → clipboard ["api","amaranthine-quokka-northern-marches"], menu open:true, menu text UNCHANGED, aria-live regions with content = only the Picker's four, all aria-live="off". tap "Share color" → clipboard written AND menu text changes "Share color"→"Copied!".
defects.mechanism: per-verb ad-hoc feedback flag threaded as a prop instead of one owned copy-result affordance
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-mobilemenudropdown/frames/mmd-probe5.mjs — stubs navigator.clipboard, taps Copy slug then Share color, diffs menu textContent.
defects.proposedCure: One copy-result affordance owned once and consumed by both rows and the desktop twin — a `useCopyFeedback()` seam in demo/platform/ returning {copy, lastCopied} keyed by verb, plus one aria-live="polite" status inside the menu. Adding a second boolean prop beside `linkCopied` doubles the contrivance the first one already is.

defects.defect: One state (isAdminAuthenticated), two visual systems: mobile renders the admin pill in muted grey one tap deep inside the menu; desktop renders it in gold with an infinite shimmer on the dock band. And the desktop shimmer is itself dead — the inline `style` color beats `.gold-shimmer`'s `color: transparent`, so the clipped gradient is painted over and a 5s infinite animation produces zero visible pixels.
defects.evidence: MobileMenuDropdown.vue:66-68 `style="border-color: var(--muted-foreground); color: var(--muted-foreground)"` vs ProfileSection.vue:96 `class="… gold-shimmer" style="border-color: var(--color-gold); color: var(--color-gold)"`. Producer recipe: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/utilities/base-misc.css — `.gold-shimmer { background: linear-gradient(…); background-clip: text; -webkit-background-clip: text; color: transparent; }`. Measured mobile 390px (frames/mmd-probe.json admin-light/admin-dark): pill.color rgb(112,89,66) / rgb(195,185,172). Measured desktop 1440x900 with admin token (probe 6): cls "slug-pill cursor-default whitespace-nowrap gold-shimmer", color "oklch(0.751 0.147 84.199997)" (the INLINE value, not transparent), backgroundImage the gold gradient, backgroundClip "text", animationName "metal-shimmer-sweep", animationDuration "5s". Frame: frames/D-390-forcedcolors-admin-open.png.
defects.mechanism: state treatment forked per responsive branch with no shared owner; inline-style specificity silently defeats a producer utility whose whole mechanism is `color: transparent`
defects.reproduction: localStorage.setItem("palette-admin-token","t"); reload /#/ — at 390x844 tap ⋮ (grey pill, no motion); at 1440x900 read the band pill (solid gold, invisible 5s animation). node frames/mmd-probe6.mjs reproduces the desktop computed style.
defects.proposedCure: One admin identity composition rendered identically on both branches: neutral ink plus an explicit scope word, not a metal — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 says elevated authority is communicated by labeling and scope, not by a fourth visual system. Delete `gold-shimmer` from the pill (a dead animation) and delete the divergent --muted-foreground inline. Any distinguishing mark belongs in glass-ui as a Chip tone, not as an inline style on two SFCs.

defects.defect: The §4 type-role matrix is broken three ways inside one popover: (a) prose/help rendered in Fraunces italic 11px; (b) `font-display` on the menu content is cascade-dead; (c) iOS text-autosizing boosts the rows 14→21px while the pill and description are untouched, reordering the rungs so the least important rows are the largest type.
defects.evidence:
(a) MobileMenuDropdown.vue:85 `

` measures Fraunces / italic / 11px / rgb(112,89,66); VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:74 assigns prose/help → text-prose, Plus Jakarta Sans, and :78 declares the matrix closed with P019 the sole exception; `text-micro` is not a role in the matrix. Duplicated at ProfileSection.vue:150. (b) line 43 `class="min-w-menu font-display"` — measured computed style of [role=menu] is Fira Code 16px; --font-display resolves correctly to '"Fraunces", "Fraunces Fallback", serif' and the utility DOES work on the

in (a), so it is cascade-dead, not a missing font. Same dead class at ProfileSection.vue:70 and :143. (c) Measured same URL, same 390px viewport, one variable (frames/mmd-probe2.json): isMobile true → menuitem 21px/lh 29.4; isMobile false → 14px/lh 19.6; .slug-pill 14px in BOTH; description 11px in BOTH; @mbabb 14px in BOTH. --type-small = clamp(0.875rem, 0.8rem + 0.25vw, 1.25rem) → 14px at 390 in both cases, so 21px is a 1.5x boost applied to the rows only.
defects.mechanism: role matrix applied by class name rather than verified by rendered computed style; a fluid clamp ladder left un-pinned against UA text autosizing
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-mobilemenudropdown/frames/mmd-probe2.mjs → compare type_isMobile_true vs type_isMobile_false. Visual: frames/D-390-light-loggedin-open.png.

(c) pin `text-size-adjust: 100%` at the app root in demo/styles/ so the fluid clamp ladder is the only size authority; the ladder was designed for this and the UA boost is fighting it. All three are root cures, not per-component ones.

defects.defect: The description text fails contrast on the real composited surface, and its contrast varies along its own line box because the menu is an 80.8%-alpha veil over the live Picker readout.
defects.evidence: Menu background measured `oklab(0.936408 0.005529 0.013284 / 0.808)` light, `oklab(0.37944 0.009899 0.01685 / 0.8944)` dark. Real-pixel sample of a rendered clip at DPR 1 (frames/mmd-probe4.json, band y 40-56, x 95-330 of a clip at y=290): darkest ink in the description line rgb(112,89,66); ground under/next to it rgb(233,193,194) (the Picker's pink bleeding through) → contrast 4.03:1; lightest ground in the same band rgb(241,226,220) → 5.21:1. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:82 — 'Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence.' Token raise at foundation.css:739 is against --background, not against a translucent veil over a chromatic ground. Frames: D-390-light-loggedin-open.png shows the 92.0%/88.8 readout legible THROUGH the menu.
defects.mechanism: structural-glass surface tier chosen for a chrome menu whose backdrop is the app's own highest-contrast display type

defects.proposedCure: A menu is not a window. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2 gives glass its blur only when it reveals live content usefully; here the reveal destroys the menu's own copy. Select an opaque/specimen-well surface tier for DropdownMenuContent at the producer root (surface="opaque"/tier), for every menu in the app — the forced-colors arm already proves that render is legible. Not a per-instance bg- override.

defects.defect: No pending, disabled or error state exists anywhere in the component, though four of seven rows fire asynchronous, networked or irreversible work — and `Regenerate slug` closes the menu, destroying the only surface in the mobile UI that displays the slug it just changed.

Async rows: :58 pm.userLogout() (network session delete), :61 pm.onRegenerateSlug() (network, irreversible), :52 → SlugEditLayer.vue:68-70 `void writeClipboard(...)` (promise discarded), :88 shareLink. `@select.prevent` appears at :52, :88, :101 only — NOT at :55/:58/:61, so Switch account / Logout / Regenerate slug all close the menu. The slug pill at :47-50 inside this menu is the only place the regenerated slug is displayed on mobile. Producer supports a `disabled` prop (DropdownMenuItem.vue.d.ts) — never used. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-08 (ADD-AFFORDANCE, persistent entity status/recovery); VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83.
defects.mechanism: identity mutations placed on fire-and-forget menu rows in a surface that dismisses itself on select
defects.reproduction: NONE for the failure render — I confirmed the ABSENCE of the mechanism by source census (grep count 0) and the dismissal by the missing @select.prevent, but did not exercise an offline/failing logout. The `Regenerate slug` dismissal is directly readable at :61 and reproducible by tapping it; the missing-state half is a hypothesis.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the state problem rather than style it: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 already assigns identity, recovery-credential rotation and logout to the Account modal side Dialog opened from the Dock (W23's owned composition). Move Logout / Regenerate slug / Switch account behind that Dialog, leaving this menu with navigation-class rows only.

defects.defect: An authenticated admin on mobile has no way out: the admin branch renders one label pill and zero identity actions.

defects.defect: The trigger is the smallest operable target in the whole flow: a 42.7x33.3 hit box opening a menu whose rows are all exactly 44.0px, sitting 7.0px from its neighbour on a phone.

Accessibility floors do not require bloated visible chrome'; PR-12 (:56) TIGHTEN 'invisible/seat geometry preserves target floor while optics follow rung'. A per-instance class here would fork the dock's one trigger rhythm.

defects.defect: PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-16 names this control explicitly and is half-unmet: the ellipsis has expanded state, but its accessible name is the generic 'Menu' rather than a purpose, and it carries no perceptible label in either scheme.

defects.defect: The boundary inventory diverges from the self-declared desktop twin in three places and in both directions: two separators the desktop has are missing, and one separator that survives fences a group of exactly one.
defects.evidence: MobileMenuDropdown.vue:22 self-documents the twinning ('the desktop twin's cure, verbatim (ProfileSection.vue)'). Measured block layout, logged-in, 390px (frames/mmd-probe.json → logged-in-light.menu.nonItemBlocks): label h39.4@76.5; menuitem 44@115.9 Copy slug; 44@159.9 Switch account; 44@203.9 Logout; 44@247.9 Regenerate slug; separator 1@295.9; div h49.8@300.9 @mbabb card (ends 350.7); menuitem 44@350.6 Share color; 55.4@394.6 GitHub; separator 1@454; 44@459 Dark mode. (1) desktop has a rule before Regenerate slug (ProfileSection.vue:86) — mobile has none, so the two most consequential rows are adjacent with no boundary. (2) desktop has a rule after the @mbabb card (ProfileSection.vue:153) — mobile measures a 0px boundary (card ends 350.7, Share starts 350.6). (3) the surviving separator at y=454 fences only Dark mode. defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-mobilemenudropdown/frames/mmd-probe.mjs → logged-in-light.menu.nonItemBlocks and .seps; compare against ProfileSection.vue:86 and :153.
defects.proposedCure: Derive both menus from one declarative section model (sections: {identity, actions, meta}) so the boundary set is a property of the grouping rather than of the file — which simultaneously deletes the 81%-identical fork (L-9/L-26) that made the divergence possible.

defects.defect: Three icon rungs in one seven-row list, and one of them is geometrically wrong: the theme glyph renders 16x24 despite `aspect-square`, making its row's icon column 10px taller than every sibling's and displacing its label 2px.

Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:73 (§5.8) 'Real rendered relation wins over token intent … token presence alone cannot close a row.' Identical defect at ProfileSection.vue:174-175.
defects.mechanism: icon size set per call site with three different answers instead of once on the row composition
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-mobilemenudropdown/frames/mmd-probe2.mjs → section iconAlign.
