defects.defect: Three import paths to one package inside one ten-line block, one of them a pure alias barrel that exists only to preserve a shadcn-shaped path.
defects.evidence: MobileMenuDropdown.vue:6 `from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dark"`, :10 `from "../../../ui/dropdown-menu"`, :11 `from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock"`, :12 `from "../../../ui/avatar"`. demo/ui/dropdown-menu/index.ts is ONE line: `export { DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuTrigger, … } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. Census: 19 directories under demo/ui/, every index.ts a pure re-export of @mkbabb/glass-ui. Owner edicts 2 (no aliases / dual paths) and 4 (glass-ui is the design system). REFUTATION of a prior row: DEFECT-LEDGER:12278 attributes this menu's type/veil defects to 'the demo-local demo/ui/dropdown-menu primitive rather than the producer's menu tier' — the barrel re-exports the producer's tier verbatim, so the primitive IS the producer's; D-05 and D-06 are consumer-class and surface-tier defects, not primitive-substitution defects.
defects.mechanism: an alias barrel layer retained after the components it aliased were migrated into the producer
defects.reproduction: cat demo/ui/dropdown-menu/index.ts; for d in demo/ui/*/; do head -1 $d/index.ts; done
defects.proposedCure: Delete the demo/ui/* barrels and import from @mkbabb/glass-ui directly — one path per package. This is a tree-wide hygiene row, not a MobileMenuDropdown row; filed here because the file exhibits three paths in six lines.

defects.defect: `.slug-pill` institutionalises per-instance overrides (its own comment says so), and this single component uses two different override mechanisms for the same recipe seventeen lines apart.
defects.evidence: foundation.css:583-587 — '.slug-pill … Consumers set color / border-color per-instance via :style.' MobileMenuDropdown.vue:47-50 uses a bound object `:style="{ color: menuInk, borderColor: menuInk }"`; :67 uses a static string `style="border-color: var(--muted-foreground); color: var(--muted-foreground)"`. Tree-wide the same recipe is driven five ways (injected value, static CSS var inline, Tailwind utilities, bare class) — already booked as a family row; what is new is two mechanisms inside one component for the same pill in two branches of one v-if. glass-ui ships ./chip (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/chip/). Owner edict 5 (style at the root, never per-instance overrides).
defects.mechanism: a CSS recipe with no tone API, forcing every consumer to invent one
defects.reproduction: grep -n 'slug-pill' demo/shell/dock/menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue demo/styles/foundation.css
defects.proposedCure: Same transposition as D-01: producer `Chip` with a `tone` prop. That closes D-01 (width law), D-04 (one admin tone) and D-14 (one mechanism) together — the argument for a transposition rather than three patches.

defects.defect: The @mbabb identity card is a plain div inside `role="menu"` containing a tabindex=0 anchor, breaking the ARIA menu roving-focus contract; the link is simultaneously unreachable to a screen reader walking menuitems and a 51.7x17.2 target.
defects.evidence: MobileMenuDropdown.vue:79-87. Measured (frames/mmd-probe4.json): identityBlock {role:null, tabIndex:-1, h:49.8, focusableChildren:1}; tabbables inside [role=menu] = [{A, tabIndex 0, "@mbabb"}, {A, tabIndex 0, "GitHub"}]; all seven menuitems measure tabindex=-1 (correct roving focus). The @mbabb anchor rect 51.7x17.2. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 ('role, accessible name, state/value … are explicit') and §5.1 overlay focus contract.
defects.mechanism: attribution content placed inside a composite widget as free-form markup rather than as a labelled header
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-mobilemenudropdown/frames/mmd-probe4.mjs → sections identityBlock and tabbables.
defects.proposedCure: The @mbabb card is attribution, not a menu command: promote it to a DropdownMenuLabel header with the decorative avatar aria-hidden and the link exposed as a real menuitem — or move provenance to the About route where §7 already assigns it. Do not leave a focusable island inside a roving-focus widget.

defects.defect: The 'certified ink' is certified twice against two different rungs, from a prop whose name asserts it is the raw opaque colour. The D6 rationale both twins quote ('each ink certifies against the surface it actually composites over') is structurally defeated, and in dark mode the live-colour identity renders at 11% of the picked chroma.
defects.evidence: Dock.vue:35 `const safeAccent = inject(SAFE_ACCENT_KEY)!`; Dock.vue:209 `:css-color-opaque="safeAccent"`. keys.ts:9 SAFE_ACCENT_KEY: InjectionKey<ComputedRef<string>>. useContrastSafeColor.ts:301-311 — safeAccentCss = certifyAccentInk(cssColorOpaque, surfaceLightnessNow("resting", …)). MobileMenuDropdown.vue:16-24 declares the prop `cssColorOpaque` and computes safeCss(cssColorOpaque) against surface "floating" (useSafeAccentFn("floating"), :23). So the composition is certifyAccentInk(certifyAccentInk(pick, resting), floating). Measured dark arm: picked accent oklch(0.470927 0.188343 9.834023) C=0.188; rendered pill AND --accent-live oklch(0.958322 0.021053 9.834023) C=0.021 → 11% of the picked chroma. Frame: frames/D-390-dark-loggedin-open.png shows an off-white capsule.
defects.mechanism: a pre-certified value passed into a certifier under a name that claims it is raw; monotone walks compose so the second certification can only move further from the pick
defects.reproduction: Mechanism: read Dock.vue:35,209 + useContrastSafeColor.ts:301-311 + MobileMenuDropdown.vue:16-24. Dark-chroma measurement: node frames/mmd-probe.mjs → logged-in-dark.menu.pill.color and .accentLive. The HARM of double-certification is a HYPOTHESIS — measured delta at the boot seed is ZERO (pill.color === --accent-live exactly), and I did not enumerate a pick for which resting requires a walk and floating does not.
defects.proposedCure: Stop passing a certified colour into a certifier: the component should receive the RAW cssColorOpaque (CSS_COLOR_KEY is already injected at Dock.vue:19) and certify once against the floating rung — which is exactly what the comment claims and what D6 requires. One certification, one rung, one honest name.

defects.defect: Producer relay (not a local defect): the menu's entry and exit transitions are both 0.35s, and the transition list includes `filter` on a backdrop-blurred surface.
defects.evidence: Measured on [role=menu]: transitionProperty 'scale, translate, opacity, filter, display, overlay', transitionDuration '0.35s' x6 — identical in both directions. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:140 (§6): 'Color/opacity effects use the corresponding short effect curve; exit is shorter than entry.' Owner: glass-ui's .dropdown-menu__content. Recorded alongside the negative findings: the SFC authors zero motion (correct) and reduced-motion IS honoured (measured 0.35s six-property → 0.15s opacity).
defects.mechanism: producer-owned surface motion; consumer has no local lever that would not violate §6's 'no consumer counter-filter fights a producer reveal'
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-mobilemenudropdown/frames/mmd-probe.mjs → menu.transProp/transDur in the default arm vs the logged-in-reduced arm.
defects.proposedCure: BH/BI relay ask to glass-ui (the standing fond): asymmetric exit curve on .dropdown-menu__content, and drop `filter` from the transition list on a backdrop-filtered surface. Never a local override.

defects.defect: Both dock menus mount at every viewport; the desktop identity chrome is fully constructed and hidden on every phone load and vice versa.
defects.evidence: Measured in the 390px DOM (frames/mmd-probe2.json → twinCensus): 3 dropdown triggers — the ⋮ (flex, 42.7x33.3) plus 'Profile' and '@mbabb' at 0x0 inside `hidden lg:flex` wrappers computing display:none. The lg: predicates are width-only (MobileMenuDropdown.vue:38, ProfileSection.vue:48,127) while the shell stamps data-layout on width AND aspect ratio — the tablet-portrait disagreement already booked at the Dock level.
defects.mechanism: responsive branching by CSS visibility over two forked component trees rather than by one composition with a compact mode
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-mobilemenudropdown/frames/mmd-probe2.mjs → section twinCensus.
defects.proposedCure: Filed as CORROBORATION of the existing L-9/L-26 identity (the 81%-identical menu fork, 87 of 108 non-blank lines shared) — NOT re-booked. Its cure is the single identity composition in §8 of the report, which is the same cure D-11 requires.

result.axis: design
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`; declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the "CERTIFIED ink" the component's own header comment promises measures 3.43:1 on the shipped light frame (16.4px/700 = normal text, floor 4.5:1), because `useSafeAccentFn("chrome")` models the dock band only while the glyph composites over the band AND the button's own `glass-wash` capsule. The identical two-alpha-layer failure was already diagnosed and cured for the `veil` surface in the same file's dependency (useContrastSafeColor.ts:154-169, "probed live: 4.30:1 measured vs the 5.75 walked target") and never migrated to the dock trigger.
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND, but these attacks failed and are recorded: (1) horizontalOverflow = 0 on all 60 captures in REPORT.json incl. 390px and the 200%-zoom arm; (2) pageErrors = 0 (the only /#/ console error is HeroBlob's `WebGL: context lost`); (3) reduced motion IS respected — `.gold-shimmer`'s animation sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` and `.button { transition: none }` under reduce, verified in glass-ui's compiled CSS; (4) tap targets 28x86.5 / 28x76.6 clear WCAG 2.5.8's 24px AA floor and do not appear in the audit's smallTapTargets rows for /#/; (5) the "Share color" -> "Copied!" swap cannot reflow the panel (width 214.6 is governed by the 148.6 tagline + 28 avatar, not the row); (6) `:focus-visible` matches on both triggers in Chromium with the producer focus-ring box-shadow present — I refused to score a focus gap from WebKit because macOS Full Keyboard Access is off (the harness's own MT-F022 note); (7) verbatimModuleSyntax: every import in the file is a value import, no type-only import to mis-declare; (8) forced-colors does not make the admin state colour-only — the literal word "admin" survives the UA override.

defects.defect: The certified accent ink on the Login/Profile dock trigger measures 3.43:1 rendered contrast in the light scheme (WCAG 1.4.3 floor 4.5:1 for 16.4px/700 normal text). Dark scheme fails on the neighbour: @mbabb measures 4.18:1.
defects.evidence: Pixel measurement on docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png over the glyph band x768-834, y30-50 CSS: ink=(170,0,67) L=0.0895, ground=(200,167,172) L=0.4290 -> 3.43:1. The ink equals the live computed `color: oklch(0.470927 0.188343 9.834023)` exactly, so the sample is the glyph core. Dark shot: @mbabb ink=(212,205,202) on (112,88,80) -> 4.18:1. Button's own background measured `oklab(0.721325 0.00492 0.010865 / 0.6)`.
defects.mechanism: Missing composite layer in the ink referent. demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:151-153 resolves the `chrome` rung from `.glass-dock`'s backgroundColor over the ambient — ONE alpha layer. The glyph composites over TWO: the dock band plus the Button's `glass-wash` capsule. The same two-layer divergence is documented and cured for `veil` at useContrastSafeColor.ts:154-206 and never migrated to the dock trigger. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1 ('a token name is not evidence') and PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.8.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=lab(92%25+88.8+20+/+82.7%25) at 1440x900 light. Sample the 'Login' glyph pixels and the pill background behind them; contrast = 3.43:1. Equivalently: getComputedStyle on the button returns color oklch(0.470927 0.188343 9.834023) and backgroundColor oklab(0.721325 .00492 .010865 / 0.6) over a dock band measured (246,169,194).
defects.proposedCure: Delete the wash from under the accent ink rather than teaching the certifier about it: glass-ui 7's `emphasis="quiet"` paints `background: transparent; box-shadow: none`, so the glyph composites on the one surface the `chrome` rung already models — the referent becomes true by construction and the control regains a real hover. If the wash must stay, add a `chrome-trigger` InkSurface probed off the MOUNTED button, the exact idiom `veil` already uses. System rule: an ink's referent is the mounted element's own painted stack, never a modelled tier.

defects.defect: The GitHub menu row renders as a broken two-line item — glyph on line 1, the word 'GitHub' on line 2, flush left instead of in the shared text column — in both schemes, desktop and mobile. It also nests a focusable <a href> inside [role=menuitem][tabindex=-1].
defects.evidence:
Rendered DOM:
…
— `as-child` (ProfileSection.vue:158) was not honoured. Computed: row display:flex gap:8px width 200.6; anchor display:block width 53.6 height 36.9. Row geometry (offsets within row): Share color icon 8/15 text 30/12.4 h44.0 | GitHub icon 8/6 text 8/21.9 h48.9 | Dark mode icon 8/10 text 32/12.4 h44.0. Mobile (iPhone 14): GitHub 55.4 vs 44.0 siblings. Visible in evidence-mbabb-menu-light.png and -dark.png.
defects.mechanism: glass-ui's DropdownMenuItem does not forward `as-child`, so the anchor stays a child of the item. As a shrink-to-fit block (53.6px) inside a 200.6px flex row it cannot hold a 14px glyph plus ' GitHub ' on one line, and wraps. Secondarily the anchor is focusable inside a roving-focus menu, so Tab can leave the menu's own order.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/ at 1440x900, click the @mbabb trigger. The GitHub row shows the octocat on one line and 'GitHub' beneath it, misaligned by 22-24px from the sibling text column, row 48.9px vs 44px.
defects.proposedCure: A link row IS a link: use the producer's supported `as="a"` on the item so exactly one element carries role=menuitem, the href and the row layout. Retire the hand-rolled 700-byte octocat <path> (duplicated byte-for-byte at ProfileSection.vue:161 and MobileMenuDropdown.vue:95) in favour of one system-owned icon so the menu's icon family stops mixing solid and 2px-stroke marks.

defects.defect: `variant="outline"` and `variant="ghost"` are not glass-ui 7 API. They ship as literal invalid DOM attributes and do nothing; both controls resolve to the same emphasis, so an account ACTION and an author WORDMARK render as materially identical capsules.
defects.evidence: glass-ui 7.0.0 Button props (dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js): emphasis|tone|size|iconOnly|loading|type|disabled|class|asChild|as — no `variant`. Emphasis vocabulary (components/button/styles.css): primary|secondary|quiet|text — no outline, no ghost. Rendered: <button data-emphasis="secondary" data-tone="neutral" data-size="xs" … variant="outline">Login</button> and … variant="ghost">@mbabb</button>. Measured identical backgroundColor oklab(0.721325 0.00492 0.010865 / 0.6), byte-identical 7-part box-shadow, border-radius 9999px on both.
defects.mechanism: Shadcn-era API addressed at a design system two majors on; the props fall through to $attrs. Both buttons therefore take the default emphasis="secondary", so the design-system lever that distinguishes an action from a credit is never pulled. Violates owner edicts 4 and 5 and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.8 ('Supporting fixtures do not compete … through equal size or equal shadow').
defects.reproduction: Inspect either dock trigger on http://localhost:9000/#/ — the `variant` attribute is present on the element and `data-emphasis` is `secondary` on both; computed backgroundColor and boxShadow strings are identical.
defects.proposedCure: Use `emphasis="quiet"` for the wordmark (it already ships `background: transparent; box-shadow: none; color: var(--muted-foreground)` plus the hover this file hand-rolls as `hover:text-foreground hover:underline underline-offset-4`), and the dock's own trigger family for the account seat. One edit also closes D-10's dark 4.18:1 (demo raises --muted-foreground to the ink floor), D-15 and D-17.

defects.defect: The accent `border-color` binding is dead code, shipped three lines below the comment that announces the retirement of exactly this cascade-dead accent.
defects.evidence: ProfileSection.vue:63 and :115 bind `:style="{ color: triggerInk, borderColor: triggerInk }"`. Live computed on the button: border-style: none, border-width: 0px, border-color: oklch(0.470927 0.188343 9.834023). Rendered attribute: style="… color: oklch(…); border-color: oklch(…)". The P9-R4 (Q10) comment at :103-110 states the outline variant paints via inset shadows with `border: none 0px` and that the cure was to move the accent to 'the channels the variant ACTUALLY paints'.
defects.mechanism: A per-instance inline paint aimed at a channel the producer does not render. The diagnosis was correct and the patch re-introduced the defect it diagnosed — the process failure and the design failure are the same shape.
defects.reproduction: getComputedStyle(loginButton) on http://localhost:9000/#/ returns borderStyle 'none', borderWidth '0px' with a non-default borderColor.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `borderColor` from both bindings; better, delete both bindings when D-1's cure lands and the ink becomes a producer token on a quiet trigger instead of an inline per-instance paint (owner edict 5).

defects.defect: The admin identity's gold shimmer is cascade-dead — the glyphs paint opaque gold over the text-clipped gradient — while the infinite `metal-shimmer-sweep` animation keeps running in the dock forever.
defects.evidence: ProfileSection.vue:96 sets style="border-color: var(--color-gold); color: var(--color-gold)" on a .gold-shimmer span. glass-ui's .gold-shimmer (dist/styles/utilities/base-misc.css) is `background: linear-gradient(…); background-clip: text; color: transparent` + `animation: metal-shimmer-sweep var(--duration-shimmer) linear infinite`. Live probe (transient injection of both spellings, removed in the same evaluate): with inline color -> color = oklch(0.751 0.147 84.199997), animationName = metal-shimmer-sweep; without inline color -> color = rgba(0,0,0,0), animationName = metal-shimmer-sweep.
defects.mechanism: An inline style attribute beats any author-layer rule, so `color: var(--color-gold)` overrides the utility's `color: transparent` and the clipped gradient is hidden behind opaque glyphs. The animation is unaffected and keeps repainting a gradient nobody can see. Sibling consumers (DockViewSelect.vue:135, PaletteCard.vue:64) set no inline color and work. Violates PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.5 (no decoration without information).
defects.reproduction: In any page that loads the app stylesheet: render admin next to admin — the first computes color oklch(0.751 0.147 84.2) (opaque, shimmer invisible), the second rgba(0,0,0,0) (shimmer visible); both report animationName metal-shimmer-sweep.
defects.proposedCure: Drop the inline `color`, keep the gold on a class (`border-gold`, the PaletteCard idiom), and let the producer's one metal register own the ink — this removes the dead decoration, the wasted compositing and one per-instance override in a single edit.

defects.defect: The theme glyph renders 16 x 24 px — non-square and 71% taller than every sibling icon — because the `aspect-square` class written to prevent exactly that is inert.
defects.evidence: Measured inside the open menu: Share2 `w-3.5 h-3.5` = 14x14; octocat `w-3.5 h-3.5` = 14x14 (fill solid rgb(28,25,23)); Sun/Moon `aspect-square w-4` = 16 wide x 24 tall, computed aspect-ratio '1 / 1', cssWidth 16px, cssHeight 24px, attrW/attrH 24/24. Row offsets confirm the optical break: icon y = 10 vs 15 and 6 for siblings.
defects.mechanism: Lucide SVGs carry width="24" height="24" presentation attributes. `w-4` overrides the width to 16px; nothing overrides the height, so the height stays definite at 24px and `aspect-ratio` is discarded. Per-instance glyph sizing (9 sites in this file) instead of the producer's rung — glass-ui already owns it via `.button > svg:not([class*="size-"]) { inline-size: var(--ui-glyph); block-size: var(--ui-glyph) }`. Violates PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.7 and owner edict 5.
defects.reproduction: Open the @mbabb menu at http://localhost:9000/#/ and read getBoundingClientRect on the three svgs: 14x14, 14x14, 16x24.
defects.proposedCure: Stop sizing glyphs per instance. Route every dock/menu icon through one `--ui-glyph` rung owned by the producer, and pick one icon family (all 2px-stroke outline) so a solid octocat never sits beside hairline marks.

defects.defect: Dark mode is a stateful toggle shipped as a stateless command: role=menuitem, aria-checked null, with the on/off truth carried only by an aria-hidden glyph — so the row is identical in both states to assistive tech.
defects.evidence: Measured on the live row: role 'menuitem', ariaChecked null. Rendered DOM shows <svg class="lucide lucide-sun … aspect-square w-4" aria-hidden="true"> plus the invariant text 'Dark mode'. demo/ui/dropdown-menu/index.ts re-exports `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` from glass-ui; it is unused in the dock. ProfileSection.vue:167-177 and its verbatim twin MobileMenuDropdown.vue:101-111.
defects.mechanism: The W44 comment frames the gap as glass-ui's missing `passive` DarkModeToggle (mark M1). The design system already ships the right primitive — a checkbox menu item — so the component asked for the wrong thing and hand-rolled a command in the meantime. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1 ('state/value … explicit', never colour-only).
defects.reproduction: Open the @mbabb menu, read the Dark mode row: getAttribute('role') === 'menuitem', getAttribute('aria-checked') === null, in both light and dark.
defects.proposedCure: Use `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` with `:model-value="isDark"`; the producer then owns the role, the checked state and the marker, and the decorative glyph question disappears. Withdraw mark M1's `passive` ask in favour of this.

defects.defect: Two copy actions in one menu with two different state designs — 'Share color' has a full success flourish, 'Copy slug' has no success state, no failure state, and leaves the menu open so the click appears to do nothing.
defects.evidence: ProfileSection.vue:154-157 swaps Share2->Check and 'Share color'->'Copied!' off `linkCopied` (App.vue:363, derived from linkCopyStatus === 'success'). ProfileSection.vue:77 emits copySlug -> Dock.vue:62 -> SlugEditLayer.vue:68-70: `function onCopySlug() { if (pm.userSlug.value) void writeClipboard(pm.userSlug.value); }` — the promise is explicitly discarded. Both rows carry @select.prevent, so neither closes the menu.
defects.mechanism: State design was applied per-row rather than per-verb. Clipboard denial, insecure context and an empty slug are all silent. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5 ('a transient flourish … never carries the only truth') and PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-08.
defects.reproduction: Log in, open the Profile menu, click 'Copy slug' — no icon change, no text change, no toast, menu stays open. Click 'Share color' in the sibling menu — Check + 'Copied!'.
defects.proposedCure: One copy affordance with one result state, shared by both rows and by every other copy seat in the shell, with an explicit failure arm — not two hand-rolled treatments in one 60-line template.

defects.defect: 'Regenerate slug' destroys the user's identity on a single click with no confirmation, no undo, no pending state and no result state — and is painted in the QUIETEST ink in the menu, below three reversible actions at normal weight.
defects.evidence: ProfileSection.vue:87-89: <DropdownMenuItem class="text-small gap-2 cursor-pointer text-muted-foreground" @click="pm.onRegenerateSlug()">. Rows above (Copy slug :77, Switch account :80, Logout :83) are all normal ink and all reversible. glass-ui exposes `tone="destructive"` (components/button/styles.css) — unused.
defects.mechanism: Consequence and emphasis are inverted: de-emphasis was used as visual hierarchy for 'secondary' when the row is in fact the most destructive. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §7 (Admin: 'dangerous confirmation') and PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-11.
defects.reproduction: Log in, open the Profile menu, click 'Regenerate slug' — the slug changes immediately with no confirm dialog and no visible result.
defects.proposedCure: Move destructive verbs out of the flat row list into a confirmed sub-step using the design system's destructive tone, with a durable result state on the entity (the same instrument D-8 needs).

defects.defect: The closed type matrix is broken in four places: control labels render Fira Code 700, and the dock band carries three families in ~190px with the heaviest label on the least-used control.
defects.evidence: Measured computed type in nav.dock-band: Home = Fraunces 16.4px/400; Tools = Plus Jakarta Sans 18.608px/400; Login = Fira Code 16.4px/700; @mbabb = Fira Code 16.4px/500. Menu tagline (ProfileSection.vue:150) = 11px Fraunces italic via `text-micro`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4: control/label -> text-small, Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold; text-mono-small (Fira Code) reserved for 'value, code, or provenance'; 'This matrix is closed across all eighteen compositions' with only P019's Picker pair exempt; `text-micro` is not a role in the matrix at all.
defects.mechanism: Four unilateral class choices (`text-mono-small font-bold` at :62 and :114, `text-micro` at :150) against a matrix the tranche declares closed. The rendered consequence is a hierarchy inversion — a mono bold 'Login' outweighs the route selector beside it.
defects.reproduction: getComputedStyle on the four dock controls at http://localhost:9000/#/ returns the families/weights above; visible in evidence-dock-light-3x.png.
defects.proposedCure: Control labels take `text-small`. If the dock wants a mono identity voice, amend §4 once with an argument rather than four class decisions in one file; help text takes `text-prose`.

defects.defect: `font-display` on DropdownMenuContent is a dead class at three sites; the producer's `--dropdown-menu-font` token owns the family, so the panel renders three type families at once.
defects.evidence: Live menu content: class = 'dropdown-menu-content dropdown-menu__content glass-reveal glass-floating min-w-menu font-display', computed fontFamily = "Fira Code", --dropdown-menu-font = '"Fira Code", "Fira Code Fallback", "Fira Mono", monospace'. glass-ui components/_shared/menu.css: `font-family: var(--dropdown-menu-font, inherit)`. Sites: ProfileSection.vue:70, :143, MobileMenuDropdown.vue:43. Rendered panel 215x223 carries Fira Code container/handle, Plus Jakarta rows, Fraunces italic tagline.
defects.mechanism: Consumer styled by class where a producer token exists (owner edict 5). The class loses and the intended display voice never appears.
defects.reproduction: Open the @mbabb menu and read getComputedStyle(menuContent).fontFamily — 'Fira Code', despite the font-display class on the same element.
defects.proposedCure: Set `--dropdown-menu-font` once at the shell root for every dock menu and delete the class from all three sites.

defects.defect: The avatar's failure state was never designed: with the image host unreachable the identity mark becomes a 28x28 fully transparent hole. The app's chrome also makes a third-party network request on every menu open.
defects.evidence: Probe with avatars.githubusercontent.com blocked, menu re-opened: img { complete: true, naturalWidth: 0, display: 'none' }; avatar box { w: 28, h: 28, backgroundColor: 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)', text: '' }; hasFallback: false. Screenshot evidence-avatar-offline.png. `AvatarFallback` is exported by glass-ui and re-exported at demo/ui/avatar/index.ts:1, unused. Sites: ProfileSection.vue:145-147, MobileMenuDropdown.vue:80-82.
defects.mechanism: An unhandled state — image error — in a component whose identity block depends on a hard-coded external URL (https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/2848617?v=4).
defects.reproduction: Block avatars.githubusercontent.com (devtools request blocking or an offline profile), reload http://localhost:9000/#/, open the @mbabb menu: an empty 28px gap sits where the avatar was, with the handle and tagline hanging off nothing.
defects.proposedCure: Add `AvatarFallback` (the design system already ships it) and inline the mark as a local asset so the dock's identity does not depend on a third-party host being reachable.

defects.defect: The desktop and mobile menus are two hand-maintained copies of one component, already drifted three measurable ways — and at 200% zoom a single device crosses the seam, losing the account affordance and the theme control from the band entirely.
defects.evidence: Duplicated verbatim between ProfileSection.vue and MobileMenuDropdown.vue: the 700-byte octocat <path> (:161 / :95), the avatar/handle/tagline block (:144-152 / :79-87), the Share row (:154-157 / :88-91), the Dark-mode row AND its six-line comment (:167-177 / :101-111). Drift: admin state = gold+shimmer pill in the band (:96) vs muted-foreground pill inside the menu (:67); a DropdownMenuSeparator precedes 'Regenerate slug' on desktop (:86) and is absent on mobile (:60->:61); logged-out is a band Button (:111) vs a menu row (:71). 200% arm: shots/zoom-200-desktop/picker.png (720 CSS px @2x) shows the dock as `Home v | Picker About | ...` with ProfileSection absent; STATES.json confirms the nodes are present-but-hidden (body text still contains 'Login  @mbabb').
defects.mechanism: `hidden lg:flex` (:48, :127) plus `lg:hidden` (twin :38) forks the component by breakpoint into two source files, so one state ('I am an administrator') has two identities. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.7 ('No desktop-tight/mobile-airy fork and no breakpoint pile') and §3.6.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/ at 1440x900 and again at 720x450 with deviceScaleFactor 2 (the 200% zoom arm) — the Login/@mbabb capsules are present in the first and absent in the second, replaced by the mobile twin's overflow menu. Compare the admin branch of the two files for the gold/muted divergence.
defects.proposedCure: One menu component with one content model and two presentations chosen by a container query. The twin, the drift and the 200%-zoom seam die together.

defects.defect: In RTL the author wordmark renders as `mbabb@` — the neutral `@` reorders to the end. The slug pill and the handle link have the same defect.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/rtl-desktop/picker.png, crop saved as evidence-rtl-wordmark.png: the dock reads `mbabb@ | Login | Tools | Home`. No dir="ltr" or <bdi> on ProfileSection.vue:140 (wordmark), :75 (slug pill), :149 (handle link). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6.1: 'CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose'; §5.2 last row repeats it for slugs/IDs.
defects.mechanism: Unisolated bidi-neutral characters in a direction-inheriting container. The mark is data, not prose, and was never wrapped.
defects.reproduction: document.documentElement.setAttribute('dir','rtl') on http://localhost:9000/#/ (the harness's post-load flip, states.mjs MT-F022 #1) — the wordmark reads 'mbabb@'.
defects.proposedCure: One <bdi>/dir="ltr" primitive for every handle, slug, ID and provenance rendering in the shell — the constitution already legislates this species, so it belongs in the shared idiom, not three ad-hoc spans.

defects.defect: Each trigger paints a desaturated neutral slab inside its own chromatic capsule, and states its boundary three times: capsule ring, inner wash edge, and a DockSeparator on each side.
defects.evidence: Pixel scan of shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png at y=40.5 CSS: band (246,169,194) chromatic; Login border box x757.7-844.2; wash slab x767.5-834.0 measured (200,167,172) near-neutral; separators at x=746.5 and x=854.0 (1px). ProfileSection.vue:49 and :123 emit the two DockSeparators. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §2: 'One surface has one tier. An inner card is not automatically another pane of glass.' PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.4/PR-05: spacing plus material already expressing the boundary makes the line duplicative.
defects.mechanism: A page-primitive Button (neutral `glass-wash`) dropped into a chromatic dock band, inset ~10px from its own capsule, adds a second material tier and a second edge inside one control; the separators then add a third statement of the same boundary.
defects.reproduction: Sample any horizontal row through the dock band in the light capture between x=740 and x=940 CSS: BAND -> separator -> band -> GRAY slab -> band -> separator -> band -> GRAY slab.
defects.proposedCure: `emphasis="quiet"` removes the wash and the inner boundary; the capsule ring plus the band's gap already separate the controls, so both DockSeparators go. One edit closes D-1, D-3, D-15 and D-16 together.

defects.defect: The two seats this component owns are 28px tall in a 32px band, and both of its separators are off-centre in their gaps — in opposite directions.
defects.evidence: Measured seat rects in nav.dock-band at 1440px: Home x496.3 w106.9 h32; Tools x626.2 w104.5 h32; Login x757.7 w86.5 h28; @mbabb x867.2 w76.6 h28. Separator positions from the pixel scan: x=746.5 (15.8px of air from Tools' right edge 730.7, 10.2px to Login's left edge 757.7) and x=854.0 (9.8px from Login's right edge 844.2, 12.2px to @mbabb's left edge 867.2).
defects.mechanism: `size="xs"` (--control-h-xs) is a valid glass-ui size but the wrong rung for a dock seat, and the component's local `gap-1` nests inside the dock layer's own gap, so the hairlines land off-centre by 3-5px in opposite directions. Violates PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §1 (every element earns its scale and interval from its job) and §5.8.
defects.reproduction: getBoundingClientRect on the four dock controls at 1440x900 returns heights 32/32/28/28; pixel-scan the light capture for the two 1px separator columns at CSS x=746.5 and x=854.0.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the dock's own trigger seat height so the band has one silhouette, and let the dock layer own ALL inter-seat spacing (delete the component-local gap) so any surviving hairline is centred by construction.

defects.defect: Two adjacent controls speak two different hover languages; the account action's entire hover feedback is 1.3px of scale.
defects.evidence: Measured rest->hover with a real pointer (Chromium): Login color oklch(0.4712 …) -> unchanged, background unchanged, scale 1 -> 1.015, no underline. @mbabb color oklab(0 0 0 / 0.7) -> rgb(0,0,0), scale 1 -> 1.015, text-decoration none -> underline. 1.5% of an 86.5px pill = 1.3px.
defects.mechanism: The inline `color` (D-4) pins the Login ink so no hover rule can move it, and `emphasis="secondary"` ships no hover background — only `quiet` does. The neighbour meanwhile gets a hand-rolled class hover.
defects.reproduction: Hover each dock trigger at http://localhost:9000/#/ and read getComputedStyle: Login's color and backgroundColor are identical at rest and on hover.
defects.proposedCure: Same as D-3: `emphasis="quiet"` gives both controls the producer's one hover language (background + ink), and the inline paint disappears.

defects.defect: The file is four components wearing one name: two sibling roots owning account identity, a product action (Share color), an outbound vanity link, and the application's ONLY theme control — all gated behind `lg:`.
defects.evidence: ProfileSection.vue:48 and :127 are two top-level roots, both `hidden lg:flex`. Jobs: account (:52-121), Share color (:154-157), GitHub link (:158-165), dark mode (:167-177). Repo-wide grep confirms toggleDark() is called from exactly two places — this file and its mobile twin.
defects.mechanism: Cohesion failure: a global system preference is discoverable only by opening a personal credit menu, and the one row a colour-picker user wants ('Share color') is filed under someone's name. Two roots also weld the account and author blocks to import order — the parent cannot place them independently. Violates owner edict 1.
defects.reproduction: Read the template: two root <div>s, four unrelated jobs; open the @mbabb menu to find the app's theme control as its last row.
defects.proposedCure: Three components — DockAccount, DockAuthor, and a DockThemeControl that is a first-class dock seat (its own DropdownMenuCheckboxItem or dock control) rather than the last row of a credit menu.

defects.defect: The same seat has two identities for tooling: the logged-in trigger carries a test hook, the logged-out trigger does not.
defects.evidence: ProfileSection.vue:64 `data-o18="profile-trigger"` on the logged-in Profile trigger; the logged-out Login trigger (:111-120) has no hook. All 60 captures in REPORT.json are the logged-out state.
defects.mechanism: The attribute was attached to a branch rather than to the seat, so any probe keyed on it silently measures nothing in the state most visitors are in.
defects.reproduction: querySelector('[data-o18="profile-trigger"]') on http://localhost:9000/#/ returns null while a Login trigger is visibly present.
defects.proposedCure: When the two branches collapse into one seat (D-18's DockAccount), the hook belongs to the seat, not to a branch.

defects.defect: States never designed: loading/pending, error, disabled, long-slug truncation, the admin logout path, and the logged-in trigger showing the word 'Profile' instead of the user's identity.
defects.evidence: No pending or failure state on pm.userLogout() (:83), pm.onRegenerateSlug() (:87) or copySlug (:77) — glass-ui's Button ships an unused `loading` prop. `whitespace-nowrap` on every label including the slug pill (:73-75) with no truncation rule. The admin branch (:95-99) renders a static, cursor-default pill with no menu, so an admin without a userSlug has no logout affordance anywhere in the dock (usePalettePorts.ts:57 destructures only isAuthenticated and login from useAdminAuth). The logged-in trigger reads 'Profile' (:67) while the admin and logged-out states both put their identity ('admin', 'Login') in the band.
defects.mechanism: State coverage was designed for the happy path of one branch. A state that was never designed is a design defect.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis for the admin-logout and long-slug arms (they need an admin token / a long slug I did not mint); the loading/error/disabled gaps are read directly from the template and the ports.
defects.proposedCure: Enumerate the account seat's states once (empty, identified, admin, pending, failed, offline) and give each a designed treatment in one component, with the identity — not the word 'Profile' — in the band.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/shell/PaneSegmentedControl.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Matches the explicit Opus 5 declaration at spawn; seat is declared, not inherited. NOT a defect.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — the component is homed one directory above its only consumer. `demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:15` (`import PaneSegmentedControl from "../PaneSegmentedControl.vue"`) is the UNIQUE case of the `dock/` module reaching outside itself for a component; every other `../` edge out of `dock/*.vue` carries a key or a type, never an SFC. Root cause is a single mis-homing: `git show --name-status --find-renames 6dc12aad` shows `R100 demo/@/components/custom/panes/PaneSegmentedControl.vue -> demo/shell/PaneSegmentedControl.vue`, a zero-content rename in the W43b "panes/ 16->0, distribute to feature homes" commit — routed by its NAME ("Pane...") instead of by its CONSUMER (the dock). Combined with L-7 (its entire content is a `0|1 <-> "0"|"1"` coercion behind four dead guards), the cure is deletion, not relocation — which is exactly what the W47 gate `PaneSegmentedControl 1->0` means.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but these specific suspicions were checked and cleared, recorded so the report is not one-sided: (1) DEEP-IMPORT — the component has exactly 2 imports, `vue` and `@mkbabb/glass-ui/tabs`; the latter is a real published subpath, verified `node -e "require('./node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json').exports['./tabs']"` -> `{"types":"./dist/tabs.d.ts","import":"./dist/tabs.js"}` at version 7.0.0, and `SegmentedTabs` is a named export of it (`dist/components/tabs/index.d.ts:1`). A real consumer could write this import verbatim. (2) VALUE.JS PUBLIC-SURFACE FALSE PROOF — the component imports value.js not at all; and repo-wide `grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/value.js"' demo/ | wc -l` = 0 while `package.json#exports` has NO "." root key (only ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize) — the two facts agree, so no demo import depends on an unresolvable root entry. `vite.config.ts:37-50` generates the self-alias set FROM the exports map by anchored regex, so a demo import a published consumer could not write cannot resolve either. (3) GOD MODULE — 52 lines, 18 of them a style comment; the opposite failure. (4) DUAL IMPLEMENTATION — only 3 `SegmentedTabs` sites exist in demo/ (`workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:105`, `palettes/browser/admin/AdminNamesPanel.vue:14`, this file); each models a different domain and only this one wraps it. The named historical suspects (ActionBarLayer's useLayerTransition shim, palettes/export.ts vs usePaletteExport.ts, the three useDark stores) were checked and none touch this component's graph. (5) EDICT 7/8 — reactive props destructure at `:20` is the correct Vue 3.5 form; both imports are value imports so `verbatimModuleSyntax` is vacuously satisfied. (6) `class="font-display"` at `:10` is deliberately NOT charged as an edict-5 violation: `class` is a declared prop (`SegmentedTabs.vue.d.ts:94`) and `.segmented-tab { font: inherit }` (`segmented.css:1`) is the producer's designed inheritance hook — measured `fontFamily: "Fraunces..."` on both tabs, working as glass-ui intends. defects.mechanism: A density variant implemented as a consumer-side :deep() patch instead of a producer prop. Violates Edict 5 (never per-instance overrides — the SFC comment's 'ROOT-LEVEL' claim is true only of the consumer's root, which is exactly the per-instance case) and Edict 4 (variants belong in glass-ui).
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at 390x844, expand the dock, read getComputedStyle on .segmented-tab (pasted above); diff against segmented.css.
defects.proposedCure: Relay to the glass-ui BI/BJ inbox per the standing relay edict: add a `density="compact"` (or `size="sm"`) prop to SegmentedTabs; delete the <style scoped> block; pass the prop at the call site. This is the transposition that makes C-1's inlining lossless and C-9's gate problem disappear.

defects.defect: `v-if="leftLabel && rightLabel"` is a dead masking guard, and the `string | null` prop type is unreachable. If the guard ever did fire, the mobile pane switcher would vanish silently and the right pane would become unreachable on mobile, with no console error and no test failure.
defects.evidence: Dock.vue:200-201 passes `... ?? ''`, so null never reaches the props (making the component's own `?? ""` at PaneSegmentedControl.vue:31-32 dead too). Dock.vue:197 already gates on `currentConfig.value.right !== null`, so the only null-right config (atmosphere, demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:170-178) never reaches the component. All 14 VIEW_MAP entries with right !== null carry non-empty leftLabel AND rightLabel (viewSchema.ts:104-233, checked row by row). PaneConfig.leftLabel is typed `string`, non-nullable (viewSchema.ts:73) — the component widens it to `string | null`.
defects.mechanism: Defensive v-if retained after its callers were tightened — a masking fallback, banned by Edict 2.
defects.reproduction: NONE — dead code, established by enumerating the 14 VIEW_MAP rows against Dock.vue:197-201.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the guard and narrow the props to `leftLabel: string; rightLabel: string`. Post-C-1, drop the props entirely and build options from currentConfig at the Dock — the label plumbing stops existing rather than being made total.

defects.defect: `Number(v) as 0 | 1` launders the producer's `string` emit contract through an unchecked cast into a `Ref<0|1>`. Any value outside {"0","1"} yields NaN, which the cast asserts is 0|1 and stores.
defects.evidence: Producer emit signature, SegmentedTabs.vue.d.ts: `"update:modelValue": (value: string) => any`. Consumer, PaneSegmentedControl.vue:11: `(v) => emit('update:modelValue', Number(v) as 0 | 1)`. Landing site, demo/shell/useViewManager.ts:67-69: `set: (v) => { paneOverride.value = { view: currentView.value, index: v } }`. Downstream failure path read in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useTabRovingFocus-YnWh-Ytr.js: with String(NaN)="NaN" no option matches, `if (e < 0) { ...opacity: "0" }` fires and neither button carries aria-pressed="true"; demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:180's `mobilePaneIndex.value === 1` then silently resolves to the left pane.
defects.mechanism: `as` used as a boundary crossing instead of a narrowing predicate — the repo's banned masking idiom in type clothing.
defects.reproduction: NONE — HYPOTHESIS. Currently unreachable because tabOptions (PaneSegmentedControl.vue:30-33) hardcodes "0"/"1". The cast is the only thing standing between the producer's string contract and a Ref<0|1>.
defects.proposedCure: `(v) => emit('update:modelValue', v === "1" ? 1 : 0)` — total, no cast. Post-C-1 the whole string↔number seam disappears if the Dock stores the pane as the option value directly.

defects.defect: `class="font-display"` is a per-instance typographic override applied to the producer's root, and it is applied inconsistently — two of the three SegmentedTabs consumers pass it, one does not, so two different segmented-tab typographic voices ship in one application.
defects.evidence: MEASURED: computed fontFamily on .segmented-tab = `Fraunces, "Fraunces Fallback", serif`, sourced from PaneSegmentedControl.vue:10. The producer's .segmented-tab deliberately declares `font: inherit` (segmented.css). Survey: PaneSegmentedControl.vue:10 yes; demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminNamesPanel.vue:16 yes; demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:105 NO. Visible in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-mobile-light/picker.png — the dock pill reads "Picker | About" in the Fraunces serif.
defects.mechanism: A design decision expressed as a utility class at 2 of 3 call sites instead of as a producer variant — Edicts 4 and 5.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at 390x844, read getComputedStyle(.segmented-tab).fontFamily → Fraunces; compare against the three-row consumer survey.
defects.proposedCure: Decide once, in glass-ui. If the display face is right for segmented tabs it is a producer `type` variant; if it is right only for app chrome then MixSourceSelector is the bug. Either way it stops being three independent class strings.

defects.defect: The drag-morph indicator is armed by omission (`motion` never passed), which makes the ACTIVE half of a 121px-wide control pointer-dead and hands its hit area to a velocity-squash drag indicator with touch-action:none.
defects.evidence: MEASURED: indicator class list `segmented-indicator segmented-indicator--js glass-capsule glass-lens glass-drag-grabbable`, touchAction "none"; and pointerEvents "none" on the aria-pressed="true" button. The rule: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/tabs/styles/drag.css — `.segmented-tabs:not(.segmented-tabs--underline):has(.segmented-indicator.glass-drag-grabbable) .segmented-tab[aria-pressed="true"] { pointer-events: none; }`. Track measured 121.02px wide; each tab 57.51x26.27. Also: data-motion rendered null on the group despite the drag being armed — a producer inconsistency worth a relay line, not a consumer defect.
defects.mechanism: A heavy interaction mode adopted by omission — the producer's richest default landing in a 2-state toggle inside a 121px dock aperture.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at 390x844, expand the dock, read getComputedStyle on the .segmented-indicator and the aria-pressed="true" .segmented-tab (pasted above). No user-visible action is lost (the active tab is already selected), so this is INFO, not a break.
defects.proposedCure: Pass motion="reduced" at the call site — click-only strip, roving focus preserved — or justify the drag deliberately in the wave spec.

result.strongestDefect: C-3 — the control takes role="group" + aria-pressed from the unpassed `semantics` default while taking selection-follows-focus from the unpassed `activation` default, and populates no `controls`, against a pane slot (App.vue:77-91) with no id, no role=tabpanel and no aria-live. Measured: role="group", ariaLabel null, aria-controls null, roving tabindex -1/0, aria-pressed true/false. Producer source (useTabRovingFocus-YnWh-Ytr.js) commits the selection on arrow-key focus move, and with exactly two options the index wraps, so either arrow flips the pane on every press — each press driving a full PaneSlot rAF-deferred KeepAlive remount of the app's main content, announced by nothing. It is the only finding whose consequence reaches a real user on a keypress alone, it has a one-line cure, and it SURVIVES the W47 1→0 cure (inlining moves it rather than killing it), so the wave must carry it.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so no global negative is claimed — but eleven hazard classes were tested and came back CLEAN, and reporting them is part of the evidence discipline. (1) TAP TARGETS PASS: measured 57.51x26.27px per tab at 390w; 26.27 >= the 24px floor, which is exactly why this control appears in NEITHER the smallTapTargets nor namelessButtons rows of docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json — safari-mobile-light /#/ lists 8 (one input 160x20, three 23x23 slug buttons, four 12x44 channel spans) and /#/palettes lists 4, none of them a segmented tab. This component contributes 0 of the measured 60 small-tap-target defects and 0 of the 18 nameless buttons. (2) No defineModel() — explicit prop + explicit emit, so the WritableComputedRef stale-read hazard and its shallowRef cure do not apply. (3) No colour code at all: no oklch→HSV roundtrip, no stableHue, no ValueUnit wrapping, no parseCssColor — every repo colour hazard class is absent. (4) No requestAnimationFrame, no listeners, no observers, no timers, no async: zero cleanup surface, so zero leak surface (the producer's ResizeObserver in useSelectionIndicator does disconnect in onUnmounted — read and verified). (5) No unbounded growth: tabOptions is a 2-element computed over two scalars. (6) Vue 3.5 reactive props destructure is correct and the computed re-derives — verified live, re-routing /#/palettes → /#/mix re-labels the tabs (activeText read back as "Mix"), and walk.spec.ts:141-149 gates it. (7) verbatimModuleSyntax satisfied — no type-only imports to mis-declare. (8) Edict 6 not engaged — no animations deleted, no keyframes added; indicator/squash motion is producer-owned and untouched. (9) Keyboard activation is NOT broken: Enter/Space fall through to the native <button type="button"> click even in automatic mode (the roving handler breaks out of its Enter/Space case when activation !== manual) — C-3 is about semantics and unintended commits, not a dead key path. (10) Zero console or page errors attributable to this component across all 60 REPORT.json captures (the matrix's sole console error is safari-desktop-light /#/ "WebGL: context lost.", HeroBlob's). (11) Zero horizontal overflow on every mobile capture (overflowX: 0) and the 121.02px track fits the 312px aperture with room — the S.W7-2 fit objective it was built for IS met.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) underneath demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m]) — matches the explicit declaration this seat was spawned with; not inherited, not undeclared.

defects.defect: PaneSlot owns the application's ONLY <KeepAlive> and publishes no activation contract. It converts onUnmounted from "runs on navigation" to "runs never" for 11 pane components. Four global-listener sites tear down only in onUnmounted/onBeforeUnmount and therefore leak across every route. The demo has ONE onActivated and ZERO onDeactivated in the entire tree.
defects.evidence: KeepAlive owner: demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120 (sole mounted KeepAlive in demo/). Census `grep -rn "onActivated|onDeactivated" demo/` -> only demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:27,246; zero onDeactivated. Leaking sites: demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:377 (window keydown, removed only at :382 onUnmounted); demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/composables/useSliderTouchGates.ts:124 (document pointercancel, removed at :127 onUnmounted); demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:239 (window keydown, removed at :243 onBeforeUnmount); demo/picker/composables/usePointerDebug.ts:227-232 (6 capture-phase document listeners). LIVE PROOF (Playwright evaluate walking #app.__vue_app__ KeepAlive.__v_cache at /#/atmosphere): {"key":"color-picker","comp":"ColorPicker","isUnmounted":false,"isDeactivated":true,"scopeActive":false}. Vue 3.5.35; runtime-core.cjs.js:6572-6598 shows the shapeFlag&256 deactivate branch returns before unmountComponent. Swallowed handler body: ColorPicker.vue:249-267 -> `if (keys.cmd?.value && keys.k?.value) { e.preventDefault(); ... }`.
defects.mechanism: KeepAlive lifecycle contract minted at one boundary and published at none — the owner's 23-line header (PaneSlot.vue:2-23) documents transition mode, the onMount prop and the appear grammar, but never states that mounting here disables onUnmounted. Eleven pane authors are asked to remember a rule nobody wrote down.
defects.reproduction: 1) start dev server (live, http://localhost:9000). 2) navigate to /#/ (ColorPicker mounts, registers window keydown). 3) navigate to /#/atmosphere. 4) evaluate: walk document.querySelector('#app').__vue_app__._instance subtree, find KeepAlive instances, read __v_cache. The 'color-picker' entry reports isUnmounted:false, isDeactivated:true. Since ColorPicker.vue:382 is the sole removeEventListener site and it lives in onUnmounted, the window keydown listener is live on /#/atmosphere.
defects.proposedCure: Do not ask 11 pane authors to remember onDeactivated — delete the ability to get it wrong. Give the shell ONE owned window keydown listener plus a `useShellKey(binding)` registration composable in demo/shell/, gated on the active route; migrate ColorPicker.vue:377, ImageEyedropper.vue:239, useSliderTouchGates.ts:124 onto it. One listener, one owner, hazard unrepresentable by construction. Rename PaneSlot -> PaneHost and state the activation contract in its first paragraph.

defects.defect: The mobile PaneSlot instance omits `:on-mount`, so `colorPickerRef` is provably always null at mobile viewports. Six affordances become silent no-ops (dock action bar, commit-edit, cancel-edit, two palette-pane edit emits, emitApply/emitSetCurrentColor fallbacks) and the palette->edit path stalls 2000 ms then console.warns and abandons.
defects.evidence: colorPickerRef.value has exactly ONE writer: demo/color-picker/App.vue:325, inside onDesktopLeftMount (App.vue:323-328). `grep -n "on-mount" demo/color-picker/App.vue` returns ONLY :105 (desktop-left) and :131 (desktop-right). The mobile slot at App.vue:83-91 passes component/component-key/component-props/transition-name/max/appear/on-appeared and NO :on-mount. Breakpoint gate: App.vue:310-312 `(min-width: 1024px) and (min-aspect-ratio: 1.1)`. Dead consumers: App.vue:38 `:action-bar="colorPickerRef?.actionBarContext ?? null"`, App.vue:41 `@commit-edit="colorPickerRef?.commitEdit(); ..."`, App.vue:42 cancel-edit, demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:156-157, demo/color-picker/composables/usePaletteWiring.ts:66-72 and :122-126. Stall: usePaletteWiring.ts:33-58 `PICKER_WAIT_ATTEMPTS = 40` x `setTimeout(poll, 50)` = 2000 ms, then console.warn('[usePaletteWiring] gave up waiting for the color picker to mount (startEdit).'); reached from emitStartEdit at :106-119. Affected surface captured at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-mobile-light/palettes.png.
defects.mechanism: A whole-application capability (edit commit) is wired per-slot-instance by hand in the template. Three slots, two wirings, nothing in the type system to catch the third — `onMount?` is an OPTIONAL prop. Every downstream call site then masks the omission with `?.`, so the failure is silent rather than loud.
defects.reproduction: Static enumeration is complete and airtight: the sole writer of colorPickerRef.value (App.vue:325) is inside onDesktopLeftMount, which is bound only at App.vue:105 (desktop-left slot). Therefore under `!isDesktop` (App.vue:77 v-if branch) colorPickerRef is null for the session lifetime. Runtime signature to observe: load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at 390x844, click a saved palette colour's edit affordance, watch the console — the [usePaletteWiring] give-up warning fires ~2 s later and the edit never starts.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the onMount ref-capture channel entirely. Panes that expose commands REGISTER them into a `PANE_COMMANDS_KEY` registry provided once by App.vue, filling their slice in onActivated and clearing it in onDeactivated. The shell reads `commands.picker?.commitEdit`. One home, provided once, structurally identical at every breakpoint — and whenColorPickerReady's 2 s poll, the PaneActionRefs Ref<any> triple, and eight `?.()` maskings die in the same commit.

defects.defect: PaneSlot's documented onMount contract is factually false — it fires on EVERY re-render, not on mount/unmount — and because the component swap is deferred one rAF while the action bar switches synchronously, App.vue files the OUTGOING pane's instance under the INCOMING pane's ref for a full frame.
defects.evidence: JSDoc claim: PaneSlot.vue:47-51 'Called with the component instance on mount, and with null on unmount.' P1 repro (jsdom + vue 3.5.35, faithful transcription): `after 5 prop ticks refCalls = ["PaneA","PaneA","PaneA","PaneA","PaneA"]`. Mechanism in Vue source: PaneSlot.vue:124 writes a fresh inline arrow every render (`:ref="onMount ? (el: any) => onMount!(el) : undefined"`); runtime-core.cjs.js:5476 re-runs setRef on every patch; setRef's stale-ref branch (runtime-core.cjs.js:1801-1817) handles only string and Ref old-refs, never a function. liveProps updates every colour tick (PaneSlot.vue:101-106). P2 repro (adds App.vue:323-328 verbatim): `t1 (config switched, PRE-rAF) generatePaneRef = ColorPicker; paneRefs.generate.value?.regenerate?.() -> SILENT NO-OP`; `t2 (post-rAF) generatePaneRef = GeneratePane -> regenerated`. Two clocks: usePaneRouter.ts:188-201 switches the action bar off viewManager.currentView synchronously; PaneSlot.vue:86-97 defers the component swap by one requestAnimationFrame.
defects.mechanism: Three independent readings of 'which pane is live': the action bar reads the route synchronously, the slot's ref lands one rAF late, and onDesktopLeftMount resolves WHICH ref to fill from currentConfig at callback time rather than from the instance it was handed. No single owner of pane identity.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/paneslot-repro.mjs and node scratchpad/appvue-repro.mjs (jsdom + the repo's own vue 3.5.35, PaneSlot.vue and App.vue:323-328 transcribed verbatim). Outputs pasted in evidence. In the live app: switch the left pane from picker to generate and click the dock's Regenerate button within the same frame — the handler dispatches onto the ColorPicker instance and `undefined?.()` silently succeeds.
defects.proposedCure: Same architectural cure as L-2: panes register their own commands, so an instance can only ever file itself under its own identity and the rAF deferral stops racing the command surface. Independently, the onMount JSDoc must not survive as written — it is load-bearing documentation that is measurably wrong.

defects.defect: usePaneRouter.ts is a four-concern god module (component registry + prop factories + three slot computeds + the dock action-bar type and data), and the dock imports its own types back out of it. Its action tables encode nine private method names of three feature panes, reached through Ref<any> and invoked with double-optional calls.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts (231 lines): registry :69-95; prop factories :126-161; slot computeds :163-184; DockAction/DockActionBar types :38-58 and per-view action tables :186-228. Its own header announces the aggregation ('folds in useGenericActionBar', 'the retired useDockActionBar.ts'). Back-imports: demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:24 `import type { DockActionBar } from "../usePaneRouter"`; demo/shell/dock/layers/GenericActionBar.vue:4 `import type { DockAction } from "../../usePaneRouter"`. Feature internals encoded at :196-223: regenerate, save, copyColors, reset, copyCSS, seedFromPalette, clearSelection, startMix, copyResult — reached via PaneActionRefs `{ generate: Ref<any>; gradient: Ref<any>; mix: Ref<any> }` (:107-111) and called as `paneRefs.generate.value?.regenerate?.()`.
defects.mechanism: Deliberate consolidation of four separable concerns into one file, justified in its own header as de-duplication. The result is that the dock (whose components are the ONLY consumers of DockAction/DockActionBar) must reach two directories into a routing module for its own vocabulary, and the router holds untypeable knowledge of three panes' private APIs.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a structural finding, established by reading the file and its two back-importers. Its runtime consequence is reproduced separately under L-3 (the double-optional call silently succeeding against the wrong instance).
defects.proposedCure: Split by concern along lines the areas already suggest: shell/panes/registry.ts (name -> loader, nothing else), shell/panes/props.ts, and shell/dock/actions.ts owning DockAction/DockActionBar AND the per-view tables beside the only components that consume them. Replace the Ref<any> handles with the typed command registry of L-2, at which point `?.()` becomes a compile error instead of a silent success.

defects.defect: The shell statically depends on the palettes FEATURE for a PLATFORM capability. 54 of the dock's 135 statically-reachable files (40%) are palette-feature files, pulled in because five shell components inject SESSION_PORT_KEY from demo/palettes/usePalettePorts — while the correct direct edge to demo/platform/auth/useSession already exists and is already used one directory over. Two homes for one concept.
defects.evidence: Measured static import closure (scratchpad/closure.mjs): `demo/shell/dock/index.ts — STATIC closure: 135 files` with `{"demo/shell":21,"demo/color-session":19,"demo/picker":16,"demo/shared":2,"demo/platform":10,"demo/ui":12,"demo/palettes":54,"demo/color-picker":1}`; `demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts — STATIC closure: 115 files` with the same 54 palettes. Shortest violating edge (scratchpad/path.mjs BFS): `demo/shell/dock/index.ts -> demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue -> demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts`. Five injectors: Dock.vue:18, DockViewSelect.vue:8, menus/ProfileSection.vue:14, menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue:13, layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:5. usePalettePorts.ts is a 17-composable aggregator (:4-17) that merely re-provides demo/platform/auth/useSession (:7). The correct edge in the SAME subtree: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:133 `import { useSession } from "../../platform/auth/useSession"`. Type-level back-edge closing the loop: usePalettePorts.ts:19 `import type { ViewId } from "../shell/useViewManager"`.
defects.mechanism: A platform capability (session identity) was re-exported through a feature aggregator, and the shell bound to the aggregator instead of the platform. Because the aggregator wires 17 palette composables, every shell consumer of session drags the whole feature into the shell's static graph — and the same subtree now reaches one concept two different ways.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/closure.mjs (transitive static-import walk over demo/, resolving relative specifiers only) and node scratchpad/path.mjs (BFS shortest violating path). Both outputs pasted in evidence and reproducible against HEAD c654824e.
defects.proposedCure: Move SESSION_PORT_KEY and its provide to demo/platform/auth/. Five one-line import rewrites; the shell's static closure sheds 54 palette files outright; the dual path collapses onto the edge ColorInput.vue:133 already uses correctly. Enforce with one lint rule: app -> shell -> panes -> features -> platform, nothing imports app/.

defects.defect: Two feature modules import UPWARD into the application root's private boot/ directory. Aggravated by inverted directory naming: demo/color-picker/ is the application (index.html, App.vue, router/, Vite root) while demo/picker/ is the ColorPicker component — and the feature imports the app.
defects.evidence: BFS from this seat's area (scratchpad/path.mjs): `demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts -> demo/picker/index.ts -> demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue -> demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useOverture.ts`. The two edges, exhaustively (`grep -rn "\.\./color-picker/|\.\./\.\./color-picker/" demo/picker demo/palettes demo/workbenches demo/scenes demo/shell`): demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:129 `import { OVERTURE_KEY } from "../color-picker/composables/boot/useOverture"`; demo/scenes/atmosphere/aurora-harmony-stops.ts:23 `import { resolveCalibratedAtmosphere } from "../../color-picker/composables/boot/atmosphere-calibration"`. demo/color-picker/ is the Vite root in dev and gh-pages (vite.config.ts `root: "./demo/color-picker/"`) and holds index.html, App.vue, ErrorBoundary.vue, router/, public/, composables/boot/.
defects.mechanism: Canonical wrong-direction edge: the app composes features, so features must not reach back into the composition. Two directories one word apart (demo/color-picker/ vs demo/picker/) with opposite roles made the inversion invisible at review time.
defects.reproduction: NONE for a runtime symptom — this is a module-graph fact, established by grep and by the BFS in scratchpad/path.mjs. Both edges are byte-verifiable at the cited file:line.
defects.proposedCure: OVERTURE_KEY is a cross-cutting choreography token: move it beside the other injection keys (demo/color-session/keys.ts already holds CSS_COLOR_KEY, EDIT_TARGET_KEY, COLOR_MODEL_KEY, SAFE_ACCENT_KEY) or into a new demo/shell/keys.ts. atmosphere-calibration is pure colour maths with no boot dependency — move it to demo/color-session/ beside view-accent.ts. Rename demo/color-picker/ -> demo/app/; the ambiguity dies with the directory.

defects.defect: componentFor widens a closed union to `string | null` in its signature, which forces an unreachable `return ColorPicker` masking fallback and destroys the compiler's exhaustiveness check — so adding a pane to viewSchema and forgetting this file silently renders the colour picker instead of failing.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:81 `function componentFor(name: string | null): Component | null` with the fallback at :94 `return ColorPicker;`. Its only callers pass closed-union values: :164 `currentConfig.value.left` (LeftPane) and :171 `currentConfig.value.right` (RightPane). The unions are enumerated at demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:52-63 (LeftPane, 11 members) and :66 (RightPane, 4 members + null). componentFor handles null, color-picker, browse, extract, generate, gradient, atmosphere, about, palettes, mix, blob, admin-* — exhausting both unions, so :94 is unreachable. The same masking shape already shows one layer up: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md reports `safari-desktop-light /#/does-not-exist` at text=859, byte-identical to `/#/` at text=859, via useViewManager.ts:47 `isViewId(name) ? name : "picker"`.
defects.mechanism: A signature that widens a deliberately closed union opts out of the exact compiler guarantee the union exists to provide, and then requires a fallback to satisfy the widened type — the fallback is the SYMPTOM of the widening, not a defensive choice.
defects.reproduction: NONE for a live failure — the fallback is unreachable today, proven by exhausting LeftPane ∪ RightPane against componentFor's branch set. The reproduction is a future one: add a member to LeftPane in viewSchema.ts and do not touch usePaneRouter.ts; the demo compiles clean and silently renders ColorPicker for the new view.
defects.proposedCure: `function componentFor(name: LeftPane | RightPane): Component | null`. TypeScript's exhaustiveness check then makes the fallback impossible to write and makes a schema addition a compile error here — which is the entire point of having the closed union in viewSchema.ts.

defects.defect: ActionBarLayer re-implements a glass-ui composable that glass-ui removed, inline in the SFC, carrying a parameter it accepts and immediately discards purely to match the retired signature.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:54-86. The shim: `function useLayerTransition(opts: { containerEl: Ref<HTMLElement | null>; activeLayer: Ref<string> }) { void opts.containerEl; // signature parity with the retired producer composable ... }`. Header comment at :54-62 concedes the design-system ownership: 'glass-ui removed the standalone useLayerTransition ... a public content-swap composable would retire this local shim.' Consumed at :86.
defects.mechanism: Back-compat shape preserved for a counterparty that no longer exists — `void opts.containerEl` is a dead parameter whose only purpose is to look like something that was deleted. Layer crossfade is also a design-system concern (glass-ui at ^7.0.0), not a demo concern.

result.strongestDefect: L-1 — PaneSlot owns the application's only <KeepAlive> and publishes no activation contract, converting onUnmounted from "runs on navigation" to "runs never" for eleven pane components. Proven live: at /#/atmosphere the cached ColorPicker reports isUnmounted:false, isDeactivated:true, so ColorPicker.vue:382 — the sole removeEventListener("keydown") site, living in onUnmounted — has not run and will not run; its handler (ColorPicker.vue:249-267) calls e.preventDefault() on Cmd+K globally, on every route, to toggle a select in an invisible pane. It is the strongest finding because it is (a) reproduced in the running application rather than inferred, (b) a CLASS not an instance — four independent listener sites (ColorPicker.vue:377, useSliderTouchGates.ts:124, ImageEyedropper.vue:239, usePointerDebug.ts:227-232) share one mechanism, and the demo answers with 1 onActivated and 0 onDeactivated tree-wide — and (c) caused by an ABSENCE rather than a mistake, which is exactly why five tranches of review never caught it: PaneSlot's 23-line header documents transition mode, the dev-mode out-in defect, the onMount prop and the appear grammar, and says nothing at all about the lifecycle it mints.
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND overall, but the axis-specific negative IS proven and must be recorded so the challenge does not manufacture a finding where none exists. PaneSlot.vue's own import hygiene is exemplary: measured static import closure is exactly ONE file (itself) — `demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue — STATIC closure: 1 files, dynamic entry points: 0, by area: {"demo/shell":1}` (scratchpad/closure.mjs) — against 135 for demo/shell/dock/index.ts and 115 for usePaneRouter.ts. Its single import (PaneSlot.vue:25) is verbatimModuleSyntax-correct with inline `type Component`, and the whole demo/shell census is clean on that edict. It uses the Vue 3.5 reactive props destructure (:27-63) and shallowRef for the component/props cells (:74, :76), which is the correct choice for non-reactive payloads. It ships no <style> block, so the root-level-styling edict is trivially satisfied, and the appear-family classes (:115-117) are named tokens rather than inline overrides. Separately, the demo's LIBRARY-import discipline is genuinely sound: all ~48 @mkbabb/value.js imports across demo/ go through published subpaths (/color, /css, /math, /easing, /quantize), zero @src/* imports survive in the demo tree, and TS compiler-API resolution confirms they land on this checkout's real dist (scratchpad/resolve.cjs: @mkbabb/value.js/css -> dist/subpaths/css.d.ts).
