result.strongestDefect: PS-1 — PaneSlot.vue:124 forwards Vue's raw function-ref channel as if it were a mount/unmount event. Vue invokes function refs on EVERY patch (runtime-core.cjs.js:5475-5476), on KeepAlive re-activation (:3611), and on deactivate-unmount (:6590), so App.vue's onDesktopLeftMount (App.vue:323-332) must re-derive pane identity from currentConfig — a clock that flips synchronously with the route while PaneSlot deliberately trails it by one rAF plus an async chunk. Measured live: colorPickerRef held a GradientPane instance for 2190 ms on /#/mix while the ColorPicker was the visibly mounted left pane; generatePaneRef held a ColorPicker for 127 ms; four wrong instances written into colorPickerRef in a 6 ms burst. Every downstream consumer (usePaletteWiring.ts:66-67, :117; App.vue:41-42; usePaneRouter.ts:156-157) guards null only, never type.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Sound sub-areas verified and recorded in the report's "Negative proofs" section: no defineModel stale-read (three shallowRef/ref mirrors, the prescribed cure applied correctly); verbatimModuleSyntax compliant at PaneSlot.vue:25; the rAF is a one-shot cancelled on both paths (:89, :108) and PaneSlot is never itself KeepAlive'd so onBeforeUnmount is the correct hook; no colour/ValueUnit/stableHue/parseCssColor surface; no pointer handling; no WebGL boot; Transition > KeepAlive > component nesting order is the one Vue requires; rapid A→B→C swap coalescing genuinely works as documented; <component :is="null"> emits NO Vue warning (resolveDynamicComponent → NULL_DYNAMIC_COMPONENT → Comment on the non-warning branch) — hypothesis killed by live probe on /#/atmosphere; zero global listeners registered anywhere in demo/shell/ (grep pasted); overture beat callbacks are idempotent (useOverture.ts:200-207); the atmosphere.png capture renders correctly and PaneSlot contributes 0 of the REPORT's 60 smallTapTargets and 18 namelessButtons.)

defects.defect: The `onMount` prop's documented contract ("Called with the component instance on mount, and with null on unmount", PaneSlot.vue:47-52) is false. The inline function ref at PaneSlot.vue:124 is invoked by Vue on every patch, on KeepAlive re-activation, and on deactivation, with whatever instance currently occupies the vnode. Because PaneSlot deliberately trails the incoming key by one rAF, App.vue's onDesktopLeftMount is handed the OUTGOING instance and files it under the INCOMING pane's name — writing the wrong component instance into colorPickerRef / generatePaneRef / gradientPaneRef / mixPaneRef.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:124 `:ref="onMount ? (el: any) => onMount!(el) : undefined"`; demo/color-picker/App.vue:323-332 (identity re-derived from `currentConfig.value.left`). Vue 3.5.35 source: node_modules/@vue/runtime-core/dist/runtime-core.cjs.js:5475-5476 (`setRef` inside `patch()` fires on every update, isUnmount=!n2=false), :1814-1815 (`if (isFunction(ref)) callWithErrorHandling(...)` unconditional), :1799-1813 (the unset-old-ref branch handles only string/isRef, never a function), :6590 (unmount setRef(null) before the KeepAlive deactivate branch), :3611 (sharedContext.activate patch path). LIVE MEASUREMENT (PS-probe4.mjs, logging setters on each pane ref, six ordinary switchView calls): `SWITCH MARKS: 344ms->generate 1625ms->picker 2907ms->gradient 4302ms->mix 5586ms->atmosphere 6868ms->picker` / `t=372ms generatePaneRef := ColorPicker` … `t=499ms generatePaneRef := GeneratePane` (127 ms wrong) / `t=1646ms colorPickerRef := GeneratePane` / `t=2935ms gradientPaneRef := ColorPicker` / `t=2936ms gradientPaneRef := GeneratePane` / `t=4327ms colorPickerRef := GradientPane` with the NEXT colorPickerRef write at `t=6517ms` = 2190 ms holding a GradientPane on /#/mix where left==="color-picker". Every stack reads `onDesktopLeftMount (App.vue:136) << _mergeProps.ref (demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:131) << callWithErrorHandling << setRef << patch`. Second run burst: `t=6524 colorPickerRef := AuroraPane / t=6525 := GeneratePane / t=6526 := GradientPane / t=6529 := null / t=6530 := ColorPicker`. Independent per-frame sampler (PS-probe2.mjs): `t=166ms pickerRef=ColorPicker` → `t=363ms pickerRef=GeneratePane`, still GeneratePane ≥900 ms later at the next probe's t=54ms.
defects.mechanism: Vue's raw function-ref channel (fires per patch / per activate / per deactivate) is published as a domain-level mount/unmount event, forcing the consumer to re-derive pane identity from a DIFFERENT clock (currentConfig, synchronous with the route) than the one PaneSlot renders on (liveKey, deliberately one rAF behind).
defects.reproduction: node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/PS-probe4.mjs against the live dev server at http://localhost:9000. It wraps colorPickerRef/generatePaneRef/gradientPaneRef/mixPaneRef `value` setters with logging accessors, then calls viewManager.switchView through picker→generate→picker→gradient→mix→atmosphere→picker. Output pasted above. Manual equivalent: on desktop, click Generate then Home in the dock; within the swap window colorPickerRef holds the GeneratePane instance. Directly-observed user-visible consequence (PS-probe5.mjs): colorPickerRef timeline after generate→palettes is `0ms=null | 75ms=ColorPicker` — for 75 ms usePaletteWiring.ts:65-73 takes its masking `else` branch and applies only colors[0] instead of the whole palette, silently.
defects.proposedCure: Kill the imperative callback rather than patch it. PaneSlot already knows the key it committed (liveKey). Preferred (option 2, architectural inversion): PaneSlot owns `const live = shallowRef<ComponentPublicInstance|null>(null)` set from the ref callback and `defineExpose({ instance: live, key: liveKey })`; App.vue derives `colorPickerRef = computed(() => leftSlot.value?.key === 'color-picker' ? leftSlot.value.instance : null)`. One source of truth, no reactive writes during the patch phase, and the three parallel God-refs collapse into derivations — this also retires PS-4 and PS-6. Minimum viable (option 1): change the signature to `onMount?: (instance: unknown, key: string) => void` invoked as `onMount(el, liveKey.value)` so the consumer switches on the key of the instance it was actually handed; cross-wiring becomes structurally impossible.

defects.defect: PaneSlot's `<KeepAlive>` (PaneSlot.vue:120) keeps deactivated panes' `window` keydown listeners bound app-wide, because `onUnmounted`/`onBeforeUnmount` do not fire on KeepAlive deactivation. A deactivated ColorPicker swallows Cmd+K, and — with preventDefault — Escape and Enter whenever an edit was left open, on every route where it is not rendered.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:376-384 registers `window.addEventListener("keydown", handleKeydown)` in `onMounted` and removes it in `onUnmounted`; the handler body at ColorPicker.vue:249-266 does `if (isEditing) { Escape → preventDefault+cancelEdit; Enter → preventDefault+commitEdit }` and `if (keys.cmd && keys.k) { preventDefault; toggle selectedColorSpaceOpen }`. demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:237-245 has the same shape with `onBeforeUnmount`, handler at :226-235 claiming Escape. Vue 3.5.35 runtime-core.cjs.js:6595-6598 — `if (shapeFlag & 256) { parentComponent.ctx.deactivate(vnode); return; }` returns before any unmount-hook path. ColorPicker is the left pane on picker/palettes/mix/blob (viewSchema.ts:105-187) and stays cached on browse, extract, generate, gradient, atmosphere and all five admin-* views. Census: `grep -rnE "addEventListener|useEventListener|onKeyStroke|window\.on|document\.on|onActivated|onDeactivated" demo/shell/` → ZERO matches (the shell itself leaks nothing); `grep -rn "window.addEventListener\|document.addEventListener" demo/ | wc -l` → 12, of which 9 sit inside KeepAlive'd pane subtrees and 3 (useDevicePixelSnap.ts:83-85) are App-setup-scoped and therefore safe.
defects.mechanism: PaneSlot adopts <KeepAlive> for scroll/state preservation but publishes no contract that cached panes must gate their global effects, and enforces none itself; `onUnmounted` is the wrong hook under KeepAlive and nothing in the shell says so.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/ (ColorPicker mounts, keydown bound), navigate to /#/generate (ColorPicker deactivates, listener survives), press Cmd+K — the deactivated picker's colour-space select toggles and the keystroke is preventDefault'd. Corroborates the sibling seat's finding. Extension: start an edit on the picker, navigate to /#/extract, open the eyedropper, press Escape — the deactivated ColorPicker's handler and the ImageEyedropper's handler both claim it.
defects.proposedCure: PaneSlot is the app's only <KeepAlive>, so it should own the invariant rather than leave it to lifecycle archaeology in each pane. Preferred: PaneSlot provides an injected `isPaneActive` ref derived from `liveKey` so cached panes gate global effects declaratively. Minimum: state the invariant in PaneSlot's header contract and move the two offending registrations to `onActivated`/`onDeactivated` (ColorPicker.vue:376-384, ImageEyedropper.vue:237-245).

defects.defect: The rAF mount-trail is gated only on `transitionName` being a non-empty string, not on the user's motion preference. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the global guard zeroes every transition-duration, so the deferral's own stated justification — landing the mount "under cover of the enter transition" — is false, and the user sees a measured 58–106 ms of the OLD pane after the dock and URL have already flipped, with no cross-fade.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:86-97 — `if (!transitionName) { commit(key); return; } raf = requestAnimationFrame(() => commit(key));` (line 90 is the only gate). Justification at PaneSlot.vue:65-73. demo/styles/animations.css:184-192 — `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *,*::before,*::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; transition-duration: 0.01ms !important; } }`. demo/color-picker/App.vue:87/106/132 pass `:transition-name="viewManager.ready.value ? 'vj-enter' : ''"` with no PRM term, while App.vue:302 already computes `prmInstant` from useDockArrival and never passes it down. MEASURED (PS-probe6.mjs, latency from switchView() to the incoming pane element appearing in .pane-wrapper--left): `B. motion:normal  generate->picker: 109.2ms  picker->generate: 85.2ms  gradient->picker: 83.7ms` vs `B'. prefers-reduced-motion:reduce  prmInstant=true  generate->picker: 106.3ms  picker->generate: 58.6ms` — statistically indistinguishable.
defects.mechanism: A motion gate keyed on a transition-name string rather than on the motion preference; the component asserts a covering animation exists without checking whether the user has switched animations off.
defects.reproduction: node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/PS-probe6.mjs — runs the same switchView latency measurement in two Playwright contexts, `{}` and `{ reducedMotion: "reduce" }`. Output pasted above.
defects.proposedCure: Make line 90's gate the honest predicate. Either take an `instant?: boolean` prop (App.vue already has `prmInstant` at :302 and can pass it in three places), or read it in the component: `if (!transitionName || matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches) { commit(key); return; }`. KISS, no new module, no new shared dir.

defects.defect: The pane-ref channel fires on every reactive tick, not per swap: 360 ref writes were measured for 180 colour-model updates with zero view changes. App.vue passes `:on-appeared` as an inline arrow PROP (v-bind, not v-on), so the compiler's cacheHandlers transform does not apply, a fresh function identity is produced on every App render, shouldUpdateComponent always returns true for PaneSlot, and PS-1's per-patch ref fires each time — each write being a reactive Ref assignment executed during the patch phase.
defects.evidence: demo/color-picker/App.vue:90 / :109 / :135 — `:on-appeared="(el: Element) => overture.noteLeftPlateSettled(el)"` (and the right-slot variant). MEASURED (PS-probe6.mjs section A, counting setter invocations across all four pane refs during 180 model writes at 1/frame, no route change): `A. ref-callback churn on 180 model writes (no view change): {"refWrites":360,"frames":180,"ms":13675}` — the correct number is 0. App.vue:38 reads `colorPickerRef?.actionBarContext` in its own template, so each write re-triggers App's render effect; it does not loop only because the value happens to settle.
defects.mechanism: An inline arrow bound as a v-bind prop defeats Vue's shouldUpdateComponent props-identity check, and the per-patch function ref (PS-1) turns each spurious re-render into four reactive writes during the patch phase. Same family as PS-1.
defects.reproduction: node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/PS-probe6.mjs, section A. Output pasted above. (Downstream corruption is prevented only by luck: useOverture.ts:200-207 makes noteLeftPlateSettled/noteDockLanded idempotent.)
defects.proposedCure: Hoist the three `onAppeared` arrows in App.vue to stable `const` handlers (three lines), and land PS-1's option-2 inversion so the ref channel writes at most once per genuine commit. Fixing PS-1 by inversion retires this finding with it.

defects.defect: The `component` prop is never watched. `commit()` is the only writer of `liveComponent` and it runs only on a `componentKey` change, so a `component` change with a stable key is silently ignored forever — while the prop contract declares the two as independent props with no stated co-variance requirement.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:86 `watch(() => componentKey, …)` — the sole trigger; :80-84 `commit()` is the sole writer of liveComponent; :74 `const liveComponent = shallowRef(component)` is the only other value it ever holds; :38-44 declares `component` and `componentKey` as independent props. Unreachable today only because demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:81-95 `componentFor()` is a pure function of the key.
defects.mechanism: Two props that must co-vary, guarded by a watcher on only one of them; the invariant lives in a different file (usePaneRouter) and is undocumented at the prop boundary.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a hypothesis. Evidence is structural (PaneSlot.vue:86 vs :38-44). It becomes a live silent never-updates bug on the first route-table edit that maps two different components to one key.
defects.proposedCure: Either `watch(() => [componentKey, component], …)`, or — better and smaller — take the single `PaneSlot` object prop that usePaneRouter.ts:61-65 already exports (`{ component, key, props }`) instead of three parallel props, so the co-variance is carried by the type.

Mutation 2 (the decisive one) — delete PaneSlot.vue:124 so onMount is never called: all 25 unit tests pass and walk.spec.ts, mobile/walk.spec.ts, admin/admin-walk.spec.ts and o20-generate-plate.spec.ts all pass, while the dock's picker action bar and all three workbench action bars die completely, undetected. Mutation 3 — invert App.vue:325-327 (`left === "generate" ? el : null` for colorPickerRef): green everywhere.
defects.proposedCure: Land PS-1's inversion first so the channel becomes declarative and testable, then add a component test that mounts PaneSlot with two stub panes, swaps the key, and asserts the exposed `{ instance, key }` pair is always self-consistent across the swap (never instance-of-A-under-key-B). Add one e2e assertion that exercises the dock action bar itself (click Tools → Regenerate on /#/generate and assert the palette changed), which is the assertion whose absence made PS-1 invisible.
